# ECalc Phase 4 (Pinouts) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Finish ECalc v1 with its last area: 47 connector, board and IC pinouts with a drawing generated from the data (plug and socket view, pins coloured by type, wire colours, variants), the agent tool action `pinout`, the completed manual chapter 32 and the acceptance across all desktop skins.

**Architecture:** Unchanged principle: a declarative catalog embedded in `internal/ecalc`, validated at load time and served localized. Part A adds the item kind `pinout`, `catalog/pinstyles.yaml` (the fixed pin type and wire colours) and the vector format. Part UP adds the DOM-free renderer `ecalc-pinout-draw.js`, the page `ecalc-pinout-page.js` and their tests. Part B adds the query API and the tool operation. Part C prepares the existing tests and adds the content, with the record of its sources. Part Z corrects what the visual acceptance found, merges the shared DOX files, completes the manual and runs the integrated verification.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.27 (`gopkg.in/yaml.v3`), vanilla JavaScript classic scripts in the AuraGo desktop, go-rod browser tests (`AURAGO_RUN_BROWSER_SMOKE=1`), Node for `scripts/test-ecalc-pinouts.mjs`.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-01-ecalc-design.md` (phase 4 = pinouts). Phases 1 to 3 are landed on `main`. This is the last phase of ECalc v1.

## Overview

### Parts, order and dependencies

| Part | Tasks | Needs | Delivers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A — engine | A1, A2 | – | item kind `pinout`, shapes and their validation, `pinstyles.yaml`, catalog JSON, vector format |
| UP — page | UP1–UP3 | A | renderer with 16 connector outlines and six shape types, page, shell routing, 24 strings, node geometry test, 5 browser tests |
| B — tool | B1–B4 | A | `QueryPinout`, `DescribePinout`, tool operation `pinout`, schema, policy, tool manual, user documentation |
| C — content | C0–C6 | A, UP, B | tests and rail ready for the fourth kind; 47 pinouts with vectors and source records |
| Z — integration | Z1–Z5 | all | two renderer corrections, the audit entry, shared DOX entries, manual chapter 32, integrated verification, skin survey, graph check |

Execution order: **A1, A2, UP1 → UP3, B1 → B4, C0, C1 → C6, Z1 → Z5.** After A, UP and B can run in parallel in their own worktrees if the commits are combined afterwards: their file sets are disjoint. Every task that changes the catalog regenerates the generated snapshot `internal/ecalc/testdata/catalog.en.json`; never hand-merge that file, regenerate it with `go test ./internal/ecalc -run TestCatalogSnapshot -update`.

### How this plan was made

Every part was implemented for real in its own scratch worktree at base `f83d3c598`, verified there, and its plan text was generated from the verified files. The pinouts were researched against named sources by five research agents that wrote the catalog items themselves, so nothing was retyped; the strict loader accepted them, and the controller then read all 47 against what it knows of these parts and looked at the drawings. All parts were applied together in an integration worktree and verified once more (Task Z5). That run and the visual survey found problems the separate drafts could not see, all fixed below: existing tests that did not know the fourth kind, the rail overflowing by its new entry, labels breaking inside a word, a segmented control whose pill radius cut off its first and last option on four skins, numbers jumping between inside and outside the contacts, and the USB-A tongue in the plug view.

`main` has moved on since `f83d3c598`. Execute on a fresh branch from the current `main`. Other sessions commit to this repository concurrently: if a task's "Replace … with …" block no longer matches because of a foreign commit (most likely in `ui/lang/desktop/*.json`, `ui/js/desktop/core/module-loader.js`, `ui/js/desktop/apps/AGENTS.md`, the agent registries and the bundles), apply the same change to the current text by hand and say so in the commit body. Never copy such a file wholesale from a drafting worktree.

### Environment (all parts)

- Windows box. Go: `GOTMPDIR` = a short backslash path (`$env:GOTMPDIR = 'C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p4'`, create it once).
- Browser tests: PowerShell with the sandbox disabled, `AURAGO_RUN_BROWSER_SMOKE=1`.
- The working copies of `ui/js/**`, `ui/css/**` and `scripts/*.mjs` are CRLF on this checkout (git stores LF): use an edit tool that matches across line endings or normalise before editing.
- The Write/Edit tools decode backslash-u escapes: write µ, Ω, °, ² as characters; in Go source write a backslash as `\x5c`.
- GitNexus: before modifying an existing function run the impact analysis (each part records its result; symbols added after the index was built answer `UNKNOWN`, which the parts confirmed by search). Before each commit run `detect_changes`. Generic JS names (`parse`, `create`, `evaluate`, `fail`, `dim`) collide with other apps by name.
- Commit messages end with the Co-Authored-By trailer of the executing model. New non-root `AGENTS.md` need `git add -f`; `docs/` is git-ignored.

### Controller notes (decisions taken while drafting; they take precedence over the contract in the appendix)

1. **Variants live inside one item.** `rj45` (T568A, T568B), `audio_trrs` (CTIA, OMTP), `displayport` (source, sink: one list would be wrong by four lanes for anyone wiring a monitor input) and `to92` (seven parts) carry `variants`; the shape is shared and every variant has the same pin numbers. The tool takes `variant`.
2. **Pin type colours are data, not theme tokens.** Several of the 15 skins are near-monochrome, and a pin type must read the same on every desktop. `catalog/pinstyles.yaml` holds the six fills with their ink (WCAG contrast of at least 4.5, checked at load) and the 15 wire colours; everything else in the drawing follows the skin. This is the rule of the code drawings of phase 3.
3. **What counts as a source.** A maker's datasheet or official board document for its own part and a free official specification are authoritative: one is enough. Paywalled standards reproduced elsewhere need two independent sources. A drawing direction counts as a fact: every record says which view it is written for and on what that rests. Only details that are not pin numbers or names may stay out when unverified. `documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/SUMMARY.md` lists the weakest points and the judgement calls on types.
4. **`xlr` draws the latch as its key** (0°), because people orient the connector by it; the polarising rib at 45° is in the notes. The research first gave the rib, and the record says so.
5. **Outlines are fixed in the `drawn` view,** and the data was written against them: `rj45` notch at the bottom, `displayport` cut corner lower left, `hdmi_a`, `usb_mini_b`, `usb_micro_b`, `dsub`, `obd2` wide side up, `usb_b` chamfers on top, `usb_a` tongue in the upper half in the receptacle, `minifit` latch on top, `molex` cut corners at the bottom, `sata_data` and `sata_power` L step at the bottom by S7 and P1. Changing a shell means checking the rows of every item that uses it (`internal/ecalc/AGENTS.md` keeps this).
6. **Tool schema:** the budget of `ecalc` stays 800 tokens (799 measured). Two search phrases of the tool gave way for the pinout phrases (12-phrase limit).
7. **Review before release:** the German texts the research wrote, the 14 other locales of the item names, the judgement calls on types in `SUMMARY.md`.
8. **Known failures that are not this plan's:** `TestUpdateConfigFallbackOnlyTrustedTransactionBackups` (`internal/audit`) and, on this Windows box, the SMTP and MCP network tests of `internal/tools` (`TestEmail*`, `TestDeliverSMTP*`, `TestSendEmail*`, `TestMCPStreamableHTTPTransportInitializeListAndCall`) and `TestAIGatewayHelperPrivacyReload`, `TestCoAgentCloudflareRESTUsesSelectedIdentity` (`internal/agent`) fail without these changes too. Do not "fix" them in this plan.

## Part A — Engine: the item kind `pinout` (tasks A1, A2)


**Goal:** The ECalc catalog gains the item kind `pinout` (contract sections 1 to 6): the loader for `pinouts/*.yaml` with every validation rule, `catalog/pinstyles.yaml` (six pin types with hex and ink, fifteen wire colours, 16 locales), the catalog JSON (`pin_types`, `wires`, the pinout items with every shape field always present), the exported Go API for the page (UP) and the tool (B), and the vector format with its Go test. No real pinout items: Z adds them.

**Architecture:** `pinstyles.go` loads and validates `pinstyles.yaml` and computes the WCAG contrast; `pinouts.go` holds the typed item, the strict raw YAML types, the shape builder (one switch per shape type, all problems reported through `fail`), the coverage rules and the JSON. `catalog.go` gets the fields and two calls in `Load`; `localize.go` gets the top-level `pin_types` and `wires` and renders the pinouts after the codes. Tests load fixtures through `fstest.MapFS` (`treeFS` plus the real `pinstyles.yaml`).

**Tech stack:** Go 1.27, `gopkg.in/yaml.v3`, `testing/fstest`. `GOTMPDIR` = a short backslash path per agent (`C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p4-a`).

**Base:** the ECalc phase 3 state (`P4\BASE`). Files this plan creates: `internal/ecalc/pinstyles.go`, `pinstyles_test.go`, `pinouts.go`, `pinouts_test.go`, `pinouts_vectors_test.go`, `catalog/pinstyles.yaml`. Files it edits: `catalog.go`, `localize.go`, `items.go`, `testdata/catalog.en.json` (regenerated).

### Contract deviations

1. **Two extra source files and two extra test files** (`pinstyles.go`, `pinstyles_test.go`, `pinouts_vectors_test.go` next to `pinouts.go` and `pinouts_test.go`): the pin styles and the vector check are separate concerns and `pinouts.go` would have been 900 lines. They are new files in the package, nothing else owns those names.
2. **`pinstyles.yaml` is optional without pinouts.** The contract says "Load checks: all six types present ..."; a catalog without `pinstyles.yaml` and without `pinouts/` still loads (so the many existing fixtures built on `treeFS` keep working untouched) and its JSON carries `pin_types: []` and `wires: []`. As soon as a `pinouts/*.yaml` file exists, a missing `pinstyles.yaml` is a load error. The embedded catalog always has the file.
3. **The style lists are `Catalog.PinTypeStyles []*PinType` and `Catalog.Wires []*Wire`**, with `Catalog.PinType(id)` and `Catalog.Wire(id)`. (`PinTypes` is the exported `[]string` of the contract, so the struct slice needs another name.) Wire names of the real file are English colour names (`white-green`), which is what the tool (B) prints.
4. **`pinstyles.yaml` is strict:** the types are exactly `power ground signal data io nc` in this order, the wires exactly the fifteen ids of section 3 in this order; the four `white_*` wires must have a `stripe`; `ink` is only for types and `stripe` only for wires. The contrast check (>= 4.5) is done by the loader (so a bad file can never reach the page) and again by a test on the embedded file.
5. **`Pinout.Shape` fields:** `PinoutShape{Type, Outline, Contact, Drawn, Key string; KeyAngle *float64; Rows []PinoutRow; DipPins int; Package string; ToPins []string; Positions []PinoutPosition; Segments []string; Left, Right, Top, Bottom []string; Connector string; Inner []PinoutInner}`. In `Left/Right/Top/Bottom` and in `PinoutRow.Pins` the empty string is the gap (`null` in YAML and JSON). `Drawn` is filled for every type exactly as in the JSON (`top` for dip and board, `front` for to, `side` for jack); `Key` is `"none"` for a `rows` shape without a key.
6. **A `rows` key other than `none` needs `outline: rect`** (contract: "only with outline rect"); a `to` shape has 2 to 5 pins; a `board` shape needs at least one side with at least one pin.
7. **Order of `PinTypes`** is the file order of `pinstyles.yaml` (`power ground signal data io nc`), not the order of the prose in section 1; `PinoutOutlines` is sorted.
8. The vector check works on any `fs.FS` (`checkPinoutVectors(cat, vecs)`), so that a fixture can prove it fails. `testdata/vectors/pinouts/` is absent until Z adds files; an absent directory counts as empty.

### Exact Go API (for UP and B)

```go
const pinoutsCategory = "pinouts" // unexported
var PinoutGroups   []string // data audio pc_power boards debug ics
var PinoutOutlines []string // sorted, 16 entries
var PinTypes       []string // power ground signal data io nc

type Pin struct { Number, Name, Type, Wire string; Function, Notes Text }
type PinoutVariant struct { ID string; Name Text; Pins []Pin }
type PinoutRow struct { Pins []string; Offset float64 }          // "" = empty position
type PinoutPosition struct { Pin string; Angle, Radius float64 }
type PinoutInner struct { Label string; Rows []PinoutRow }
type PinoutShape struct { /* see deviation 5 */ }
func (s PinoutShape) Numbers() []string                           // every pin number the shape names, drawing order
type Pinout struct {
    ID, Category, Group string
    Name, Doc, Notes    Text
    Tags                []string
    Source              string
    Views               map[string]Text // "plug", "socket"; nil when the shape has one view
    Shape               PinoutShape
    Pins                []Pin
    Variants            []PinoutVariant
}
func (p *Pinout) PinsOf(variant string) (pins []Pin, id string, ok bool)

type PinType struct { ID, Hex, Ink string; Name Text }
type Wire struct { ID, Hex, Stripe string; Name Text }

// Catalog gains:
Pinouts       []*Pinout
PinTypeStyles []*PinType
Wires         []*Wire
func (c *Catalog) Pinout(id string) *Pinout
func (c *Catalog) PinType(id string) *PinType
func (c *Catalog) Wire(id string) *Wire
// Catalog.Item(id) answers "pinout".
```

Catalog JSON additions: top level `pin_types: [{id, hex, ink, name}]`, `wires: [{id, hex, stripe, name}]` (between `categories` and `items`); a pinout item has the 14 keys `kind id category group name name_en doc notes tags source views shape pins variants`; `shape` has the 16 keys `type outline contact drawn key rows pins package positions segments left right top bottom connector inner`, always all present.

### Task A1: pin styles and the pinout loader

**Files:** create `internal/ecalc/catalog/pinstyles.yaml`, `internal/ecalc/pinstyles.go`, `internal/ecalc/pinouts.go`, `internal/ecalc/pinstyles_test.go`, `internal/ecalc/pinouts_test.go`; edit `internal/ecalc/catalog.go`, `localize.go`, `items.go`; regenerate `internal/ecalc/testdata/catalog.en.json`.

**GitNexus impact (before editing):** `Load` and `render` of `internal/ecalc` report risk UNKNOWN (ambiguous names, no resolved callers). Confirmed by grep: `ecalc.Default()` is called by `internal/server/ecalc_handlers.go` (the catalog endpoint) and by `internal/tools` (ecalc.go and its tests); nothing constructs `Catalog` outside `Load`. The change is additive (new fields, new top-level JSON keys, one more loop in `render`); existing catalogs without `pinstyles.yaml` still load. After the change, `go test ./internal/tools ./internal/server -run 'Ecalc|ECalc'` must stay green (it does).

`internal/ecalc/pinstyles_test.go`:
```go
package ecalc

import (
	"math"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"testing/fstest"
)

func TestContrastRatio(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range []struct {
		a, b string
		want float64
	}{
		{"#000000", "#ffffff", 21},
		{"#ffffff", "#ffffff", 1},
		{"#777777", "#ffffff", 4.48}, // the well-known grey that just fails 4.5
		{"#767676", "#ffffff", 4.54}, // and the one that just passes
	} {
		if got := contrastRatio(c.a, c.b); math.Abs(got-c.want) > 0.01 {
			t.Errorf("contrastRatio(%s, %s) = %.3f, want %.2f", c.a, c.b, got, c.want)
		}
		if got := contrastRatio(c.b, c.a); math.Abs(got-contrastRatio(c.a, c.b)) > 1e-12 {
			t.Errorf("contrastRatio is not symmetric for %s, %s", c.a, c.b)
		}
	}
}

// The embedded pinstyles.yaml: six pin types in order, fifteen wires, every ink readable on its fill, 16 locales.
func TestPinStylesOfTheCatalog(t *testing.T) {
	cat, err := Default()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var ids []string
	for _, pt := range cat.PinTypeStyles {
		ids = append(ids, pt.ID)
		if c := contrastRatio(pt.Ink, pt.Hex); c < 4.5 {
			t.Errorf("pin type %s: ink %s on %s has a contrast of %.2f, want at least 4.5", pt.ID, pt.Ink, pt.Hex, c)
		}
		for _, lang := range Locales {
			if pt.Name[lang] == "" {
				t.Errorf("pin type %s has no %s name", pt.ID, lang)
			}
		}
		if cat.PinType(pt.ID) != pt {
			t.Errorf("PinType(%s) does not return the style", pt.ID)
		}
	}
	if strings.Join(ids, " ") != "power ground signal data io nc" || strings.Join(ids, " ") != strings.Join(PinTypes, " ") {
		t.Errorf("pin types = %v, PinTypes = %v", ids, PinTypes)
	}
	var wires []string
	for _, w := range cat.Wires {
		wires = append(wires, w.ID)
		for _, lang := range Locales {
			if w.Name[lang] == "" {
				t.Errorf("wire %s has no %s name", w.ID, lang)
			}
		}
		if (w.Stripe != "") != strings.HasPrefix(w.ID, "white_") || cat.Wire(w.ID) != w {
			t.Errorf("wire %s: stripe %q", w.ID, w.Stripe)
		}
	}
	if len(wires) != 15 || strings.Join(wires, " ") != strings.Join(wireIDs, " ") {
		t.Errorf("wires = %v", wires)
	}
}

func TestLoadRejectsBrokenPinStyles(t *testing.T) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile("catalog/pinstyles.yaml")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	base := string(data)
	cases := []struct{ name, old, new, want string }{
		{"not a colour", `hex: "#c62828"`, `hex: "red"`, `type power: hex must be a colour like #1565c0`},
		{"upper case colour", `hex: "#c62828"`, `hex: "#C62828"`, "hex must be a colour"},
		{"ink missing", `ink: "#000000"`, `ink: ""`, `type signal: ink must be a colour`},
		{"ink too weak", `hex: "#f9a825"`, `hex: "#7b5200"`, "type signal: ink #000000 on #7b5200 has a contrast of"},
		{"missing locale", `, zh: "电源"`, "", `type power: name: missing "zh" text`},
		{"missing wire locale", `, zh: "黑色"`, "", `wire black: name: missing "zh" text`},
		{"type renamed", "  nc:", "  nx:", "types must be power, ground, signal, data, io, nc in this order"},
		{"wire renamed", "  pink:", "  rosa:", "wires must be black, brown,"},
		{"stripe lost", `stripe: "#ef6c00"`, `stripe: ""`, "wire white_orange: a striped wire needs a stripe colour"},
		{"stripe not a colour", `stripe: "#ef6c00"`, `stripe: "orange"`, "wire white_orange: stripe must be a colour"},
		{"unknown field", `hex: "#212121"`, `hex: "#212121"` + "\n    colour: red", "colour"},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		fsys := treeFS(t, nil)
		fsys["pinstyles.yaml"] = &fstest.MapFile{Data: []byte(mutate(t, base, c.old, c.new))}
		_, err := Load(fsys)
		if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), c.want) {
			t.Errorf("%s: error = %v, want it to contain %q", c.name, err, c.want)
		}
	}
}
```

`internal/ecalc/pinouts_test.go`:
```go
package ecalc

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"os"
	"reflect"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"testing/fstest"
)

// pinTreeFS is treeFS plus the real pinstyles.yaml (a catalog with pinouts needs it) and the given files.
func pinTreeFS(t *testing.T, files map[string]string) fstest.MapFS {
	t.Helper()
	fsys := treeFS(t, files)
	data, err := os.ReadFile("catalog/pinstyles.yaml")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, ok := fsys["pinstyles.yaml"]; !ok {
		fsys["pinstyles.yaml"] = &fstest.MapFile{Data: data}
	}
	return fsys
}

// fixtureItem writes one pinout item with a valid header; views, shape and pins are the indented YAML blocks of the rest.
func fixtureItem(id, views, shape, pins string) string {
	return strings.ReplaceAll(`- id: `+id+`
  kind: pinout
  category: pinouts
  group: data
  name: NAME16
  doc: {en: "Doc.", de: "Doku."}
  notes: {en: "Note.", de: "Hinweis."}
  tags: [test]
  source: "Datasheet"
`+views+`  shape:
`+shape+pins, "NAME16", flow16("T"))
}

const fixtureViews = `  views:
    plug: {en: "Male", de: "Stecker"}
    socket: {en: "Female", de: "Buchse"}
`

// pinLine writes one pin of a fixture.
func pinLine(number, name, typ, extra string) string {
	if extra != "" {
		extra = ", " + extra
	}
	return `    - {number: "` + number + `", name: ` + name + `, function: {en: "Func ` + name + `", de: "Funktion ` + name + `"}, type: ` + typ + extra + `}
`
}

// basePinout is a valid "rows" item: a rect connector with a key, three pins, a wire colour and a pin note.
var basePinout = fixtureItem("t_conn", fixtureViews, `    type: rows
    outline: rect
    contact: round
    drawn: plug
    key: top
    rows:
      - {pins: ["1", "2"]}
      - {pins: ["3"], offset: 0.5}
`, `  pins:
`+pinLine("1", "VCC", "power", "wire: red")+
	pinLine("2", "GND", "ground", `notes: {en: "Shield too.", de: "Auch Schirm."}`)+
	pinLine("3", "TX", "data", ""))

func loadPinouts(t *testing.T, src string) *Catalog {
	t.Helper()
	cat, err := Load(pinTreeFS(t, map[string]string{"pinouts/p.yaml": src}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Load: %v", err)
	}
	return cat
}

func TestLoadPinoutItem(t *testing.T) {
	cat := loadPinouts(t, basePinout)
	p := cat.Pinout("t_conn")
	if p == nil || len(cat.Pinouts) != 1 || p.Category != "pinouts" || p.Group != "data" || p.Source != "Datasheet" || p.Name["en"] != "T" {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected pinout %+v", p)
	}
	if kind, ok := cat.Item("t_conn"); !ok || kind != "pinout" || cat.Calculator("t_conn") != nil || cat.Table("t_conn") != nil || cat.Code("t_conn") != nil {
		t.Errorf("Item(t_conn) = %q, %v", kind, ok)
	}
	if p.Views["plug"]["de"] != "Stecker" || p.Views["socket"]["en"] != "Female" {
		t.Errorf("Views = %v", p.Views)
	}
	s := p.Shape
	if s.Type != "rows" || s.Outline != "rect" || s.Contact != "round" || s.Drawn != "plug" || s.Key != "top" ||
		!reflect.DeepEqual(s.Rows, []PinoutRow{{Pins: []string{"1", "2"}}, {Pins: []string{"3"}, Offset: 0.5}}) {
		t.Errorf("Shape = %+v", s)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(s.Numbers(), []string{"1", "2", "3"}) {
		t.Errorf("Numbers() = %v", s.Numbers())
	}
	if len(p.Pins) != 3 || p.Pins[0].Wire != "red" || p.Pins[1].Notes["de"] != "Auch Schirm." || p.Pins[2].Type != "data" || p.Variants != nil {
		t.Errorf("Pins = %+v", p.Pins)
	}
	pins, id, ok := p.PinsOf("")
	if !ok || id != "" || len(pins) != 3 {
		t.Errorf("PinsOf(\"\") = %d pins, %q, %v", len(pins), id, ok)
	}
	if _, _, ok := p.PinsOf("x"); ok {
		t.Error("PinsOf(x) must fail for an item without variants")
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(PinoutGroups, []string{"data", "audio", "pc_power", "boards", "debug", "ics"}) {
		t.Errorf("PinoutGroups = %v", PinoutGroups)
	}
	if !sort.StringsAreSorted(PinoutOutlines) || len(PinoutOutlines) != 16 || !reflect.DeepEqual(PinTypes, []string{"power", "ground", "signal", "data", "io", "nc"}) {
		t.Errorf("PinoutOutlines = %v, PinTypes = %v", PinoutOutlines, PinTypes)
	}
}

func TestPinoutVariants(t *testing.T) {

    segments: ["T", "R", "S"]

      name: {en: "First", de: "Erste"}

	if len(p.Variants) != 2 || p.Pins != nil || p.Variants[1].Name["de"] != "Zweite" {

	pins, id, ok = p.PinsOf("second")
	if !ok || id != "second" || pins[2].Name != "R" {
		t.Errorf("PinsOf(second) = %v, %q, %v", pins, id, ok)
	}
	if pins, id, ok = p.PinsOf("nope"); ok || pins != nil || id != "" {
		t.Errorf("PinsOf(nope) = %v, %q, %v", pins, id, ok)
	}
}

// indent prefixes every line of s.
func indent(s, prefix string) string {
	lines := strings.SplitAfter(s, "\n")
	for i, l := range lines {
		if l != "" {
			lines[i] = prefix + l
		}
	}
	return strings.Join(lines, "")
}

// variantsOf builds an item with two variants whose pin lists are given.
func variantsOf(a, b string) string {
	return fixtureItem("t_conn", fixtureViews, `    type: rows
    outline: rect
    contact: round
    drawn: plug
    rows:
      - {pins: ["1", "2", "3"]}
`, `  variants:
    - id: aa
      name: {en: "A", de: "A"}
      pins:
`+indent(a, "    ")+`    - id: bb
      name: {en: "B", de: "B"}
      pins:
`+indent(b, "    "))
}

func TestLoadRejectsBrokenPinouts(t *testing.T) {
	three := pinLine("1", "A", "power", "") + pinLine("2", "B", "ground", "") + pinLine("3", "C", "data", "")
	otherThree := pinLine("1", "A", "power", "") + pinLine("2", "B", "ground", "") + pinLine("9", "C", "data", "")
	cases := []struct{ name, src, want string }{
		// item fields
		{"wrong kind", mutate(t, basePinout, "kind: pinout", "kind: table"), "kind must be pinout in pinouts/"},
		{"wrong category", mutate(t, basePinout, "category: pinouts", "category: tables"), "category must be pinouts"},
		{"unknown group", mutate(t, basePinout, "group: data", "group: wires"), "group must be one of data, audio, pc_power, boards, debug, ics"},
		{"bad id", mutate(t, basePinout, "id: t_conn", "id: T-conn"), "id must match"},
		{"missing name locale", mutate(t, basePinout, `, zh: "T"}`, `}`), `missing "zh" text`},
		{"doc without german", mutate(t, basePinout, `doc: {en: "Doc.", de: "Doku."}`, `doc: {en: "Doc."}`), `doc: missing "de" text`},
		{"notes without german", mutate(t, basePinout, `notes: {en: "Note.", de: "Hinweis."}`, `notes: {en: "Note."}`), `notes: missing "de" text`},
		{"no source", mutate(t, basePinout, `source: "Datasheet"`, `source: ""`), "source is required"},
		{"no tags", mutate(t, basePinout, `tags: [test]`, `tags: []`), "at least one tag is required"},
		{"unknown field", mutate(t, basePinout, `tags: [test]`, "tags: [test]\n  colour: red"), "colour"},
		// views
		{"views missing", mutate(t, basePinout, fixtureViews, ""), "views are required when the shape is drawn as plug or socket"},
		{"views without a socket", mutate(t, basePinout, `    socket: {en: "Female", de: "Buchse"}`+"\n", ""), `views: missing "socket" caption`},
		{"views without german", mutate(t, basePinout, `plug: {en: "Male", de: "Stecker"}`, `plug: {en: "Male"}`), `views.plug: missing "de" text`},
		{"unknown view", mutate(t, basePinout, `    socket:`, `    side: {en: "S", de: "S"}`+"\n    socket:"), `unknown view "side"`},
		{"views on a dip", fixtureItem("t_conn", fixtureViews, "    type: dip\n    pins: 4\n", "  pins:\n"+pinLine("1", "A", "power", "")+pinLine("2", "B", "power", "")+pinLine("3", "C", "power", "")+pinLine("4", "D", "power", "")), "views are only for shapes that are drawn as plug or socket"},
		// pins
		{"pins and variants", basePinout + "  variants:\n    - {id: aa, name: {en: A, de: A}, pins: []}\n    - {id: bb, name: {en: B, de: B}, pins: []}\n", "use either pins or variants, not both"},
		{"neither pins nor variants", mutate(t, basePinout, "  pins:\n"+pinLine("1", "VCC", "power", "wire: red")+pinLine("2", "GND", "ground", `notes: {en: "Shield too.", de: "Auch Schirm."}`)+pinLine("3", "TX", "data", ""), ""), "pins or variants are required"},
		{"duplicate number", mutate(t, basePinout, `number: "2"`, `number: "1"`), `pin "1": number is used twice`},
		{"empty number", mutate(t, basePinout, `number: "2"`, `number: ""`), "number must be 1 to 8 characters"},
		{"long number", mutate(t, basePinout, `number: "2"`, `number: "123456789"`), "number must be 1 to 8 characters"},
		{"long name", mutate(t, basePinout, `name: GND`, `name: ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXY`), "name must be 1 to 24 characters"},
		{"empty name", mutate(t, basePinout, `name: GND`, `name: ""`), "name must be 1 to 24 characters"},
		{"function without german", mutate(t, basePinout, `de: "Funktion TX"`, `de: ""`), `function: missing "de" text`},
		{"pin notes without german", mutate(t, basePinout, `de: "Auch Schirm."`, `de: ""`), `notes: missing "de" text`},
		{"unknown type", mutate(t, basePinout, `type: data`, `type: bus`), `type must be one of power, ground, signal, data, io, nc, got "bus"`},
		{"unknown wire", mutate(t, basePinout, `wire: red`, `wire: teal`), `wire "teal" is not in pinstyles.yaml`},
		{"unknown pin field", mutate(t, basePinout, `type: data`, `type: data, colour: red`), "colour"},
		// shape coverage
		{"pin not drawn", mutate(t, basePinout, `{pins: ["3"], offset: 0.5}`, `{pins: [null], offset: 0.5}`), "has no pins"},
		{"pin missing in the shape", mutate(t, basePinout, `{pins: ["1", "2"]}`, `{pins: ["1"]}`), `pin "2" is not drawn`},
		{"shape position without a pin", mutate(t, basePinout, `{pins: ["3"], offset: 0.5}`, `{pins: ["3", "4"], offset: 0.5}`), `position "4" names no pin`},
		{"pin drawn twice", mutate(t, basePinout, `{pins: ["3"], offset: 0.5}`, `{pins: ["3", "1"], offset: 0.5}`), `pin "1" is drawn more than once`},
		// variants
		{"one variant", strings.Replace(variantsOf(three, three), "    - id: bb\n      name: {en: \"B\", de: \"B\"}\n      pins:\n"+indent(three, "    "), "", 1), "needs at least 2 variants"},
		{"variant id twice", strings.Replace(variantsOf(three, three), "id: bb", "id: aa", 1), `variant id "aa" is used twice`},
		{"bad variant id", strings.Replace(variantsOf(three, three), "id: bb", "id: B-b", 1), `variant id "B-b" must match`},
		{"variant name without german", strings.Replace(variantsOf(three, three), `name: {en: "B", de: "B"}`, `name: {en: "B"}`, 1), `variant bb: name: missing "de" text`},
		{"variants with other numbers", variantsOf(three, otherThree), "variant bb has other pin numbers than variant aa (missing 3; extra 9)"},
		{"variant pin broken", variantsOf(three, strings.Replace(three, "type: data", "type: bus", 1)), "variant bb: pins: pin \"3\": type must be one of"},
		// shapes
		{"unknown shape type", mutate(t, basePinout, "type: rows", "type: ring"), "shape: type must be one of rows, dip, to, circular, jack, board"},
		{"field of another type", mutate(t, basePinout, "    key: top", "    key: top\n    segments: [a, b]"), "shape: field segments is not used by type rows"},
		{"rows without outline", mutate(t, basePinout, "    outline: rect\n", ""), "shape: type rows needs outline"},
		{"unknown outline", mutate(t, basePinout, "outline: rect", "outline: oval"), `shape: outline must be one of displayport, dsub,`},
		{"unknown contact", mutate(t, basePinout, "contact: round", "contact: hex"), "shape: contact must be one of round, square, blade"},
		{"unknown drawn", mutate(t, basePinout, "drawn: plug", "drawn: top"), "shape: drawn must be one of plug, socket"},
		{"unknown key", mutate(t, basePinout, "key: top", "key: middle"), "shape: key must be one of none, top, bottom, left, right"},
		{"key on a connector without rect", mutate(t, basePinout, "outline: rect", "outline: dsub"), "shape: key top needs the outline rect"},
		{"offset too large", mutate(t, basePinout, "offset: 0.5", "offset: 2.5"), "offset must be from 0 to 2 pitches"},
		{"negative offset", mutate(t, basePinout, "offset: 0.5", "offset: -1"), "offset must be from 0 to 2 pitches"},
		{"empty rows", mutate(t, basePinout, "    rows:\n      - {pins: [\"1\", \"2\"]}\n      - {pins: [\"3\"], offset: 0.5}\n", "    rows: []\n"), "shape: rows must not be empty"},
		{"empty pin number in a row", mutate(t, basePinout, `{pins: ["1", "2"]}`, `{pins: ["1", ""]}`), "has an empty pin number"},
		{"dip odd", dipFixture(5), "an even number of pins from 4 to 64"},
		{"dip too small", dipFixture(2), "an even number of pins from 4 to 64"},
		{"dip too large", dipFixture(66), "an even number of pins from 4 to 64"},
		{"dip not numbered 1..N", strings.Replace(dipFixture(4), `number: "4"`, `number: "A4"`, 1), `shape: pin "A4" is not drawn`},
		{"dip with a package", strings.Replace(dipFixture(4), "    pins: 4\n", "    pins: 4\n    package: to92\n", 1), "field package is not used by type dip"},
		{"to bad package", toFixture("to247", `["B", "C", "E"]`), "shape: package must be one of to92, to220"},
		{"to one pin", toFixture("to92", `["B"]`), "a to shape has 2 to 5 pins"},
		{"to pins as a number", toFixture("to92", `3`), "pins of a to shape must be the list of pin numbers"},
		{"jack one segment", jackFixture(`["T"]`), "a jack has 2 to 5 segments"},
		{"jack six segments", jackFixture(`["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]`), "a jack has 2 to 5 segments"},
		{"circular without drawn", strings.Replace(circularFixture(), "    drawn: socket\n", "", 1), "shape: type circular needs drawn"},
		{"circular key out of range", strings.Replace(circularFixture(), "key: 0", "key: 360", 1), "key angle must be 0 or more and less than 360"},
		{"circular key text", strings.Replace(circularFixture(), "key: 0", "key: top", 1), "key must be an angle in degrees or null"},
		{"circular angle out of range", strings.Replace(circularFixture(), "angle: 45", "angle: 400", 1), "angle is required, 0 or more and less than 360"},
		{"circular radius out of range", strings.Replace(circularFixture(), "radius: 0.7, angle: 315", "radius: 1.5, angle: 315", 1), "radius is required, from 0 to 1"},
		{"circular without radius", strings.Replace(circularFixture(), ", radius: 0}", "}", 1), "radius is required"},
		{"circular without positions", fixtureItem("t_din", fixtureViews, "    type: circular\n    contact: round\n    drawn: socket\n    positions: []\n", "  pins:\n"+pinLine("1", "L", "signal", "")), "positions must not be empty"},
		{"board without sides", strings.Replace(boardFixture(), "    left: [\"1\", null, \"2\"]\n    right: [\"3\", \"4\"]\n", "", 1), "a board needs at least one of left, right, top and bottom"},
		{"board bad connector", strings.Replace(boardFixture(), "connector: bottom", "connector: middle", 1), "shape: connector must be one of top, bottom, left, right, none"},
		{"board inner without label", strings.Replace(boardFixture(), "label: ICSP", "label: \"\"", 1), "inner 1 needs a label"},
		{"board with a plug", strings.Replace(boardFixture(), "    connector:", "    drawn: plug\n    connector:", 1), "field drawn is not used by type board"},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		_, err := Load(pinTreeFS(t, map[string]string{"pinouts/p.yaml": c.src}))
		if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), c.want) {
			t.Errorf("%s: error = %v, want it to contain %q", c.name, err, c.want)
		}
	}

	// The id space is shared with the other kinds.
	_, err := Load(pinTreeFS(t, map[string]string{"tables/t.yaml": baseTable, "pinouts/p.yaml": strings.Replace(basePinout, "id: t_conn", "id: t_sec", 1)}))
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "id is already used in tables/t.yaml") {
		t.Errorf("pinout with the id of a table: error = %v", err)
	}
	_, err = Load(pinTreeFS(t, map[string]string{"pinouts/p.yaml": basePinout, "pinouts/q.yaml": basePinout}))
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "id is already used in pinouts/p.yaml") {
		t.Errorf("two pinouts with one id: error = %v", err)
	}
	// A pinout does not belong in the other directories, nor a table in pinouts/; an empty file is an error.
	_, err = Load(pinTreeFS(t, map[string]string{"codes/k.yaml": basePinout}))
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "field shape not found in type ecalc.rawCode") {
		t.Errorf("pinout in codes/: error = %v", err)
	}
	_, err = Load(pinTreeFS(t, map[string]string{"pinouts/p.yaml": baseTable}))
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "field columns not found in type ecalc.rawPinout") {
		t.Errorf("table in pinouts/: error = %v", err)
	}
	_, err = Load(pinTreeFS(t, map[string]string{"pinouts/p.yaml": ""}))
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "the file is empty") {
		t.Errorf("empty file: error = %v", err)
	}
	// Pinouts need pinstyles.yaml.
	fsys := pinTreeFS(t, map[string]string{"pinouts/p.yaml": basePinout})
	delete(fsys, "pinstyles.yaml")
	_, err = Load(fsys)
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "pinstyles.yaml") {
		t.Errorf("pinouts without pinstyles.yaml: error = %v", err)
	}
}

// Every problem of an item is reported at once, with the file and the item.
func TestPinoutProblemsAreReportedTogether(t *testing.T) {
	src := mutate(t, basePinout, "group: data", "group: wires", "type: data", "type: bus", "wire: red", "wire: teal", `source: "Datasheet"`, `source: ""`)
	_, err := Load(pinTreeFS(t, map[string]string{"pinouts/p.yaml": src}))
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("want errors")
	}
	for _, want := range []string{"pinouts/p.yaml: t_conn: group must be", "t_conn: source is required", `pin "3": type must be`, `pin "1": wire "teal"`} {
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("error lacks %q:\n%v", want, err)
		}
	}
}

func dipFixture(n int) string {
	shape := "    type: dip\n    pins: " + itoa(n) + "\n"
	pins := "  pins:\n"
	for i := 1; i <= n && i <= 8; i++ {
		pins += pinLine(itoa(i), "P"+itoa(i), "io", "")
	}
	return fixtureItem("t_dip", "", shape, pins)
}

func itoa(n int) string {
	b, _ := json.Marshal(n)
	return string(b)
}

func toFixture(pkg, pins string) string {
	return fixtureItem("t_to", "", "    type: to\n    package: "+pkg+"\n    pins: "+pins+"\n",
		"  pins:\n"+pinLine("B", "B", "signal", "")+pinLine("C", "C", "signal", "")+pinLine("E", "E", "ground", ""))
}

func jackFixture(segments string) string {
	return fixtureItem("t_jack", "", "    type: jack\n    segments: "+segments+"\n",
		"  pins:\n"+pinLine("T", "L", "signal", "")+pinLine("R", "R", "signal", "")+pinLine("S", "GND", "ground", ""))
}

func circularFixture() string {
	return fixtureItem("t_din", fixtureViews, `    type: circular
    contact: round
    drawn: socket
    key: 0
    positions:
      - {pin: "1", angle: 45, radius: 0.7}
      - {pin: "2", radius: 0.7, angle: 315}
      - {pin: "3", angle: 0, radius: 0}
`, "  pins:\n"+pinLine("1", "L", "signal", "")+pinLine("2", "R", "signal", "")+pinLine("3", "GND", "ground", ""))
}

func boardFixture() string {
	return fixtureItem("t_board", "", `    type: board
    left: ["1", null, "2"]
    right: ["3", "4"]
    connector: bottom
    inner:
      - label: ICSP
        rows:
          - {pins: ["5", "6"]}
          - {pins: ["7", "8"], offset: 1}
`, "  pins:\n"+pinLine("1", "D0", "io", "")+pinLine("2", "D1", "io", "")+pinLine("3", "VIN", "power", "")+pinLine("4", "GND", "ground", "")+
		pinLine("5", "MISO", "data", "")+pinLine("6", "SCK", "data", "")+pinLine("7", "RST", "signal", "")+pinLine("8", "NC", "nc", ""))
}

// jsonItems loads the fixtures and returns the pinout items of the catalog JSON in a language.
func jsonItems(t *testing.T, cat *Catalog, lang string) (items []map[string]any, doc map[string]any) {
	t.Helper()
	body, _, err := cat.LocalizedJSON(lang)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &doc); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, it := range doc["items"].([]any) {
		items = append(items, it.(map[string]any))
	}
	return items, doc
}

// One item per shape type pins the JSON of a shape: every field is always there, with "", null or [] when unused.
func TestPinoutJSONShapes(t *testing.T) {
	all := basePinout + dipFixture(4) + toFixture("to92", `["B", "C", "E"]`) + circularFixture() + jackFixture(`["T", "R", "S"]`) + boardFixture()
	// dipFixture(4) lists 4 pins, to92 and the others 3 or more; the ids are distinct.
	cat := loadPinouts(t, all)
	items, doc := jsonItems(t, cat, "de")
	if len(items) != 6 {
		t.Fatalf("%d items, want 6", len(items))
	}
	types, wires := doc["pin_types"].([]any), doc["wires"].([]any)
	if len(types) != 6 || len(wires) != 15 {
		t.Errorf("pin_types %d, wires %d", len(types), len(wires))
	}

	row := func(offset float64, pins ...any) map[string]any {
		return map[string]any{"pins": append([]any{}, pins...), "offset": offset}
	}
	shape := func(over map[string]any) map[string]any {
		out := map[string]any{
			"type": "", "outline": "", "contact": "", "drawn": "", "key": nil, "rows": []any{}, "pins": nil, "package": "",
			"positions": []any{}, "segments": []any{}, "left": []any{}, "right": []any{}, "top": []any{}, "bottom": []any{},
			"connector": "", "inner": []any{},
		}
		for k, v := range over {
			out[k] = v
		}
		return out
	}
	want := map[string]map[string]any{
		"t_conn": shape(map[string]any{"type": "rows", "outline": "rect", "contact": "round", "drawn": "plug", "key": "top",
			"rows": []any{row(0, "1", "2"), row(0.5, "3")}}),
		"t_dip": shape(map[string]any{"type": "dip", "drawn": "top", "pins": float64(4)}),
		"t_to":  shape(map[string]any{"type": "to", "drawn": "front", "package": "to92", "pins": []any{"B", "C", "E"}}),
		"t_din": shape(map[string]any{"type": "circular", "contact": "round", "drawn": "socket", "key": float64(0),
			"positions": []any{
				map[string]any{"pin": "1", "angle": float64(45), "radius": 0.7},
				map[string]any{"pin": "2", "angle": float64(315), "radius": 0.7},
				map[string]any{"pin": "3", "angle": float64(0), "radius": float64(0)}}}),
		"t_jack": shape(map[string]any{"type": "jack", "drawn": "side", "segments": []any{"T", "R", "S"}}),
		"t_board": shape(map[string]any{"type": "board", "drawn": "top", "connector": "bottom",
			"left": []any{"1", nil, "2"}, "right": []any{"3", "4"},
			"inner": []any{map[string]any{"label": "ICSP", "rows": []any{row(0, "5", "6"), row(1, "7", "8")}}}}),
	}
	for _, it := range items {
		id := it["id"].(string)
		if len(it) != 14 {
			t.Errorf("%s has %d keys, want 14: %v", id, len(it), it)
		}
		if it["kind"] != "pinout" || it["category"] != "pinouts" || it["group"] != "data" || it["name"] != "T" || it["name_en"] != "T" ||
			it["doc"] != "Doku." || it["notes"] != "Hinweis." || it["source"] != "Datasheet" || !reflect.DeepEqual(it["tags"], []any{"test"}) {
			t.Errorf("%s: item = %v", id, it)
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(it["shape"], any(want[id])) {
			t.Errorf("%s: shape = %#v\nwant %#v", id, it["shape"], want[id])
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(it["variants"], []any{}) {
			t.Errorf("%s: variants = %#v, want []", id, it["variants"])
		}
		switch id {
		case "t_conn", "t_din":
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(it["views"], map[string]any{"plug": "Stecker", "socket": "Buchse"}) {
				t.Errorf("%s: views = %#v", id, it["views"])
			}
		default:
			if v, ok := it["views"]; !ok || v != nil {
				t.Errorf("%s: views = %#v, want null", id, v)
			}
		}
	}

	// The pins of the first item: all six keys, German texts, "" for notes and wire when unset.
	pins := items[0]["pins"].([]any)
	if len(pins) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("pins = %v", pins)
	}
	wantPin := []map[string]any{
		{"number": "1", "name": "VCC", "function": "Funktion VCC", "type": "power", "notes": "", "wire": "red"},
		{"number": "2", "name": "GND", "function": "Funktion GND", "type": "ground", "notes": "Auch Schirm.", "wire": ""},
		{"number": "3", "name": "TX", "function": "Funktion TX", "type": "data", "notes": "", "wire": ""},
	}
	for i, p := range pins {
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(p, any(wantPin[i])) {
			t.Errorf("pin %d = %#v, want %#v", i, p, wantPin[i])
		}
	}

	// A language without texts falls back to English.
	fr, _ := jsonItems(t, cat, "fr")
	if fr[0]["doc"] != "Doc." || fr[0]["pins"].([]any)[0].(map[string]any)["function"] != "Func VCC" ||
		fr[0]["views"].(map[string]any)["plug"] != "Male" {
		t.Errorf("French fallback: %v", fr[0])
	}
}

func TestPinoutJSONVariantsAndStyles(t *testing.T) {
	three := pinLine("1", "A", "power", "") + pinLine("2", "B", "ground", "") + pinLine("3", "C", "data", "")
	cat := loadPinouts(t, variantsOf(three, strings.Replace(three, `name: A`, `name: Z`, 1)))
	items, doc := jsonItems(t, cat, "en")
	it := items[0]
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(it["pins"], []any{}) {
		t.Errorf("an item with variants has pins = %#v, want []", it["pins"])
	}
	variants := it["variants"].([]any)
	if len(variants) != 2 || variants[1].(map[string]any)["id"] != "bb" || variants[1].(map[string]any)["name"] != "B" ||
		len(variants[1].(map[string]any)["pins"].([]any)) != 3 {
		t.Errorf("variants = %#v", variants)
	}
	types := doc["pin_types"].([]any)
	first := types[0].(map[string]any)
	if len(types) != 6 || first["id"] != "power" || first["hex"] != "#c62828" || first["ink"] != "#ffffff" || first["name"] != "Power" || len(first) != 4 {
		t.Errorf("pin_types = %v", types)
	}
	wires := doc["wires"].([]any)
	red, wg := wires[2].(map[string]any), wires[12].(map[string]any)
	if len(wires) != 15 || red["id"] != "red" || red["stripe"] != "" || wg["id"] != "white_green" || wg["stripe"] != "#2e7d32" || wg["name"] != "white-green" || len(red) != 4 {
		t.Errorf("wires = %v", wires)
	}
	_, deDoc := jsonItems(t, cat, "de")
	if deDoc["wires"].([]any)[12].(map[string]any)["name"] != "weiß-grün" || deDoc["pin_types"].([]any)[1].(map[string]any)["name"] != "Masse" {
		t.Errorf("German style names: %v", deDoc["wires"])
	}
}

// Without pinouts the pin styles still load, and without pinstyles.yaml the lists are empty arrays.
func TestCatalogWithoutPinouts(t *testing.T) {
	cat, err := Load(treeFS(t, nil))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Load without pinstyles.yaml: %v", err)
	}
	_, doc := jsonItems(t, cat, "en")
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(doc["pin_types"], []any{}) || !reflect.DeepEqual(doc["wires"], []any{}) {
		t.Errorf("pin_types = %#v, wires = %#v, want empty arrays", doc["pin_types"], doc["wires"])
	}
	if cat.Pinout("x") != nil || cat.PinType("power") != nil || cat.Wire("red") != nil || len(cat.Pinouts) != 0 {
		t.Error("an empty catalog must have no pinouts and no styles")
	}
}
```

`internal/ecalc/pinstyles.go`:
```go
package ecalc

import (
	"errors"
	"io"
	"io/fs"
	"math"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

// pinstyles.yaml holds the colours of the pinout drawings: one fill and ink per pin type and the standard wire colours.
// They are data and not theme tokens (a pin type must read the same on every skin).

// PinTypes are the six pin types of a pin, in the order of pinstyles.yaml.
var PinTypes = []string{"power", "ground", "signal", "data", "io", "nc"}

// wireIDs are the wire colours of pinstyles.yaml, in file order.
var wireIDs = []string{
	"black", "brown", "red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "purple", "grey", "white", "pink",
	"white_orange", "white_green", "white_blue", "white_brown",
}

var hexRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^#[0-9a-f]{6}$`)

// minInkContrast is the WCAG contrast that the ink of a pin type needs on its fill.
const minInkContrast = 4.5

// PinType is the colour of one pin type: the fill of its contacts and the ink of the number on it.
type PinType struct {
	ID   string
	Hex  string
	Ink  string
	Name Text
}

// Wire is a standard wire colour; Stripe is the second colour of a striped wire, "" for a plain one.
type Wire struct {
	ID     string
	Hex    string
	Stripe string
	Name   Text
}

// PinType returns the style of a pin type, or nil.
func (c *Catalog) PinType(id string) *PinType { return c.pinTypeByID[id] }

// Wire returns the wire colour with the given id, or nil.
func (c *Catalog) Wire(id string) *Wire { return c.wireByID[id] }

type rawStyle struct {
	Hex    string `yaml:"hex"`
	Ink    string `yaml:"ink"`
	Stripe string `yaml:"stripe"`
	Name   Text   `yaml:"name"`
}

// pinstyles reads pinstyles.yaml. The file may be missing from a catalog without pinouts; with pinouts it is required.
func (l *loader) pinstyles(fsys fs.FS, cat *Catalog, needed bool) {
	data, err := fs.ReadFile(fsys, "pinstyles.yaml")
	if err != nil {
		if needed || !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
			l.fail("pinstyles.yaml: %v", err)
		}
		return
	}
	var doc struct {
		Types yaml.Node `yaml:"types"`
		Wires yaml.Node `yaml:"wires"`
	}
	if err := decodeStrict(data, &doc); err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
			err = errors.New("the file is empty")
		}
		l.fail("pinstyles.yaml: %v", err)
		return
	}
	types, err := orderedMap(&doc.Types, "pinstyles.yaml: types")
	if err != nil {
		l.fail("%v", err)
	}
	var typeIDs []string
	for _, e := range types {
		typeIDs = append(typeIDs, e.Key)
		what := "pinstyles.yaml: type " + e.Key
		var rs rawStyle
		if err := decodeNode(e.Val, &rs); err != nil {
			l.fail("%s: %v", what, err)
			continue
		}
		l.styleColour(what, "hex", rs.Hex, false)
		l.styleColour(what, "ink", rs.Ink, false)
		if rs.Stripe != "" {
			l.fail("%s: stripe is only for wires", what)
		}
		if hexRe.MatchString(rs.Hex) && hexRe.MatchString(rs.Ink) {
			if c := contrastRatio(rs.Ink, rs.Hex); c < minInkContrast {
				l.fail("%s: ink %s on %s has a contrast of %.2f, need at least %.1f", what, rs.Ink, rs.Hex, c, minInkContrast)
			}
		}
		l.checkText(what+": name", rs.Name, Locales)
		pt := &PinType{ID: e.Key, Hex: rs.Hex, Ink: rs.Ink, Name: rs.Name}
		cat.PinTypeStyles = append(cat.PinTypeStyles, pt)
		cat.pinTypeByID[e.Key] = pt
	}
	if !equalLists(typeIDs, PinTypes) {
		l.fail("pinstyles.yaml: types must be %s in this order, got %s", strings.Join(PinTypes, ", "), strings.Join(typeIDs, ", "))
	}

	wires, err := orderedMap(&doc.Wires, "pinstyles.yaml: wires")
	if err != nil {
		l.fail("%v", err)
	}
	var ids []string
	for _, e := range wires {
		ids = append(ids, e.Key)
		what := "pinstyles.yaml: wire " + e.Key
		var rs rawStyle
		if err := decodeNode(e.Val, &rs); err != nil {
			l.fail("%s: %v", what, err)
			continue
		}
		l.styleColour(what, "hex", rs.Hex, false)
		l.styleColour(what, "stripe", rs.Stripe, true)
		if rs.Ink != "" {
			l.fail("%s: ink is only for pin types", what)
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(e.Key, "white_") && rs.Stripe == "" {
			l.fail("%s: a striped wire needs a stripe colour", what)
		}
		l.checkText(what+": name", rs.Name, Locales)
		w := &Wire{ID: e.Key, Hex: rs.Hex, Stripe: rs.Stripe, Name: rs.Name}
		cat.Wires = append(cat.Wires, w)
		cat.wireByID[e.Key] = w
	}
	if !equalLists(ids, wireIDs) {
		l.fail("pinstyles.yaml: wires must be %s in this order, got %s", strings.Join(wireIDs, ", "), strings.Join(ids, ", "))
	}
}

// styleColour checks a #rrggbb colour (lower case); an optional one may be empty.
func (l *loader) styleColour(what, field, value string, optional bool) {
	if value == "" && optional {
		return
	}
	if !hexRe.MatchString(value) {
		l.fail("%s: %s must be a colour like #1565c0 (lower case), got %q", what, field, value)
	}
}

func equalLists(a, b []string) bool {
	if len(a) != len(b) {
		return false
	}
	for i := range a {
		if a[i] != b[i] {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// luminance is the WCAG relative luminance of a #rrggbb colour.
func luminance(hex string) float64 {
	var c [3]float64
	for i := range c {
		v, _ := strconv.ParseUint(hex[1+2*i:3+2*i], 16, 8)
		s := float64(v) / 255
		if s <= 0.03928 {
			c[i] = s / 12.92
		} else {
			c[i] = math.Pow((s+0.055)/1.055, 2.4)
		}
	}
	return 0.2126*c[0] + 0.7152*c[1] + 0.0722*c[2]
}

// contrastRatio is the WCAG contrast ratio of two #rrggbb colours (1 to 21).
func contrastRatio(a, b string) float64 {
	la, lb := luminance(a), luminance(b)
	if la < lb {
		la, lb = lb, la
	}
	return (la + 0.05) / (lb + 0.05)
}

type pinTypeJSON struct {
	ID   string `json:"id"`
	Hex  string `json:"hex"`
	Ink  string `json:"ink"`
	Name string `json:"name"`
}

type wireJSON struct {
	ID     string `json:"id"`
	Hex    string `json:"hex"`
	Stripe string `json:"stripe"`
	Name   string `json:"name"`
}

func (c *Catalog) pinStylesJSON(lang string) ([]pinTypeJSON, []wireJSON) {
	types := make([]pinTypeJSON, 0, len(c.PinTypeStyles))
	for _, t := range c.PinTypeStyles {
		types = append(types, pinTypeJSON{ID: t.ID, Hex: t.Hex, Ink: t.Ink, Name: t.Name.in(lang)})
	}
	wires := make([]wireJSON, 0, len(c.Wires))
	for _, w := range c.Wires {
		wires = append(wires, wireJSON{ID: w.ID, Hex: w.Hex, Stripe: w.Stripe, Name: w.Name.in(lang)})
	}
	return types, wires
}
```

`internal/ecalc/pinouts.go`:
```go
package ecalc

import (
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"math"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

// Pinout items: a catalog item of kind "pinout" (pinouts/*.yaml) describes a connector, a board header or an IC package:
// the pins with number, name, function, type and optionally the wire colour, and the shape that the page draws. The
// loader checks every rule; the drawing itself is in the page (ecalc-pinout-draw.js).

const pinoutsCategory = "pinouts"

// PinoutGroups are the list sections of the pinout rail, in display order.
var PinoutGroups = []string{"data", "audio", "pc_power", "boards", "debug", "ics"}

// PinoutOutlines are the outlines of a "rows" shape (sorted); the page draws every one of them.
var PinoutOutlines = []string{
	"displayport", "dsub", "hdmi_a", "jst", "minifit", "molex", "obd2", "rect", "rj45", "sata_data", "sata_power",
	"usb_a", "usb_b", "usb_c", "usb_micro_b", "usb_mini_b",
}

var (
	pinoutContacts   = []string{"round", "square", "blade"}
	pinoutDrawn      = []string{"plug", "socket"}
	pinoutRowKeys    = []string{"none", "top", "bottom", "left", "right"}
	pinoutConnectors = []string{"top", "bottom", "left", "right", "none"}
	pinoutPackages   = []string{"to92", "to220"}
	pinoutShapeTypes = []string{"rows", "dip", "to", "circular", "jack", "board"}
)

const (
	maxPinNumberLen = 8
	maxPinNameLen   = 24
	maxRowOffset    = 2.0
)

// Pin is one pin of a connector. Function and Notes are localized; Wire is an id of pinstyles.yaml or "".
type Pin struct {
	Number, Name, Type, Wire string
	Function, Notes          Text
}

// PinoutVariant is one variant of a pinout (T568A and T568B, CTIA and OMTP): the same pin numbers, other pins.
type PinoutVariant struct {
	ID   string
	Name Text
	Pins []Pin
}

// PinoutRow is one row of a "rows" shape or of an inner header, as seen looking at the mating face: Pins are the pin
// numbers left to right, "" is an empty position, Offset is the shift to the right in pitches.
type PinoutRow struct {
	Pins   []string
	Offset float64
}

// PinoutPosition places a pin of a "circular" shape: Angle in degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock, Radius from 0 (centre)
// to 1 (the shell).
type PinoutPosition struct {
	Pin           string
	Angle, Radius float64
}

// PinoutInner is an extra header on a "board" shape with a neutral label (ICSP).
type PinoutInner struct {
	Label string
	Rows  []PinoutRow
}

// PinoutShape is the typed shape. Type is rows, dip, to, circular, jack or board; the fields of the other types are zero.
//
//	rows:     Outline, Contact, Drawn (plug|socket), Rows, Key (none|top|bottom|left|right, none unless the outline is rect)
//	dip:      DipPins (even, 4 to 64; the pins are "1" ... "N")
//	to:       Package (to92|to220), ToPins (left to right)
//	circular: Contact, Drawn (plug|socket), KeyAngle (nil = no notch), Positions
//	jack:     Segments (tip to sleeve, 2 to 5)
//	board:    Left, Right (top to bottom), Top, Bottom (left to right), "" = a gap of one pitch; Connector, Inner
type PinoutShape struct {
	Type, Outline, Contact, Drawn, Key string
	KeyAngle                           *float64
	Rows                               []PinoutRow
	DipPins                            int
	Package                            string
	ToPins                             []string
	Positions                          []PinoutPosition
	Segments                           []string
	Left, Right, Top, Bottom           []string
	Connector                          string
	Inner                              []PinoutInner
}

// Numbers lists every pin number that the shape names, in drawing order (a dip as "1" ... "N"); gaps are left out.
func (s PinoutShape) Numbers() []string {
	var out []string
	add := func(list []string) {
		for _, n := range list {
			if n != "" {
				out = append(out, n)
			}
		}
	}
	rows := func(rows []PinoutRow) {
		for _, r := range rows {
			add(r.Pins)
		}
	}
	switch s.Type {
	case "rows":
		rows(s.Rows)
	case "dip":
		for i := 1; i <= s.DipPins; i++ {
			out = append(out, strconv.Itoa(i))
		}
	case "to":
		add(s.ToPins)
	case "circular":
		for _, p := range s.Positions {
			out = append(out, p.Pin)
		}
	case "jack":
		add(s.Segments)
	case "board":
		add(s.Left)
		add(s.Right)
		add(s.Top)
		add(s.Bottom)
		for _, in := range s.Inner {
			rows(in.Rows)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// Pinout is a catalog item of kind "pinout". Views is nil when the shape has one fixed view; Pins is empty when the
// item has Variants.
type Pinout struct {
	ID, Category, Group string
	Name, Doc, Notes    Text
	Tags                []string
	Source              string
	Views               map[string]Text // "plug" and "socket" captions, nil when the shape has one view
	Shape               PinoutShape
	Pins                []Pin
	Variants            []PinoutVariant
}

// PinsOf returns the pins of a variant, "" meaning the pins of the item or the first variant, together with the id of the
// variant used. ok is false for a variant the item does not have.
func (p *Pinout) PinsOf(variant string) (pins []Pin, id string, ok bool) {
	if len(p.Variants) == 0 {
		return p.Pins, "", variant == ""
	}
	if variant == "" {
		return p.Variants[0].Pins, p.Variants[0].ID, true
	}
	for _, v := range p.Variants {
		if v.ID == variant {
			return v.Pins, v.ID, true
		}
	}
	return nil, "", false
}

// Pinout returns the pinout item with the given id, or nil.
func (c *Catalog) Pinout(id string) *Pinout { return c.pinoutByID[id] }

type rawPinRow struct {
	Pins   []*string `yaml:"pins"`
	Offset float64   `yaml:"offset"`
}

type rawPosition struct {
	Pin    string   `yaml:"pin"`
	Angle  *float64 `yaml:"angle"`
	Radius *float64 `yaml:"radius"`
}

type rawInner struct {
	Label string      `yaml:"label"`
	Rows  []rawPinRow `yaml:"rows"`
}

type rawPinoutShape struct {
	Type      string        `yaml:"type"`
	Outline   string        `yaml:"outline"`
	Contact   string        `yaml:"contact"`
	Drawn     string        `yaml:"drawn"`
	Key       yaml.Node     `yaml:"key"`
	Rows      []rawPinRow   `yaml:"rows"`
	Pins      yaml.Node     `yaml:"pins"`
	Package   string        `yaml:"package"`
	Positions []rawPosition `yaml:"positions"`
	Segments  []string      `yaml:"segments"`
	Left      []*string     `yaml:"left"`
	Right     []*string     `yaml:"right"`
	Top       []*string     `yaml:"top"`
	Bottom    []*string     `yaml:"bottom"`
	Connector string        `yaml:"connector"`
	Inner     []rawInner    `yaml:"inner"`
}

type rawPin struct {
	Number   string `yaml:"number"`

type rawVariant struct {
	ID   string   `yaml:"id"`

type rawPinout struct {
	ID       string          `yaml:"id"`
	Kind     string          `yaml:"kind"`
	Category string          `yaml:"category"`
	Group    string          `yaml:"group"`
	Name     Text            `yaml:"name"`
	Doc      Text            `yaml:"doc"`
	Notes    Text            `yaml:"notes"`
	Tags     []string        `yaml:"tags"`
	Source   string          `yaml:"source"`
	Views    map[string]Text `yaml:"views"`
	Shape    rawPinoutShape  `yaml:"shape"`
	Pins     []rawPin        `yaml:"pins"`
	Variants []rawVariant    `yaml:"variants"`
}

// shapeFields are the fields of a shape that each type uses.
var shapeFields = map[string][]string{
	"rows":     {"outline", "contact", "drawn", "key", "rows"},
	"dip":      {"pins"},
	"to":       {"package", "pins"},
	"circular": {"contact", "drawn", "key", "positions"},
	"jack":     {"segments"},
	"board":    {"left", "right", "top", "bottom", "connector", "inner"},
}

// fieldsSet lists the fields that a shape has written down.
func (s *rawPinoutShape) fieldsSet() map[string]bool {
	return map[string]bool{
		"outline": s.Outline != "", "contact": s.Contact != "", "drawn": s.Drawn != "", "key": s.Key.Kind != 0,
		"rows": s.Rows != nil, "pins": s.Pins.Kind != 0, "package": s.Package != "", "positions": s.Positions != nil,
		"segments": s.Segments != nil, "left": s.Left != nil, "right": s.Right != nil, "top": s.Top != nil, "bottom": s.Bottom != nil,
		"connector": s.Connector != "", "inner": s.Inner != nil,
	}
}

// pinouts reads pinouts/*.yaml (sorted) into the catalog.
func (l *loader) pinouts(fsys fs.FS, cat *Catalog) error {
	files, err := fs.Glob(fsys, "pinouts/*.yaml")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	sort.Strings(files)
	for _, file := range files {
		raws, ok := readItems[rawPinout](l, fsys, file)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		for i := range raws {
			if p := l.pinout(file, &raws[i], cat); p != nil {
				cat.Pinouts = append(cat.Pinouts, p)
				cat.pinoutByID[p.ID] = p
				cat.kinds[p.ID] = "pinout"
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// pinout builds and validates one pinout item; it returns nil when something is wrong.
func (l *loader) pinout(file string, r *rawPinout, cat *Catalog) *Pinout {
	before := len(l.errs)
	label := r.ID
	if label == "" {
		label = "(item without id)"
	}
	fail := func(format string, args ...any) {
		l.errs = append(l.errs, fmt.Errorf("%s: %s: %s", file, label, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)))
	}
	text := func(what string, t Text, required []string) {
		l.checkText(fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s: %s", file, label, what), t, required)
	}
	p := &Pinout{ID: r.ID, Category: r.Category, Group: r.Group, Name: r.Name, Doc: r.Doc, Notes: r.Notes, Tags: r.Tags, Source: r.Source}
	l.claimID(r.ID, file, fail)
	if r.Kind != "pinout" {
		fail("kind must be pinout in pinouts/, got %q", r.Kind)
	}
	if r.Category != pinoutsCategory {
		fail("category must be %s, got %q", pinoutsCategory, r.Category)
	}
	if !contains(PinoutGroups, r.Group) {
		fail("group must be one of %s, got %q", strings.Join(PinoutGroups, ", "), r.Group)
	}
	l.commonFields(fail, text, r.Name, r.Doc, r.Tags, r.Source)
	if len(r.Notes) > 0 {
		text("notes", r.Notes, docLocales)
	}

	shapeProblems := 0
	shape, shapeNumbers := buildShape(&r.Shape, func(format string, args ...any) {
		shapeProblems++
		fail(format, args...)
	})
	p.Shape = shape

	// The captions of the two views belong to the shapes that can be drawn as plug and as socket.
	twoViews := shape.Drawn == "plug" || shape.Drawn == "socket"
	switch {
	case twoViews && len(r.Views) == 0:
		fail("views are required when the shape is drawn as plug or socket")
	case !twoViews && len(r.Views) > 0:
		fail("views are only for shapes that are drawn as plug or socket")
	case twoViews:
		for _, v := range pinoutDrawn {
			if len(r.Views[v]) == 0 {
				fail("views: missing %q caption", v)
			} else {
				text("views."+v, r.Views[v], docLocales)
			}
		}
		for v := range r.Views {
			if !contains(pinoutDrawn, v) {
				fail("views: unknown view %q (plug, socket)", v)
			}
		}
		p.Views = r.Views
	}

	// Pins or variants.
	var pinLists [][]Pin
	var listNames []string
	switch {
	case len(r.Pins) > 0 && len(r.Variants) > 0:
		fail("use either pins or variants, not both")
	case len(r.Pins) == 0 && len(r.Variants) == 0:
		fail("pins or variants are required")
	case len(r.Pins) > 0:
		p.Pins = l.pins(fail, text, "pins", r.Pins, cat)
		pinLists, listNames = [][]Pin{p.Pins}, []string{"pins"}
	default:
		if len(r.Variants) < 2 {
			fail("variants needs at least 2 variants (use pins for a single one)")
		}
		seen := map[string]bool{}
		for i := range r.Variants {
			rv := &r.Variants[i]
			what := "variant " + rv.ID
			switch {
			case !idRe.MatchString(rv.ID):
				fail("variant id %q must match %s", rv.ID, idRe)
				what = fmt.Sprintf("variant %d", i+1)
			case seen[rv.ID]:
				fail("variant id %q is used twice", rv.ID)
			}
			seen[rv.ID] = true
			text(what+": name", rv.Name, docLocales)
			v := PinoutVariant{ID: rv.ID, Name: rv.Name, Pins: l.pins(fail, text, what+": pins", rv.Pins, cat)}
			p.Variants = append(p.Variants, v)
			pinLists, listNames = append(pinLists, v.Pins), append(listNames, what)
		}
	}

	// Every variant has the same pin numbers, and the shape draws exactly those.
	if len(pinLists) > 0 {
		base := numbersOf(pinLists[0])
		for i := 1; i < len(pinLists); i++ {
			if missing, extra := diffNumbers(base, numbersOf(pinLists[i])); len(missing)+len(extra) > 0 {
				fail("%s has other pin numbers than %s (missing %s; extra %s)", listNames[i], listNames[0], listOrNone(missing), listOrNone(extra))
			}
		}
		if shapeProblems == 0 { // a broken shape would only add noise
			coverage(fail, shapeNumbers, base)
		}
	}
	if len(l.errs) > before {
		return nil
	}
	return p
}

func listOrNone(list []string) string {
	if len(list) == 0 {
		return "none"
	}
	return strings.Join(list, ", ")
}

func numbersOf(pins []Pin) []string {
	out := make([]string, len(pins))
	for i, p := range pins {
		out[i] = p.Number
	}
	return out
}

// diffNumbers returns the numbers of want that are not in got, and those of got that are not in want.
func diffNumbers(want, got []string) (missing, extra []string) {
	in := func(list []string, s string) bool { return contains(list, s) }
	for _, n := range want {
		if !in(got, n) {
			missing = append(missing, n)
		}
	}
	for _, n := range got {
		if !in(want, n) {
			extra = append(extra, n)
		}
	}
	return missing, extra
}

// coverage checks that every pin is drawn exactly once and that every position of the shape names a pin.
func coverage(fail func(string, ...any), shape, pins []string) {
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, n := range shape {
		if seen[n] {
			fail("shape: pin %q is drawn more than once", n)
		}
		seen[n] = true
	}
	for _, n := range shape {
		if !contains(pins, n) {
			fail("shape: position %q names no pin", n)
			pins = append(pins[:len(pins):len(pins)], n) // report it once
		}
	}
	for _, n := range pins {
		if !seen[n] {
			fail("shape: pin %q is not drawn", n)
		}
	}
}

// pins validates and converts one list of pins; what names the list in messages.
func (l *loader) pins(fail func(string, ...any), text func(string, Text, []string), what string, raws []rawPin, cat *Catalog) []Pin {
	out := make([]Pin, 0, len(raws))
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for i, rp := range raws {
		label := fmt.Sprintf("%s: pin %q", what, rp.Number)
		if rp.Number == "" {
			label = fmt.Sprintf("%s: pin %d", what, i+1)
		}
		switch n := utf8.RuneCountInString(rp.Number); {
		case strings.TrimSpace(rp.Number) != rp.Number || n == 0 || n > maxPinNumberLen:
			fail("%s: number must be 1 to %d characters without surrounding spaces", label, maxPinNumberLen)
		case seen[rp.Number]:
			fail("%s: number is used twice", label)
		}
		seen[rp.Number] = true
		if n := utf8.RuneCountInString(rp.Name); strings.TrimSpace(rp.Name) != rp.Name || n == 0 || n > maxPinNameLen {
			fail("%s: name must be 1 to %d characters without surrounding spaces", label, maxPinNameLen)
		}
		text(label+": function", rp.Function, docLocales)
		if len(rp.Notes) > 0 {
			text(label+": notes", rp.Notes, docLocales)
		}
		if !contains(PinTypes, rp.Type) {
			fail("%s: type must be one of %s, got %q", label, strings.Join(PinTypes, ", "), rp.Type)
		}
		if rp.Wire != "" && cat.wireByID[rp.Wire] == nil {
			fail("%s: wire %q is not in pinstyles.yaml (%s)", label, rp.Wire, strings.Join(wireIDs, ", "))
		}
		out = append(out, Pin{Number: rp.Number, Name: rp.Name, Type: rp.Type, Wire: rp.Wire, Function: rp.Function, Notes: rp.Notes})
	}
	return out
}

// buildShape validates a raw shape and returns the typed one together with every pin number that it names.
func buildShape(raw *rawPinoutShape, fail func(string, ...any)) (PinoutShape, []string) {
	s := PinoutShape{Type: raw.Type}
	if !contains(pinoutShapeTypes, raw.Type) {
		fail("shape: type must be one of %s, got %q", strings.Join(pinoutShapeTypes, ", "), raw.Type)
		return s, nil
	}
	set := raw.fieldsSet()
	names := make([]string, 0, len(set))
	for name := range set {
		names = append(names, name)
	}
	sort.Strings(names)
	for _, name := range names {
		if set[name] && !contains(shapeFields[raw.Type], name) {
			fail("shape: field %s is not used by type %s", name, raw.Type)
		}
	}
	need := func(name string) bool {
		if !set[name] {
			fail("shape: type %s needs %s", raw.Type, name)
		}
		return set[name]
	}
	oneOf := func(what, v string, list []string) string {
		if !contains(list, v) {
			fail("shape: %s must be one of %s, got %q", what, strings.Join(list, ", "), v)
		}
		return v
	}

	switch raw.Type {
	case "rows":
		s.Outline, s.Contact, s.Drawn, s.Key = raw.Outline, raw.Contact, raw.Drawn, "none"
		if need("outline") {
			oneOf("outline", raw.Outline, PinoutOutlines)
		}
		if need("contact") {
			oneOf("contact", raw.Contact, pinoutContacts)
		}
		if need("drawn") {
			oneOf("drawn", raw.Drawn, pinoutDrawn)
		}
		if set["key"] {
			var key string
			if raw.Key.Kind != yaml.ScalarNode || raw.Key.Decode(&key) != nil {
				fail("shape: key must be one of %s", strings.Join(pinoutRowKeys, ", "))
			} else {
				s.Key = oneOf("key", key, pinoutRowKeys)
				if key != "none" && raw.Outline != "rect" {
					fail("shape: key %s needs the outline rect", key)
				}
			}
		}
		if need("rows") {
			s.Rows = shapeRows(fail, "rows", raw.Rows)
		}
	case "dip":
		if need("pins") {
			var n int
			if raw.Pins.Kind != yaml.ScalarNode || raw.Pins.Decode(&n) != nil {
				fail("shape: pins of a dip must be the number of pins")
			} else if n < 4 || n > 64 || n%2 != 0 {
				fail("shape: a dip has an even number of pins from 4 to 64, got %d", n)
			} else {
				s.DipPins = n
			}
		}
		s.Drawn = "top"
	case "to":
		s.Drawn = "front"
		if need("package") {
			s.Package = oneOf("package", raw.Package, pinoutPackages)
		}
		if need("pins") {
			var list []string
			switch {
			case raw.Pins.Kind != yaml.SequenceNode || raw.Pins.Decode(&list) != nil:
				fail("shape: pins of a to shape must be the list of pin numbers, left to right")
			case len(list) < 2 || len(list) > 5:
				fail("shape: a to shape has 2 to 5 pins, got %d", len(list))
			default:
				for _, n := range list {
					if n == "" {
						fail("shape: pins must not contain an empty number")
					}
				}
				s.ToPins = list
			}
		}
	case "circular":
		s.Contact, s.Drawn = raw.Contact, raw.Drawn
		if need("contact") {
			oneOf("contact", raw.Contact, pinoutContacts)
		}
		if need("drawn") {
			oneOf("drawn", raw.Drawn, pinoutDrawn)
		}
		if set["key"] {
			var k *float64
			if raw.Key.Kind != yaml.ScalarNode || raw.Key.Decode(&k) != nil {
				fail("shape: key must be an angle in degrees or null")
			} else if k != nil && (*k < 0 || *k >= 360 || math.IsNaN(*k)) {
				fail("shape: key angle must be 0 or more and less than 360, got %v", *k)
			} else {
				s.KeyAngle = k
			}
		}
		if need("positions") {
			if len(raw.Positions) == 0 {
				fail("shape: positions must not be empty")
			}
			for i, rp := range raw.Positions {
				where := fmt.Sprintf("shape: position %d", i+1)
				switch {
				case rp.Pin == "":
					fail("%s: pin is required", where)
				case rp.Angle == nil || *rp.Angle < 0 || *rp.Angle >= 360 || math.IsNaN(*rp.Angle):
					fail("%s (pin %s): angle is required, 0 or more and less than 360", where, rp.Pin)
				case rp.Radius == nil || *rp.Radius < 0 || *rp.Radius > 1 || math.IsNaN(*rp.Radius):
					fail("%s (pin %s): radius is required, from 0 to 1", where, rp.Pin)
				default:
					s.Positions = append(s.Positions, PinoutPosition{Pin: rp.Pin, Angle: *rp.Angle, Radius: *rp.Radius})
				}
			}
		}
	case "jack":
		s.Drawn = "side"
		if need("segments") {
			if len(raw.Segments) < 2 || len(raw.Segments) > 5 {
				fail("shape: a jack has 2 to 5 segments, got %d", len(raw.Segments))
			}
			for _, seg := range raw.Segments {
				if seg == "" {
					fail("shape: segments must not contain an empty number")
				}
			}
			s.Segments = raw.Segments
		}
	case "board":
		s.Drawn = "top"
		s.Connector = raw.Connector
		if need("connector") {
			oneOf("connector", raw.Connector, pinoutConnectors)
		}
		if raw.Left == nil && raw.Right == nil && raw.Top == nil && raw.Bottom == nil {
			fail("shape: a board needs at least one of left, right, top and bottom")
		}
		s.Left = shapeList(fail, "left", raw.Left)
		s.Right = shapeList(fail, "right", raw.Right)
		s.Top = shapeList(fail, "top", raw.Top)
		s.Bottom = shapeList(fail, "bottom", raw.Bottom)
		for i, in := range raw.Inner {
			where := fmt.Sprintf("inner %d", i+1)
			if strings.TrimSpace(in.Label) == "" {
				fail("shape: %s needs a label", where)
			}
			s.Inner = append(s.Inner, PinoutInner{Label: in.Label, Rows: shapeRows(fail, where+" rows", in.Rows)})
		}
	}
	return s, s.Numbers()
}

// shapeList converts a list of pin numbers where null is a gap.
func shapeList(fail func(string, ...any), what string, in []*string) []string {
	out := make([]string, len(in))
	hasPin := false
	for i, n := range in {
		if n == nil {
			continue
		}
		if strings.TrimSpace(*n) == "" {
			fail("shape: %s has an empty pin number (write null for a gap)", what)
		}
		out[i] = *n
		hasPin = true
	}
	if in != nil && !hasPin {
		fail("shape: %s has no pins", what)
	}
	return out
}

// shapeRows converts the rows of a rows shape or of an inner header.
func shapeRows(fail func(string, ...any), what string, in []rawPinRow) []PinoutRow {
	if len(in) == 0 {
		fail("shape: %s must not be empty", what)
	}
	out := make([]PinoutRow, 0, len(in))
	for i, r := range in {
		if r.Offset < 0 || r.Offset > maxRowOffset || math.IsNaN(r.Offset) {
			fail("shape: %s %d: offset must be from 0 to %v pitches, got %v", what, i+1, maxRowOffset, r.Offset)
		}
		out = append(out, PinoutRow{Pins: shapeList(fail, fmt.Sprintf("%s %d", what, i+1), r.Pins), Offset: r.Offset})
	}
	return out
}

// The catalog JSON of a pinout; every field of a shape is always there.
type pinoutViewsJSON struct {
	Plug   string `json:"plug"`
	Socket string `json:"socket"`
}

type pinoutPinJSON struct {
	Number   string `json:"number"`
	Name     string `json:"name"`
	Function string `json:"function"`
	Type     string `json:"type"`
	Notes    string `json:"notes"`
	Wire     string `json:"wire"`
}

type pinoutVariantJSON struct {
	ID   string          `json:"id"`
	Name string          `json:"name"`
	Pins []pinoutPinJSON `json:"pins"`
}

type pinoutRowJSON struct {
	Pins   []*string `json:"pins"`
	Offset float64   `json:"offset"`
}

type pinoutPositionJSON struct {
	Pin    string  `json:"pin"`
	Angle  float64 `json:"angle"`
	Radius float64 `json:"radius"`
}

type pinoutInnerJSON struct {
	Label string          `json:"label"`
	Rows  []pinoutRowJSON `json:"rows"`
}

type pinoutShapeJSON struct {
	Type      string               `json:"type"`
	Outline   string               `json:"outline"`
	Contact   string               `json:"contact"`
	Drawn     string               `json:"drawn"`
	Key       any                  `json:"key"`
	Rows      []pinoutRowJSON      `json:"rows"`
	Pins      any                  `json:"pins"`
	Package   string               `json:"package"`
	Positions []pinoutPositionJSON `json:"positions"`
	Segments  []string             `json:"segments"`
	Left      []*string            `json:"left"`
	Right     []*string            `json:"right"`
	Top       []*string            `json:"top"`
	Bottom    []*string            `json:"bottom"`
	Connector string               `json:"connector"`
	Inner     []pinoutInnerJSON    `json:"inner"`
}

type pinoutJSON struct {
	Kind     string              `json:"kind"`
	ID       string              `json:"id"`
	Category string              `json:"category"`
	Group    string              `json:"group"`
	Name     string              `json:"name"`
	NameEN   string              `json:"name_en"`
	Doc      string              `json:"doc"`
	Notes    string              `json:"notes"`
	Tags     []string            `json:"tags"`
	Source   string              `json:"source"`
	Views    *pinoutViewsJSON    `json:"views"`
	Shape    pinoutShapeJSON     `json:"shape"`
	Pins     []pinoutPinJSON     `json:"pins"`
	Variants []pinoutVariantJSON `json:"variants"`
}

// gapList writes a list of pin numbers with null for a gap; the list is never null.
func gapList(in []string) []*string {
	out := make([]*string, len(in))
	for i := range in {
		if in[i] != "" {
			out[i] = &in[i]
		}
	}
	return out
}

func rowsJSON(in []PinoutRow) []pinoutRowJSON {
	out := make([]pinoutRowJSON, len(in))
	for i, r := range in {
		out[i] = pinoutRowJSON{Pins: gapList(r.Pins), Offset: r.Offset}
	}
	return out
}

func pinsJSON(in []Pin, lang string) []pinoutPinJSON {
	out := make([]pinoutPinJSON, len(in))
	for i, p := range in {
		out[i] = pinoutPinJSON{Number: p.Number, Name: p.Name, Function: p.Function.in(lang), Type: p.Type, Notes: p.Notes.in(lang), Wire: p.Wire}
	}
	return out
}

func (p *Pinout) json(lang string) pinoutJSON {
	out := pinoutJSON{
		Kind: "pinout", ID: p.ID, Category: p.Category, Group: p.Group, Name: p.Name.in(lang), NameEN: p.Name.in("en"),
		Doc: p.Doc.in(lang), Notes: p.Notes.in(lang), Tags: orEmpty(p.Tags), Source: p.Source,
		Pins: pinsJSON(p.Pins, lang), Variants: make([]pinoutVariantJSON, 0, len(p.Variants)),
	}
	if p.Views != nil {
		out.Views = &pinoutViewsJSON{Plug: p.Views["plug"].in(lang), Socket: p.Views["socket"].in(lang)}
	}
	for _, v := range p.Variants {
		out.Variants = append(out.Variants, pinoutVariantJSON{ID: v.ID, Name: v.Name.in(lang), Pins: pinsJSON(v.Pins, lang)})
	}
	s := p.Shape
	sj := pinoutShapeJSON{
		Type: s.Type, Outline: s.Outline, Contact: s.Contact, Drawn: s.Drawn, Rows: rowsJSON(s.Rows), Package: s.Package,
		Positions: make([]pinoutPositionJSON, len(s.Positions)), Segments: orEmpty(s.Segments),
		Left: gapList(s.Left), Right: gapList(s.Right), Top: gapList(s.Top), Bottom: gapList(s.Bottom),
		Connector: s.Connector, Inner: make([]pinoutInnerJSON, len(s.Inner)),
	}
	switch s.Type {
	case "rows":
		sj.Key = s.Key
	case "circular":
		if s.KeyAngle != nil {
			sj.Key = *s.KeyAngle
		}
	case "dip":
		sj.Pins = s.DipPins
	case "to":
		sj.Pins = s.ToPins
	}
	for i, pos := range s.Positions {
		sj.Positions[i] = pinoutPositionJSON{Pin: pos.Pin, Angle: pos.Angle, Radius: pos.Radius}
	}
	for i, in := range s.Inner {
		sj.Inner[i] = pinoutInnerJSON{Label: in.Label, Rows: rowsJSON(in.Rows)}
	}
	out.Shape = sj
	return out
}
```
