## Part B — Agent tool action `pinout` (tasks B1–B4)


**Goal:** The `ecalc` agent tool reads pinouts (contract section 8): the new operation `pinout` (`id`, `pin`, `variant`, `filter`, `offset`, `limit`) answers the pins of one variant in English, `search`, `describe`, `open`, `Overview` and `ItemCount` cover the pinout items, `pinout` is a read operation that A2A peers may use, the manual and the user documentation (en and de) describe it. No real pinout items: the tests run on fixture pinouts.

**Architecture:** `internal/ecalc/query_pinout.go` holds the query API (`QueryPinout`, `DescribePinout`, the texts for connector and view) next to `query_table.go` and `query_codes.go`; `query.go` and `query_items.go` learn the fourth item kind. `internal/tools/ecalc.go` gets the operation, the fit to the inline budget (`ecalcFit`) and the describe/open cases, and its entry point is split into `ExecuteECalc` (loads the shipped catalog) and `executeECalc(cfg, cat, req)` so that tests can hand it a fixture catalog. `internal/agent` gets the schema (enum, `pin`, `variant`), the argument decoding, the A2A read list, the discovery texts and the manual.

**Tech stack:** Go 1.27, `testing/fstest`. `GOTMPDIR` = `C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p4-b` (any short backslash path per agent).

**Base:** the ECalc phase 3 state plus Part A (`ecalc.Pinout`, `Pin`, `PinsOf`, `Catalog.Pinouts`, `Catalog.Wire`, `Catalog.Item` answers `pinout`, the fixture helpers `pinTreeFS`, `flow16` and `queryTables` of A's and the existing tests). Files this plan creates: `internal/ecalc/query_pinout.go`, `internal/ecalc/query_pinout_test.go`, `internal/tools/ecalc_pinout_test.go`, `internal/agent/ecalc_pinout_test.go`. Files it edits: `internal/ecalc/{query,query_items,query_test,query_items_test}.go`, `internal/tools/{ecalc,ecalc_test,ecalc_items_test,audit_json_test}.go`, `internal/agent/{native_tools_ecalc,tool_args_ecalc,tool_role_policy,tool_categories,ecalc_tool_test,ecalc_policy_test}.go`, `internal/agent/tool_search_terms/infrastructure_b.yaml`, `prompts/tools_manuals/ecalc.md`, `documentation/manuals/{en,de}/{06-tools,22-internal-tools}.md`. `internal/agent/action_policy.go` needs no change (only `open` mutates; `TestECalcActionPolicyOnlyOpenMutates` gets the new operation).

### Contract deviations

1. **`found` is set only when `pin` is given** (`true` or `false`); a listing without `pin` carries no `found`. A `pin` that matches nothing answers `status: ok`, `found: false`, `pins: []`, the `variants` and a `note`; it is never an error. A `pin` longer than 24 characters finds nothing and is not repeated in the note.
2. **`pin` and `filter` combine** (both must match). `filter` matches number, name, function and notes in English and German (like `table`, which also reads German text cells), at most `MaxFilterLength` (128) characters, error `invalid_filter`.
3. **Extra fields beside the contract:** `variant_name` (the English name of the variant read), `next_offset` (where to continue, like `table`) and `note` (what was shortened, or why nothing was found). `variants` and `variant` are absent for an item without variants. `wire` is the English colour name of `pinstyles.yaml` (`white-green`), absent without a wire; `notes` of a pin absent when unset.
4. **`describe` of a pinout** answers `id kind category group name doc connector view pin_count counts variants[{id,name,counts}] notes source` and no pins. `pin_count` and `counts` (pins per type, types without a pin left out) are those of the first variant.
5. **New error codes** `not_a_pinout` (like `not_a_table`) and `unknown_variant` (the message lists the variant ids, or says that the item has none). The messages that listed "calculator, table or code" now say "calculator, table, code or pinout", and the pinout message of `invalid_operation` lists `pinout` between `table` and `decode`; the tests that pinned those texts and the test that pinned `pinout` as an invalid operation are updated.
6. **Fit order** (`ecalcPinout`): clip the notes of the pinout and the source, drop the notes of the pins, drop the notes of the pinout, list fewer pins (one step per pin, at least one stays), drop the source, and as the last resort for a budget of `ecalcMinBudget` and up list no pin (`advice`: name one with `pin`). A page of pins is never refused with `output_budget_exceeded`.
7. **Seam for tests:** `ExecuteECalc` now loads `ecalc.Default()` and calls the unexported `executeECalc(cfg, cat, req)`. Behaviour is unchanged; the only reason is that the bound test needs a catalog with fixture pinouts.
8. **Tests that pin the state of the shipped catalog were relaxed** so that they keep passing when Z adds the 47 items: the overview test in `query_test.go` and the search test in `ecalc_items_test.go` used to demand that the category `pinouts` is not listed; they now demand that it is listed exactly when the catalog has pinouts. The manual-example test runs a `pinout` or `describe` example only when its id exists in the shipped catalog (until Z adds the items it checks the example against the schema and logs that it did not run it); after Z adds `usb_a`, `rj45` and `raspberry_pi_40` the three examples really run.
9. **Schema budget:** measured 755 tokens before, 799 after (+44); the limit of 800 stays unchanged. To get there the descriptions of the operation enum, `id`, `limit`, `offset` and `filter` were kept as short hints.
10. **Search terms:** `ecalc` was at the limit of 12 phrases per language. Two phrases per language went (`RC time constant`, `filter cutoff frequency` and the German pair) for `connector pinout`, `USB connector pins`, `Steckerbelegung`, `Pinbelegung Stecker`; the discovery description of `ecalc` also names the pinouts.

### Exact API (for UP and Z)

```go
// internal/ecalc/query_pinout.go
const DefaultPinoutLimit, MaxPinoutLimit = 50, 50
type PinoutRequest struct{ Pin, Variant, Filter string; Offset, Limit int }
type PinAnswer struct{ Number, Name, Function, Type, Wire, Notes string } // json: number name function type wire? notes?
type PinoutResult struct { ID, Name, Group, Connector, View, Variant, VariantName string; Variants []string; Found *bool
    Pins []PinAnswer; Total, Offset, Returned int; Truncated bool; NextOffset int; Notes, Source, Note string }
func (r *PinoutResult) Keep(n int)
type PinoutVariantInfo struct{ ID, Name string; Counts map[string]int }
type PinoutDescription struct{ ID, Kind, Category, Group, Name, Doc, Connector, View string; PinCount int
    Counts map[string]int; Variants []PinoutVariantInfo; Notes, Source string }
func (c *Catalog) QueryPinout(id string, req PinoutRequest) (PinoutResult, error)
func (c *Catalog) DescribePinout(id string) (PinoutDescription, error)
const CodeNotAPinout, CodeUnknownVariant = "not_a_pinout", "unknown_variant"
// internal/tools: ECalcRequest gains Pin and Variant (Filter, Offset, Limit are shared with table).
```

Tool answer of `pinout` (one line of JSON): `status operation id name group connector view [variant variant_name variants] [found] pins[{number name function type [wire] [notes]}] total offset returned [truncated next_offset] [notes] source [note]`. `connector` is for example `D-sub connector, 2 rows, round contacts, 9 pins`, `DIP package, 8 pins`, `Board, main connector at the bottom, 40 pins`; `view` is one sentence such as `Rows as seen looking at the mating face of the male connector (pins).` (the English `views` caption of the drawn view, first letter lower case unless it starts with an acronym), `Package seen from above: notch at the top, pin 1 at the top left, numbers run counter-clockwise.`, `TO-92 seen from the front (flat side), leads pointing down, pins left to right.`, `Plug seen from the side, tip at the left, segments from tip to sleeve.`, `Board seen from the component side, portrait, main connector at the bottom.`

**GitNexus impact (before editing).** `ExecuteECalc`, `ecalcSchema`, `decodeECalcArgs`, `a2aDesktopWrite`, `ecalcDescribe` and `ecalcSearch` report risk UNKNOWN with no resolved callers (the index does not resolve them); `notFound` and `searchItems` resolve to unrelated symbols of other packages and `ItemCount` is not found. Confirmed by grep: `ExecuteECalc` is called by `internal/agent/ecalc_tool.go` (`dispatchECalc`) and by the tests of `internal/tools`; `ecalcSchema` by `native_tools_content.go`; `decodeECalcArgs` by `dispatchECalc` and the agent tests; `a2aDesktopWrite` by `roleToolRestriction` and `applyCatalogEntryPolicies`; `Catalog.notFound`, `searchItems`, `ItemCount` and `Overview` by the query API, `internal/tools/ecalc.go` and the server catalog endpoint. All edits are additive (a new operation, a new item kind, two new parameters); the existing behaviour changes only in the texts listed under deviation 5.

```go
package ecalc

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// The pinout queries run against fixture pinouts (a MapFS next to the real units, categories and pin styles), never
// against the real items: a large board-like item with repeated names and long texts, an item with two variants whose
// pins have wires and notes, and a small DIP without views.

// pinoutBoardFixture is a 40-pin board: GND on every fifth pin, long function texts and a note on every pin.
func pinoutBoardFixture() string {
	var left, right, pins strings.Builder
	for n := 1; n <= 40; n++ {
		name, typ := fmt.Sprintf("GPIO%d", n), "io"
		if n%5 == 0 {
			name, typ = "GND", "ground"
		}
		list := &left
		if n > 20 {
			list = &right
		}
		if list.Len() > 0 {
			list.WriteString(", ")
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(list, `"%d"`, n)
		fmt.Fprintf(&pins, `    - {number: "%d", name: %s, function: {en: "General purpose line %d of the header with a deliberately long description so that the page is large", de: "Allzweckleitung %d des Headers"}, type: %s, notes: {en: "Note for pin %d: a deliberately long hint that the bound test has to shorten before it drops rows.", de: "Hinweis %d"}}`+"\n", n, name, n, n, typ, n, n)
	}
	return strings.ReplaceAll(`- id: t_board
  kind: pinout
  category: pinouts
  group: boards
  name: NAME16
  doc: {en: "A large test board. Second sentence.", de: "Ein grosses Testboard."}
  notes: {en: "Board notes: 3V3 logic only.", de: "Boardhinweise: nur 3V3."}
  tags: [board, testboard]
  source: "Fixture datasheet"
  shape:
    type: board
    left: [`+left.String()+`]
    right: [`+right.String()+`]
    connector: bottom
  pins:
`+pins.String(), "NAME16", flow16("Test board"))
}

// pinoutVariantsFixture is a two-variant RJ45-like item with wires and notes.
var pinoutVariantsFixture = strings.ReplaceAll(`- id: t_rj
  kind: pinout
  category: pinouts
  group: data
  name: NAME16
  doc: {en: "Two wiring variants.", de: "Zwei Belegungen."}
  notes: {en: "Pair 1 is the centre pair.", de: "Paar 1 ist das mittlere."}
  tags: [rj, ethernet]
  source: "Fixture standard"
  views:
    plug: {en: "Male connector (pins)", de: "Stecker (Stifte)"}
    socket: {en: "Female connector (sockets)", de: "Buchse"}
  shape:
    type: rows
    outline: rj45
    contact: blade
    drawn: socket
    rows:
      - {pins: ["1", "2", "3", "4"]}
  variants:
    - id: t568a
      name: {en: "T568A", de: "T568A"}
      pins:
        - {number: "1", name: "TX+", function: {en: "Transmit +", de: "Senden +"}, type: data, wire: white_green}
        - {number: "2", name: "TX-", function: {en: "Transmit -", de: "Senden -"}, type: data, wire: green, notes: {en: "Twisted with pin 1.", de: "Verdrillt mit Pin 1."}}
        - {number: "3", name: "RX+", function: {en: "Receive +", de: "Empfangen +"}, type: data, wire: white_orange}
        - {number: "4", name: "GND", function: {en: "Ground", de: "Masse"}, type: ground}
    - id: t568b
      name: {en: "T568B", de: "T568B"}
      pins:
        - {number: "1", name: "TX+", function: {en: "Transmit +", de: "Senden +"}, type: data, wire: white_orange}
        - {number: "2", name: "TX-", function: {en: "Transmit -", de: "Senden -"}, type: data, wire: orange}
        - {number: "3", name: "RX+", function: {en: "Receive +", de: "Empfangen +"}, type: data, wire: white_green}
        - {number: "4", name: "GND", function: {en: "Ground", de: "Masse"}, type: ground}
`, "NAME16", flow16("Test jack"))

var pinoutDipFixture = strings.ReplaceAll(`- id: t_dip
  kind: pinout
  category: pinouts
  group: ics
  name: NAME16
  tags: [dip, timer]
  source: "Fixture datasheet"
  shape:
    type: dip
    pins: 4
  pins:
    - {number: "1", name: GND, function: {en: "Ground", de: "Masse"}, type: ground}
    - {number: "2", name: IN, function: {en: "Input", de: "Eingang"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "3", name: OUT, function: {en: "Output", de: "Ausgang"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "4", name: VCC, function: {en: "Supply", de: "Versorgung"}, type: power}
`, "NAME16", flow16("Test timer"))

func pinoutQueryCatalog(t *testing.T) *Catalog {
	t.Helper()
	cat, err := Load(pinTreeFS(t, map[string]string{
		"pinouts/a_board.yaml": pinoutBoardFixture(), "pinouts/b_rj.yaml": pinoutVariantsFixture, "pinouts/c_dip.yaml": pinoutDipFixture,
		"tables/amp.yaml": queryTables,
	}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Load: %v", err)
	}
	return cat
}

func pinNumbers(pins []PinAnswer) string {
	out := make([]string, len(pins))
	for i, p := range pins {
		out[i] = p.Number
	}
	return strings.Join(out, ",")
}

func TestQueryPinoutListsAPageOfPins(t *testing.T) {
	cat := pinoutQueryCatalog(t)
	res, err := cat.QueryPinout(" T_BOARD ", PinoutRequest{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if res.ID != "t_board" || res.Name != "Test board" || res.Group != "boards" || res.Total != 40 || res.Returned != 40 || res.Truncated || res.NextOffset != 0 ||
		res.Variant != "" || len(res.Variants) != 0 || res.Found != nil || res.Source != "Fixture datasheet" || res.Notes != "Board notes: 3V3 logic only." {
		t.Fatalf("result = %+v", res)
	}
	if res.Connector != "Board, main connector at the bottom, 40 pins" || res.View != "Board seen from the component side, portrait, main connector at the bottom." {
		t.Errorf("connector %q, view %q", res.Connector, res.View)
	}
	if p := res.Pins[4]; p.Number != "5" || p.Name != "GND" || p.Type != "ground" || p.Function == "" || !strings.HasPrefix(p.Notes, "Note for pin 5") || p.Wire != "" {
		t.Errorf("pin 5 = %+v", p)
	}

	// Paging: offset and limit; the continuation is said.
	res, err = cat.QueryPinout("t_board", PinoutRequest{Offset: 10, Limit: 5})
	if err != nil || pinNumbers(res.Pins) != "11,12,13,14,15" || res.Total != 40 || res.Offset != 10 || res.Returned != 5 || !res.Truncated || res.NextOffset != 15 {
		t.Fatalf("page = %v %+v", err, res)
	}
	// The limit is 1 to 50 (default 50): zero and too large values mean 50, an offset past the end lists nothing.
	for _, limit := range []int{0, -3, 51, 1000} {
		if res, _ = cat.QueryPinout("t_board", PinoutRequest{Limit: limit}); res.Returned != 40 {
			t.Errorf("limit %d returned %d pins", limit, res.Returned)
		}
	}
	if res, _ = cat.QueryPinout("t_board", PinoutRequest{Offset: 99}); res.Returned != 0 || res.Total != 40 || res.Truncated || len(res.Pins) != 0 || res.Pins == nil {
		t.Errorf("offset past the end = %+v", res)
	}
	// The pins are English and a pinout page is always the same JSON shape: pins is a list even when empty.
	raw, _ := json.Marshal(res)
	if !strings.Contains(string(raw), `"pins":[]`) {
		t.Errorf("an empty page must carry pins: %s", raw)
	}
}

func TestQueryPinoutPinMatchesNumbersAndNamesExactly(t *testing.T) {
	cat := pinoutQueryCatalog(t)
	// Several pins share a name: all of them come back, in pin order.
	res, err := cat.QueryPinout("t_board", PinoutRequest{Pin: "gnd"})
	if err != nil || pinNumbers(res.Pins) != "5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40" || res.Total != 8 || res.Found == nil || !*res.Found {
		t.Fatalf("GND = %v %+v", err, res)
	}
	// A number matches the number only, and the name exactly: GPIO1 is not GPIO11.
	for pin, want := range map[string]string{"7": "7", " 12 ": "12", "GPIO1": "1", "gpio11": "11", "GPIO": ""} {
		res, err := cat.QueryPinout("t_board", PinoutRequest{Pin: pin})
		if err != nil || pinNumbers(res.Pins) != want {
			t.Errorf("pin %q = %v %s, want %q", pin, err, pinNumbers(res.Pins), want)
		}
	}
	// A pin that matches nothing is an answer: found false, the variants (none here) and a note, not an error.
	res, err = cat.QueryPinout("t_board", PinoutRequest{Pin: "SDA"})
	if err != nil || res.Found == nil || *res.Found || res.Total != 0 || res.Returned != 0 || res.Pins == nil || len(res.Pins) != 0 || !strings.Contains(res.Note, `"SDA"`) {
		t.Fatalf("SDA = %v %+v", err, res)
	}
	raw, _ := json.Marshal(res)
	if !strings.Contains(string(raw), `"found":false`) {
		t.Errorf("found:false must be in the JSON: %s", raw)
	}
	// pin and filter both have to match; an overlong pin is found:false without echoing it.
	if res, _ = cat.QueryPinout("t_board", PinoutRequest{Pin: "GND", Filter: "pin 25"}); pinNumbers(res.Pins) != "25" {
		t.Errorf("GND + filter = %s", pinNumbers(res.Pins))
	}
	res, err = cat.QueryPinout("t_board", PinoutRequest{Pin: strings.Repeat("x", 5000)})
	if err != nil || *res.Found || strings.Contains(res.Note, "xxxx") || len(res.Note) > 300 {
		t.Errorf("long pin = %v %q", err, res.Note)
	}
}

func TestQueryPinoutVariants(t *testing.T) {
	cat := pinoutQueryCatalog(t)
	// Without variant the first one is used; the variants are listed.
	res, err := cat.QueryPinout("t_rj", PinoutRequest{})
	if err != nil || res.Variant != "t568a" || res.VariantName != "T568A" || !slices.Equal(res.Variants, []string{"t568a", "t568b"}) || res.Total != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("default variant = %v %+v", err, res)
	}
	if p := res.Pins[0]; p.Wire != "white-green" || p.Name != "TX+" || p.Type != "data" {
		t.Errorf("pin 1 = %+v (the wire is the English colour name)", p)
	}
	if res.Pins[1].Wire != "green" || res.Pins[1].Notes != "Twisted with pin 1." || res.Pins[3].Wire != "" {
		t.Errorf("pins = %+v", res.Pins)
	}
	res, err = cat.QueryPinout("t_rj", PinoutRequest{Variant: " T568B ", Pin: "1"})
	if err != nil || res.Variant != "t568b" || res.Pins[0].Wire != "white-orange" {
		t.Fatalf("t568b = %v %+v", err, res)
	}
	// An unknown variant is an error that lists the ids; so is a variant of an item that has none.
	_, err = cat.QueryPinout("t_rj", PinoutRequest{Variant: "t568c"})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownVariant, `no variant "t568c"`, "t568a, t568b")
	_, err = cat.QueryPinout("t_dip", PinoutRequest{Variant: "a"})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownVariant, "t_dip has no variants")
	// A pin that is in no variant answers found:false and still lists the variants.
	res, err = cat.QueryPinout("t_rj", PinoutRequest{Pin: "SDA"})
	if err != nil || res.Found == nil || *res.Found || !slices.Equal(res.Variants, []string{"t568a", "t568b"}) || !strings.Contains(res.Note, "t568a, t568b") {
		t.Errorf("SDA in a variant item = %v %+v", err, res)
	}
}

func TestQueryPinoutFilterAndErrors(t *testing.T) {
	cat := pinoutQueryCatalog(t)
	// The filter looks at number, name, function and notes, in English and German, ignoring case.
	for filter, want := range map[string]string{"gpio3": "3,31,32,33,34,36,37,38,39", "allzweckleitung 7 ": "7", "HINWEIS 40": "40", "Note for pin 1:": "1"} {
		res, err := cat.QueryPinout("t_board", PinoutRequest{Filter: filter})
		if err != nil || pinNumbers(res.Pins) != want {
			t.Errorf("filter %q = %v %s, want %s", filter, err, pinNumbers(res.Pins), want)
		}
	}
	res, _ := cat.QueryPinout("t_board", PinoutRequest{Filter: "zzz"})
	if res.Total != 0 || res.Note != "No pin matches the filter." || res.Found != nil {
		t.Errorf("filter without a match = %+v", res)
	}
	_, err := cat.QueryPinout("t_board", PinoutRequest{Filter: strings.Repeat("a", MaxFilterLength+1)})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeInvalidFilter, "at most 128 characters")

	// Ids: case-insensitive, the id of another kind says what it is, an unknown id suggests the pinouts only.
	_, err = cat.QueryPinout("t_amp", PinoutRequest{})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeNotAPinout, "t_amp is a table, not a pinout")
	_, err = cat.QueryPinout("board", PinoutRequest{})
	qe := wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownID, `unknown pinout "board"`, "did you mean")
	for _, id := range suggestedIDs(qe.Message) {
		if kind, _ := cat.Item(id); kind != "pinout" {
			t.Errorf("only pinouts are suggested, got the %s %s", kind, id)
		}
	}
	_, err = cat.QueryPinout("", PinoutRequest{})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownID, "id is required", "pinout id")
	_, err = cat.QueryPinout(strings.Repeat("x", MaxIDLength+1), PinoutRequest{})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownID, "longer than 256 characters")
	// The other kinds say what a pinout is.
	_, err = cat.DescribeTable("t_board")
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeNotATable, "t_board is a pinout, not a table", "pinout reads its pins")
	_, err = cat.Describe("t_board")
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeNotACalculator, "t_board is a pinout")
	_, err = cat.DescribeCode("t_board")
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeNotACode, "t_board is a pinout")
}

		d.Source != "Fixture standard" || d.PinCount != 4 || d.Counts["data"] != 3 || d.Counts["ground"] != 1 || len(d.Counts) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("description = %+v", d)

		t.Errorf("connector %q, view %q", d.Connector, d.View)

		t.Errorf("dip = %+v", dip)

	if _, err := cat.DescribePinout("t_amp"); AsQueryError(err) == nil || AsQueryError(err).Code != CodeNotAPinout {
		t.Errorf("describe of a table = %v", err)
	}
}

// Every outline of the loader has an English name, and the view sentence of every shape type is one sentence.
func TestPinoutTextsCoverEveryOutlineAndShape(t *testing.T) {
	for _, o := range PinoutOutlines {
		if pinoutOutlineNames[o] == "" {
			t.Errorf("outline %s has no English name", o)
		}
	}
	if len(pinoutOutlineNames) != len(PinoutOutlines) {
		t.Errorf("%d names for %d outlines", len(pinoutOutlineNames), len(PinoutOutlines))
	}
	views := map[string]Text{"plug": {"en": "Male connector (pins)"}, "socket": {"en": "Female connector (sockets)"}}
	for _, c := range []struct {
		shape PinoutShape
		view  string
	}{
		{PinoutShape{Type: "rows", Drawn: "plug"}, "Rows as seen looking at the mating face of the male connector (pins)."},
		{PinoutShape{Type: "rows", Drawn: "socket"}, "Rows as seen looking at the mating face of the female connector (sockets)."},
		{PinoutShape{Type: "circular", Drawn: "plug"}, "Pin positions as seen looking at the mating face of the male connector (pins)."},
		{PinoutShape{Type: "to", Package: "to92"}, "TO-92 seen from the front (flat side), leads pointing down, pins left to right."},
		{PinoutShape{Type: "to", Package: "to220"}, "TO-220 seen from the front (label side), leads pointing down, pins left to right."},
		{PinoutShape{Type: "jack"}, "Plug seen from the side, tip at the left, segments from tip to sleeve."},
		{PinoutShape{Type: "board", Connector: "none"}, "Board seen from the component side, portrait, without a main connector."},
		{PinoutShape{Type: "board", Connector: "top"}, "Board seen from the component side, portrait, main connector at the top."},
	} {
		if got := pinoutView(&Pinout{Shape: c.shape, Views: views}); got != c.view {
			t.Errorf("%s/%s view = %q, want %q", c.shape.Type, c.shape.Drawn, got, c.view)
		}
	}
	// A caption with a leading acronym keeps its capitals.
	if got := pinoutView(&Pinout{Shape: PinoutShape{Type: "rows", Drawn: "plug"}, Views: map[string]Text{"plug": {"en": "USB plug."}}}); got != "Rows as seen looking at the mating face of the USB plug." {
		t.Errorf("acronym caption = %q", got)
	}
}
```

```go
package ecalc

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"unicode"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// The query API of the pinouts for the agent tool: DescribePinout describes a pinout item without its pins, QueryPinout
// lists the pins of one variant (all of them, those with a number or name, or those that match a filter), one page at a
// time. Output texts are English; the structs carry JSON tags because the tool sends them as they are.

const (
	// DefaultPinoutLimit and MaxPinoutLimit bound the number of pins of one QueryPinout answer.
	DefaultPinoutLimit = 50
	MaxPinoutLimit     = 50
	// maxPinQueryLength is the longest pin number or name a request can match (the loader allows 24 characters for a
	// name); a longer text finds nothing and is not repeated in the answer.
	maxPinQueryLength = 24
)

// pinoutOutlineNames are the English names of the outlines of a "rows" shape (the keys are PinoutOutlines).
var pinoutOutlineNames = map[string]string{
	"displayport": "DisplayPort", "dsub": "D-sub", "hdmi_a": "HDMI type A", "jst": "JST", "minifit": "Mini-Fit", "molex": "Molex",
	"obd2": "OBD-II", "rect": "Rectangular", "rj45": "RJ45", "sata_data": "SATA data", "sata_power": "SATA power",
	"usb_a": "USB-A", "usb_b": "USB-B", "usb_c": "USB-C", "usb_micro_b": "USB micro-B", "usb_mini_b": "USB mini-B",
}

func plural(n int, one, many string) string {
	if n == 1 {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%d %s", n, one)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%d %s", n, many)
}

// pinoutConnector is the short English text for the shape of a pinout: what it is and how many pins it has.
func pinoutConnector(p *Pinout, pinCount int) string {
	s := p.Shape
	pins := plural(pinCount, "pin", "pins")
	switch s.Type {
	case "rows":
		name := pinoutOutlineNames[s.Outline]
		if name == "" {
			name = s.Outline
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s connector, %s, %s contacts, %s", name, plural(len(s.Rows), "row", "rows"), s.Contact, pins)
	case "dip":
		return "DIP package, " + pins
	case "to":
		return strings.ToUpper(s.Package[:2]) + "-" + s.Package[2:] + " package, " + pins
	case "circular":
		return fmt.Sprintf("Circular connector, %s contacts, %s", s.Contact, pins)
	case "jack":
		return "Audio jack plug, " + plural(len(s.Segments), "segment", "segments")
	case "board":
		if s.Connector == "none" {
			return "Board without a main connector, " + pins
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("Board, main connector at the %s, %s", s.Connector, pins)
	}
	return pins
}

// lowerFirst makes the first letter of a caption lower case unless the caption starts with an acronym (USB, HDMI).
func lowerFirst(s string) string {
	r := []rune(s)
	if len(r) == 0 || !unicode.IsUpper(r[0]) || (len(r) > 1 && unicode.IsUpper(r[1])) {
		return s
	}
	r[0] = unicode.ToLower(r[0])
	return string(r)
}

// pinoutView is one English sentence that says what the drawing of the pinout shows, derived from the shape and the
// English caption of the view that is drawn.
func pinoutView(p *Pinout) string {
	s := p.Shape
	face := func(what string) string {
		caption := strings.TrimRight(strings.TrimSpace(p.Views[s.Drawn].in("en")), ".")
		if caption == "" {
			caption = map[string]string{"plug": "male connector (plug)", "socket": "female connector (socket)"}[s.Drawn]
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s as seen looking at the mating face of the %s.", what, lowerFirst(caption))
	}
	switch s.Type {
	case "rows":
		return face("Rows")
	case "circular":
		return face("Pin positions")
	case "dip":
		return "Package seen from above: notch at the top, pin 1 at the top left, numbers run counter-clockwise."
	case "to":
		side := "flat side"
		if s.Package == "to220" {
			side = "label side"
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s seen from the front (%s), leads pointing down, pins left to right.", strings.ToUpper(s.Package[:2])+"-"+s.Package[2:], side)
	case "jack":
		return "Plug seen from the side, tip at the left, segments from tip to sleeve."
	case "board":
		if s.Connector == "none" {
			return "Board seen from the component side, portrait, without a main connector."
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("Board seen from the component side, portrait, main connector at the %s.", s.Connector)
	}
	return ""
}

// typeCounts counts the pins of every type (types without a pin are left out).
func typeCounts(pins []Pin) map[string]int {
	counts := map[string]int{}
	for _, p := range pins {
		counts[p.Type]++
	}
	return counts
}

// lookupPinout finds a pinout by id (case-insensitive), like lookupTable.
func (c *Catalog) lookupPinout(id string) (*Pinout, error) {
	if qe := idTooLong(id, "pinout"); qe != nil {
		return nil, qe
	}
	key := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(id))
	if key == "" {
		return nil, queryErr(CodeUnknownID, "id is required; use search to find a pinout id")
	}
	if p := c.Pinout(key); p != nil {
		return p, nil
	}
	return nil, c.notFound(id, key, "pinout")
}

// ---- describe -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// PinoutVariantInfo is one variant in a PinoutDescription: its id, its name and the number of pins of every type.
type PinoutVariantInfo struct {
	ID     string         `json:"id"`
	Name   string         `json:"name"`
	Counts map[string]int `json:"counts"`
}

// PinoutDescription is what DescribePinout returns: everything but the pins. Connector says what the shape is, View what
// the drawing shows. PinCount and Counts (pins per type) are those of the first variant for an item with variants.
type PinoutDescription struct {
	ID        string              `json:"id"`
	Kind      string              `json:"kind"`
	Category  string              `json:"category"`
	Group     string              `json:"group"`
	Name      string              `json:"name"`
	Doc       string              `json:"doc,omitempty"`
	Connector string              `json:"connector"`
	View      string              `json:"view"`
	PinCount  int                 `json:"pin_count"`
	Counts    map[string]int      `json:"counts"`
	Variants  []PinoutVariantInfo `json:"variants,omitempty"`
	Notes     string              `json:"notes,omitempty"`
	Source    string              `json:"source"`
}

// DescribePinout returns what a pinout is: its group, connector, view, number of pins, variants, the pin counts per type,
// the notes and the source. The pins themselves are read with QueryPinout.
func (c *Catalog) DescribePinout(id string) (PinoutDescription, error) {
	p, err := c.lookupPinout(id)
	if err != nil {
		return PinoutDescription{}, err
	}
	pins, _, _ := p.PinsOf("")
	d := PinoutDescription{
		ID: p.ID, Kind: "pinout", Category: p.Category, Group: p.Group, Name: p.Name.in("en"), Doc: p.Doc.in("en"),
		Connector: pinoutConnector(p, len(pins)), View: pinoutView(p), PinCount: len(pins), Counts: typeCounts(pins),
		Notes: p.Notes.in("en"), Source: p.Source,
	}
	for _, v := range p.Variants {
		d.Variants = append(d.Variants, PinoutVariantInfo{ID: v.ID, Name: v.Name.in("en"), Counts: typeCounts(v.Pins)})
	}
	return d, nil
}

// ---- pins -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// PinoutRequest is the input of QueryPinout. Pin keeps the pins whose number or name equals it (case-insensitive, exact:
// several pins can share a name such as GND). Variant is a variant id ("" = the first). Filter keeps the pins with a
// number, name, function or note that contains the text (English and German, case-insensitive); with Pin both have to
// match. Offset and Limit page through the kept pins (Limit 0 = DefaultPinoutLimit, at most MaxPinoutLimit).
type PinoutRequest struct {
	Pin     string
	Variant string
	Filter  string
	Offset  int
	Limit   int
}

// PinAnswer is one pin of a QueryPinout answer. Wire is the English name of the standard wire colour, empty when the
// pin has none.
type PinAnswer struct {
	Number   string `json:"number"`
	Name     string `json:"name"`
	Function string `json:"function"`
	Type     string `json:"type"`
	Wire     string `json:"wire,omitempty"`
	Notes    string `json:"notes,omitempty"`
}

// PinoutResult is what QueryPinout returns. Variant (with VariantName) is the variant that was read and Variants the ids
// of all variants (both absent for an item without variants). Found is set when a Pin was asked for: false means no
// pin of that variant has the number or name, which is an answer and not an error. Total counts the pins that match,
// Truncated means that more of them exist than are listed and NextOffset is where to continue.
type PinoutResult struct {
	ID          string      `json:"id"`
	Name        string      `json:"name"`
	Group       string      `json:"group"`
	Connector   string      `json:"connector"`
	View        string      `json:"view"`
	Variant     string      `json:"variant,omitempty"`
	VariantName string      `json:"variant_name,omitempty"`
	Variants    []string    `json:"variants,omitempty"`
	Found       *bool       `json:"found,omitempty"`
	Pins        []PinAnswer `json:"pins"`
	Total       int         `json:"total"`
	Offset      int         `json:"offset"`
	Returned    int         `json:"returned"`
	Truncated   bool        `json:"truncated,omitempty"`
	NextOffset  int         `json:"next_offset,omitempty"`
	Notes       string      `json:"notes,omitempty"`
	Source      string      `json:"source"`
	Note        string      `json:"note,omitempty"`
}

// Keep shortens the listed pins to the first n (the tool does that to fit its output budget) and keeps Returned,
// Truncated and NextOffset consistent.
func (r *PinoutResult) Keep(n int) {
	if n < 0 || n >= len(r.Pins) {
		return
	}
	r.Pins = r.Pins[:n]
	r.Returned = n
	r.Truncated = true
	r.NextOffset = r.Offset + n
}

func pinMatchesFilter(p Pin, needle string) bool {
	for _, s := range []string{p.Number, p.Name, p.Function.in("en"), p.Function.in("de"), p.Notes.in("en"), p.Notes.in("de")} {
		if s != "" && strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(s), needle) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// QueryPinout reads the pins of a pinout: those that match Pin and Filter, one page of them.
func (c *Catalog) QueryPinout(id string, req PinoutRequest) (PinoutResult, error) {
	p, err := c.lookupPinout(id)
	if err != nil {
		return PinoutResult{}, err
	}
	filter := strings.TrimSpace(req.Filter)
	if utf8.RuneCountInString(filter) > MaxFilterLength {
		return PinoutResult{}, queryErr(CodeInvalidFilter, "filter must be at most %d characters; give a word or a number that occurs in a pin", MaxFilterLength)
	}
	variant := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(req.Variant))
	pins, used, ok := p.PinsOf(variant)
	if !ok {
		if len(p.Variants) == 0 {
			return PinoutResult{}, queryErr(CodeUnknownVariant, "pinout %s has no variants; leave variant out", p.ID)
		}
		return PinoutResult{}, queryErr(CodeUnknownVariant, "pinout %s has no variant %q; variants: %s", p.ID, clipText(req.Variant, MaxIDLength), strings.Join(variantIDs(p), ", "))
	}
	res := PinoutResult{
		ID: p.ID, Name: p.Name.in("en"), Group: p.Group, Connector: pinoutConnector(p, len(pins)), View: pinoutView(p),
		Variant: used, Variants: variantIDs(p), Pins: []PinAnswer{}, Offset: max(req.Offset, 0), Notes: p.Notes.in("en"), Source: p.Source,
	}
	for _, v := range p.Variants {
		if v.ID == used {
			res.VariantName = v.Name.in("en")
		}
	}

	pin := strings.TrimSpace(req.Pin)
	needle := strings.ToLower(filter)
	var matches []Pin
	if utf8.RuneCountInString(pin) <= maxPinQueryLength {
		for _, pn := range pins {
			if pin != "" && !strings.EqualFold(pn.Number, pin) && !strings.EqualFold(pn.Name, pin) {
				continue
			}
			if needle != "" && !pinMatchesFilter(pn, needle) {
				continue
			}
			matches = append(matches, pn)
		}
	}
	res.Total = len(matches)
	if pin != "" {
		found := res.Total > 0
		res.Found = &found
		if !found {
			what := "No pin has that number or name"
			if utf8.RuneCountInString(pin) <= maxPinQueryLength {
				what = fmt.Sprintf("No pin has the number or name %q", pin)
			}
			if needle != "" {
				what += " that also matches the filter"
			}
			res.Note = what + fmt.Sprintf(" in %s", pinoutScope(p, used)) + "."
			if len(p.Variants) > 1 {
				res.Note += " Variants: " + strings.Join(variantIDs(p), ", ") + "."
			}
			res.Note += " Leave pin out to list the pins."
		}
	} else if res.Total == 0 {
		res.Note = "No pin matches the filter."
	}

	limit := req.Limit
	if limit < 1 {
		limit = DefaultPinoutLimit
	}
	limit = min(limit, MaxPinoutLimit)
	page := matches[min(res.Offset, len(matches)):]
	if len(page) > limit {
		page = page[:limit]
	}
	for _, pn := range page {
		out := PinAnswer{Number: pn.Number, Name: pn.Name, Function: pn.Function.in("en"), Type: pn.Type, Notes: pn.Notes.in("en")}
		if pn.Wire != "" {
			out.Wire = pn.Wire
			if w := c.Wire(pn.Wire); w != nil {
				out.Wire = w.Name.in("en")
			}
		}
		res.Pins = append(res.Pins, out)
	}
	res.Returned = len(page)
	if end := min(res.Offset, len(matches)) + len(page); end < len(matches) {
		res.Truncated, res.NextOffset = true, end
	}
	return res, nil
}

func variantIDs(p *Pinout) []string {
	var ids []string
	for _, v := range p.Variants {
		ids = append(ids, v.ID)
	}
	return ids
}

// pinoutScope names where a pin was looked for: the pinout, with its variant when it has any.
func pinoutScope(p *Pinout, variant string) string {
	if variant == "" {
		return p.ID
	}
	return p.ID + " variant " + variant
}

// clipText cuts s to at most n characters (a trailing ellipsis counts), for texts of a request that an error repeats.
func clipText(s string, n int) string {
	s = strings.Join(strings.Fields(strings.ToValidUTF8(s, "")), " ")
	if r := []rune(s); len(r) > n {
		return strings.TrimSpace(string(r[:n-1])) + "…"
	}
	return s
}
```

```go
// The pinout operation of the ecalc tool is tested on a fixture catalog (a MapFS next to the real units, categories and
// pin styles), never on the real pinouts: a 40-pin board with long texts and a note on every pin, an item with two
// variants whose pins have wires and notes, and a small DIP without views.

func ecalcPinoutName(v string) string {
	parts := make([]string, len(ecalc.Locales))
	for i, l := range ecalc.Locales {
		parts[i] = l + `: "` + v + `"`
	}
	return "{" + strings.Join(parts, ", ") + "}"
}

func ecalcFixtureBoard() string {
	var left, right, pins strings.Builder
	for n := 1; n <= 40; n++ {
		name, typ := fmt.Sprintf("GPIO%d", n), "io"
		if n%5 == 0 {
			name, typ = "GND", "ground"
		}
		list := &left
		if n > 20 {
			list = &right
		}
		if list.Len() > 0 {
			list.WriteString(", ")
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(list, `"%d"`, n)
		fmt.Fprintf(&pins, `    - {number: "%d", name: %s, function: {en: "General purpose line %d of the header, described at length so that a page of fifty pins is large", de: "Allzweckleitung %d"}, type: %s, notes: {en: "Note for pin %d: a long hint about voltage levels, pull resistors and alternate functions of the pin.", de: "Hinweis %d"}}`+"\n", n, name, n, n, typ, n, n)
	}
	return `- id: t_board
  kind: pinout
  category: pinouts
  group: boards
  name: ` + ecalcPinoutName("Test board") + `
  doc: {en: "A large test board. Second sentence.", de: "Ein grosses Testboard."}
  notes: {en: "Board notes: 3V3 logic only. ` + strings.Repeat("A long remark about the board. ", 20) + `", de: "Boardhinweise."}
  tags: [board, testboard]
  source: "Fixture datasheet ` + strings.Repeat("with a very long title ", 20) + `"
  shape:
    type: board
    left: [` + left.String() + `]
    right: [` + right.String() + `]
    connector: bottom
  pins:
` + pins.String()
}

  tags: [rj, ethernet]

// ecalcPinoutCatalog loads the fixture pinouts with the real units, categories and pin styles.
func ecalcPinoutCatalog(t *testing.T) *ecalc.Catalog {
	t.Helper()
	fsys := fstest.MapFS{}
	for _, name := range []string{"units.yaml", "categories.yaml", "pinstyles.yaml"} {
		data, err := os.ReadFile("../ecalc/catalog/" + name)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		fsys[name] = &fstest.MapFile{Data: data}
	}
	fsys["pinouts/a_board.yaml"] = &fstest.MapFile{Data: []byte(ecalcFixtureBoard())}
	fsys["pinouts/b_rj.yaml"] = &fstest.MapFile{Data: []byte(strings.Replace(ecalcFixtureJack, "NAME", ecalcPinoutName("Test jack"), 1))}
	fsys["pinouts/c_dip.yaml"] = &fstest.MapFile{Data: []byte(strings.Replace(ecalcFixtureDip, "NAME", ecalcPinoutName("Test timer"), 1))}
	cat, err := ecalc.Load(fsys)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("fixture catalog: %v", err)
	}
	return cat
}

func ecalcRunOn(t *testing.T, cat *ecalc.Catalog, req ECalcRequest) (map[string]any, VirtualDesktopExecution) {
	t.Helper()
	exec := executeECalc(ecalcDesktopConfig(), cat, req)
	return ecalcDecode(t, exec), exec
}

func pinNumberList(out map[string]any) []string {
	var numbers []string
	pins, _ := out["pins"].([]any)
	for _, p := range pins {
		numbers = append(numbers, p.(map[string]any)["number"].(string))
	}
	return numbers
}

func TestECalcPinoutAnswersPinsVariantsAndNotFound(t *testing.T) {
	cat := ecalcPinoutCatalog(t)

	// Variants: the first is the default, wires are English colour names, the variant ids are listed.
	out, exec := ecalcRunOn(t, cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "pinout", ID: "T_RJ"})
	pins, _ := out["pins"].([]any)
	if out["status"] != "ok" || out["operation"] != "pinout" || out["id"] != "t_rj" || out["name"] != "Test jack" || out["group"] != "data" || out["variant"] != "t568a" ||
		!slices.Equal(anyStrings(out["variants"]), []string{"t568a", "t568b"}) || out["total"] != float64(4) || out["returned"] != float64(4) || len(pins) != 4 ||
		out["connector"] != "RJ45 connector, 1 row, blade contacts, 4 pins" || out["view"] != "Rows as seen looking at the mating face of the female connector (sockets)." ||
		out["notes"] != "Pair 1 is the centre pair." || out["source"] != "Fixture standard" || exec.Event != nil {
		t.Fatalf("output = %s", exec.Output)
	}
	if first := pins[0].(map[string]any); first["wire"] != "white-green" || first["name"] != "TX+" || first["type"] != "data" || first["function"] != "Transmit +" {
		t.Errorf("pin 1 = %v", first)
	}
	out, _ = ecalcRunOn(t, cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "pinout", ID: "t_rj", Variant: "t568b", Pin: "tx+"})
	if numbers := pinNumberList(out); !slices.Equal(numbers, []string{"1"}) || out["variant"] != "t568b" || out["found"] != true || out["pins"].([]any)[0].(map[string]any)["wire"] != "white-orange" {
		t.Errorf("t568b pin tx+ = %v", out)
	}

	// Several pins share a name: all of them are returned.
	out, _ = ecalcRunOn(t, cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "pinout", ID: "t_board", Pin: "gnd"})
	if numbers := pinNumberList(out); !slices.Equal(numbers, []string{"5", "10", "15", "20", "25", "30", "35", "40"}) || out["found"] != true || out["total"] != float64(8) {
		t.Errorf("GND = %v", out)
	}

	// A pin that matches nothing is found:false with the variants, not an error.
	out, _ = ecalcRunOn(t, cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "pinout", ID: "t_rj", Pin: "SDA"})
	if out["status"] != "ok" || out["found"] != false || out["code"] != nil || out["total"] != float64(0) || !slices.Equal(anyStrings(out["variants"]), []string{"t568a", "t568b"}) {
		t.Errorf("SDA = %v", out)
	}
	if pins, ok := out["pins"].([]any); !ok || len(pins) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("found:false carries an empty pins list: %v", out["pins"])
	}

	// An unknown variant is an error that lists the ids; filter and paging work.
	out, _ = ecalcRunOn(t, cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "pinout", ID: "t_rj", Variant: "t568c"})
	if out["status"] != "error" || out["code"] != "unknown_variant" || !strings.Contains(out["message"].(string), "t568a, t568b") {
		t.Errorf("unknown variant = %v", out)
	}
	out, _ = ecalcRunOn(t, cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "pinout", ID: "t_board", Filter: "allzweckleitung 3", Offset: 1, Limit: 2})
	if numbers := pinNumberList(out); !slices.Equal(numbers, []string{"30", "31"}) || out["total"] != float64(11) || out["truncated"] != true || out["next_offset"] != float64(3) {
		t.Errorf("filtered page = %v", out)
	}
	// The id of a table says what it is (the fixture catalog has no tables, the shipped one does).
	if out := ecalcDecode(t, ExecuteECalc(nil, ECalcRequest{Operation: "pinout", ID: "awg"})); out["code"] != "not_a_pinout" || !strings.Contains(out["message"].(string), "awg is a table, not a pinout") {
		t.Errorf("pinout on a table = %v", out)
	}
	for _, c := range []struct {
		req  ECalcRequest
		code string
	}{
		{ECalcRequest{Operation: "pinout"}, "unknown_id"},
		{ECalcRequest{Operation: "pinout", ID: "t_rjj"}, "unknown_id"},
		{ECalcRequest{Operation: "pinout", ID: "t_dip", Variant: "a"}, "unknown_variant"},
		{ECalcRequest{Operation: "pinout", ID: "t_dip", Filter: strings.Repeat("x", 129)}, "invalid_filter"},
	} {
		if out, _ := ecalcRunOn(t, cat, c.req); out["status"] != "error" || out["code"] != c.code {
			t.Errorf("%+v = %v, want code %s", c.req, out, c.code)
		}
	}
}

func anyStrings(v any) []string {
	var out []string
	list, _ := v.([]any)
	for _, s := range list {
		out = append(out, s.(string))
	}
	return out
}

func TestECalcSearchDescribeAndOpenCoverPinouts(t *testing.T) {
	cat := ecalcPinoutCatalog(t)
	out, _ := ecalcRunOn(t, cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "search"})
	cats, _ := out["categories"].([]any)
	listed := false
	for _, c := range cats {
		if c.(map[string]any)["id"] == "pinouts" {
			listed = c.(map[string]any)["count"] == float64(3)
		}
	}
	if out["total"] != float64(cat.ItemCount()) || !listed || cat.ItemCount() != len(cat.Calculators)+len(cat.Tables)+len(cat.Codes)+3 {
		t.Errorf("search without a query = %v", out)
	}
	out, _ = ecalcRunOn(t, cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "search", Query: "ethernet"})
	results, _ := out["results"].([]any)
	if len(results) == 0 || results[0].(map[string]any)["id"] != "t_rj" || results[0].(map[string]any)["kind"] != "pinout" || results[0].(map[string]any)["category"] != "pinouts" {
		t.Fatalf("search = %v", out)
	}

	// describe: group, connector, view, pin count, variants, counts per type, notes and source, but no pins.
	out, exec := ecalcRunOn(t, cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "describe", ID: "T_RJ"})
	variants, _ := out["variants"].([]any)
	counts, _ := out["counts"].(map[string]any)
	if out["status"] != "ok" || out["operation"] != "describe" || out["kind"] != "pinout" || out["group"] != "data" || out["pin_count"] != float64(4) || len(variants) != 2 ||
		counts["data"] != float64(3) || counts["ground"] != float64(1) || out["notes"] != "Pair 1 is the centre pair." || out["source"] != "Fixture standard" ||
		out["connector"] == nil || out["view"] == nil || out["pins"] != nil || exec.Event != nil {
		t.Fatalf("describe = %s", exec.Output)
	}
	if out, _ = ecalcRunOn(t, cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "calculate", ID: "t_rj", Inputs: ecalcPairs("x", "1")}); out["code"] != "not_a_calculator" || !strings.Contains(out["message"].(string), "t_rj is a pinout") {
		t.Errorf("calculate on a pinout = %v", out)
	}
	if out, _ = ecalcRunOn(t, cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "table", ID: "t_rj"}); out["code"] != "not_a_table" || !strings.Contains(out["message"].(string), "pinout reads its pins") {
		t.Errorf("table on a pinout = %v", out)
	}

	// open works with the id of a pinout and takes no values.
	exec = executeECalc(ecalcDesktopConfig(), cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "open", ID: "t_rj"})
	out = ecalcDecode(t, exec)
	if out["status"] != "ok" || out["page"] != "t_rj" || exec.Event == nil || !strings.Contains(out["message"].(string), "Test jack pinout") || !strings.Contains(out["message"].(string), "Use pinout to read its pins") {
		t.Fatalf("open = %s", exec.Output)
	}
	if out, _ = ecalcRunOn(t, cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "open", ID: "t_rj", Inputs: ecalcPairs("x", "1")}); out["code"] != "not_a_calculator" {
		t.Errorf("open with values = %v", out)
	}
}

// The outer bound of the tool (ecalc_budget.go) refuses a result that is over the budget. A page of pins can always be
// shortened, so it must never get that answer, for the fixture pinouts and for every pinout the catalog will ever hold:
// the loop over ecalc.Default().Pinouts is empty until the content exists and then checks every real item, every variant,
// with and without a pin, at the default budget and at the smallest budgets the agent can hand over.
func TestECalcPinoutPagesStayWithinTheBound(t *testing.T) {
	shipped, err := ecalc.Default()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for name, cat := range map[string]*ecalc.Catalog{"fixture": ecalcPinoutCatalog(t), "real": shipped} {
		if name == "fixture" && len(cat.Pinouts) != 3 {
			t.Fatalf("the fixture catalog has %d pinouts", len(cat.Pinouts))
		}
		for _, p := range cat.Pinouts {
			variants := []string{""}
			for _, v := range p.Variants {
				variants = append(variants, v.ID)
			}
			for _, variant := range variants {
				pins, _, _ := p.PinsOf(variant)
				requests := []ECalcRequest{
					{Operation: "pinout", ID: p.ID, Variant: variant, Limit: 50},
					{Operation: "pinout", ID: p.ID, Variant: variant, Pin: pins[0].Name, Limit: 50},
					{Operation: "pinout", ID: p.ID, Variant: variant, Pin: pins[len(pins)-1].Number},
					{Operation: "describe", ID: p.ID},
				}
				for _, outputBudget := range []int{0, 6000, 2100, 1} {
					budget := ecalcBudget(outputBudget)
					for _, req := range requests {
						req.OutputBudget = outputBudget
						exec := executeECalc(nil, cat, req)
						out := ecalcDecode(t, exec)
						if out["status"] != "ok" || out["code"] != nil || len(exec.Output) > budget {
							t.Errorf("%s %s/%s with budget %d: %d bytes, status %v, code %v: %.300s", name, req.Operation, p.ID, budget, len(exec.Output), out["status"], out["code"], exec.Output)
							continue
						}
						if req.Operation != "pinout" {
							continue
						}
						// A shortened page says where to continue and carries at least the one pin a named pin asks for.
						listed, _ := out["pins"].([]any)
						if out["returned"] != float64(len(listed)) || (out["truncated"] == true && len(listed) > 0 && out["next_offset"] != float64(len(listed))) {
							t.Errorf("%s %s with budget %d: returned %v of %d pins, truncated %v, next_offset %v", name, p.ID, budget, out["returned"], len(listed), out["truncated"], out["next_offset"])
						}
						if req.Pin != "" && out["found"] != true {
							t.Errorf("%s %s pin %q is not found", name, p.ID, req.Pin)
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}

	// The 40-pin board with a note on every pin: the default page loses the notes first and then pins; at the smallest
	// budget a page is a few pins and the next page starts right after them.
	cat := ecalcPinoutCatalog(t)
	full, _ := ecalcRunOn(t, cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "pinout", ID: "t_board", OutputBudget: 1 << 20})
	if full["returned"] != float64(40) || full["truncated"] != nil {
		t.Fatalf("the full page = %v", full["returned"])
	}
	small, exec := ecalcRunOn(t, cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "pinout", ID: "t_board", OutputBudget: 2100})
	listed, _ := small["pins"].([]any)
	if len(listed) < 3 || len(listed) >= 40 || small["total"] != float64(40) || small["truncated"] != true || small["next_offset"] != float64(len(listed)) ||
		!strings.Contains(small["note"].(string), "pin notes left out") || strings.Contains(exec.Output, "Note for pin") {
		t.Fatalf("a page at the smallest budget: %d pins, %s", len(listed), exec.Output)
	}
	next, _ := ecalcRunOn(t, cat, ECalcRequest{Operation: "pinout", ID: "t_board", Offset: len(listed), Limit: 3, OutputBudget: 2100})
	if next["offset"] != float64(len(listed)) || next["returned"] != float64(3) {
		t.Errorf("the next page = %v", next)
	}
}
```

```go
type ecalcDescribePinoutOut struct {
	Status    string `json:"status"`
	Operation string `json:"operation"`
	ecalc.PinoutDescription
	Truncated bool `json:"truncated,omitempty"`
}

// ecalcDescribePinout answers what a pinout is, without its pins. A long description loses its optional text first (the
// texts are clipped, then the per-variant counts, then the texts go), the view last.
func ecalcDescribePinout(cat *ecalc.Catalog, id string, budget int) VirtualDesktopExecution {
	d, err := cat.DescribePinout(id)
	if err != nil {
		return ecalcQueryFailure(err)
	}
	out := ecalcDescribePinoutOut{Status: "ok", Operation: "describe", PinoutDescription: d}
	return ecalcFit(budget, func() any { return out },
		func() { out.Doc, out.Notes, out.Truncated = ecalcClip(out.Doc, 240), ecalcClip(out.Notes, 240), true },
		func() { out.Source = ecalcClip(out.Source, 120) },
		func() {
			variants := make([]ecalc.PinoutVariantInfo, len(out.Variants))
			copy(variants, out.Variants)
			for i := range variants {
				variants[i].Counts = nil
			}
			out.Variants = variants
		},
		func() { out.Doc, out.Notes, out.Source = "", "", "" },
		func() { out.View = "" },
	)
}

type ecalcPinoutOut struct {
	Status    string `json:"status"`
	Operation string `json:"operation"`
	ecalc.PinoutResult
}

// ecalcPinout answers the pins of a pinout. When the answer is over the budget it shortens the notes first (the clipped
// notes and source, the notes of the pins, the notes of the pinout), then lists fewer pins (the answer says where to
// continue), then leaves out the source and, as the last resort for a budget that ExecuteECalc can really hand over (from
// ecalcMinBudget), the listed pins themselves. A page of pins is shortened, never refused for its size.
func ecalcPinout(cat *ecalc.Catalog, req ECalcRequest, budget int) VirtualDesktopExecution {
	res, err := cat.QueryPinout(req.ID, ecalc.PinoutRequest{Pin: req.Pin, Variant: req.Variant, Filter: req.Filter, Offset: req.Offset, Limit: req.Limit})
	if err != nil {
		return ecalcQueryFailure(err)
	}
	out := ecalcPinoutOut{Status: "ok", Operation: "pinout", PinoutResult: res}
	note, shortened, advice := res.Note, []string{}, ""
	build := func() any {
		out.Note = note
		if len(shortened) > 0 {
			out.Note = strings.TrimSpace(note + " Shortened to fit the output limit: " + strings.Join(shortened, ", ") + "." + advice)
		}
		return out
	}
	steps := []func(){
		func() {
			out.Notes, out.Source, shortened = ecalcClip(out.Notes, 160), ecalcClip(out.Source, 120), append(shortened, "notes and source clipped")
		},
		func() {
			pins := make([]ecalc.PinAnswer, len(out.Pins))
			copy(pins, out.Pins)
			dropped := false
			for i := range pins {
				dropped = dropped || pins[i].Notes != ""
				pins[i].Notes = ""
			}
			out.Pins = pins
			if dropped {
				shortened = append(shortened, "pin notes left out")
			}
		},
		func() {
			if out.Notes != "" {
				out.Notes, shortened = "", append(shortened, "pinout notes left out")
			}
		},
	}
	for range len(out.Pins) {
		steps = append(steps, func() {
			if n := len(out.Pins); n > 1 {
				out.Keep(n - 1)
			}
		})
	}
	steps = append(steps, func() { out.Source, shortened = "", append(shortened, "source left out") })
	if budget >= ecalcMinBudget {
		steps = append(steps, func() {
			if len(out.Pins) > 0 {
				out.Keep(0)
				shortened = append(shortened, "pins left out")
				advice = " No pin fits the output limit: name one with pin."
			}
		})
	}
	return ecalcFit(budget, build, steps...)
}
```

```go
package agent

import (
	"context"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"aurago/internal/config"
)

// The pinout operation of the ecalc tool as the agent sees it: pin and variant are no ToolCall fields (a pin number
// arrives as a number as often as a text), the dispatcher runs the operation without the desktop, and discovery finds
// the tool for connector words.

func TestECalcPinoutParametersAreNoToolCallFields(t *testing.T) {
	typ := reflect.TypeOf(ToolCall{})
	for i := 0; i < typ.NumField(); i++ {
		name := strings.Split(typ.Field(i).Tag.Get("json"), ",")[0]
		if name == "pin" || name == "variant" {
			t.Errorf("ToolCall has the field %s (json %q): ecalc would have to share its type", typ.Field(i).Name, name)
		}
	}
	if _, ok := toolCallStringFields["pin"]; ok {
		t.Error("pin must not be a coerced string field")
	}
}

func TestECalcNativeCallDecodesPinoutArguments(t *testing.T) {
	req := decodeECalcArgs(ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"pinout","id":"rj45","variant":"t568b","pin":"TX+","filter":"data","offset":2,"limit":5}`))
	if req.Operation != "pinout" || req.ID != "rj45" || req.Variant != "t568b" || req.Pin != "TX+" || req.Filter != "data" || req.Offset != 2 || req.Limit != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("request = %+v", req)
	}
	// A pin number arrives as a number (or a numeric text) and is read as typed; a call without them leaves both empty.
	for name, arguments := range map[string]string{
		"number":      `{"operation":"pinout","id":"usb_a","pin":4}`,
		"numeric":     `{"operation":"pinout","id":"usb_a","pin":"4"}`,
		"padded text": `{"operation":"pinout","id":"usb_a","pin":" 4 "}`,
	} {
		if got := decodeECalcArgs(ecalcNativeCall(t, arguments)); got.Pin != "4" || got.Variant != "" {
			t.Errorf("%s: pin %q, variant %q", name, got.Pin, got.Variant)
		}
	}
	if got := decodeECalcArgs(ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"pinout","id":"usb_a","variant":2}`)); got.Variant != "2" {
		t.Errorf("a number as variant = %q", got.Variant)
	}
	if got := decodeECalcArgs(ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"pinout","id":"usb_a"}`)); got.Pin != "" || got.Variant != "" || got.Filter != "" {
		t.Errorf("a plain pinout call = %+v", got)
	}
	// A text-mode call (a JSON object in the reply) reaches the same request.
	req = decodeECalcArgs(ParseToolCall(`{"action":"ecalc","operation":"pinout","id":"raspberry_pi_40","pin":"GND","limit":3}`))
	if req.Operation != "pinout" || req.ID != "raspberry_pi_40" || req.Pin != "GND" || req.Limit != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("text-mode request = %+v", req)
	}
}

func TestECalcDispatchRunsPinoutCallsWithoutTheDesktop(t *testing.T) {
	broker := &ecalcJSONBroker{}
	dc := &DispatchContext{Cfg: &config.Config{}, Logger: testLogger, Broker: broker}
	// The shipped catalog may have no pinouts yet: an unknown id is the tool's own error, not a failure of the dispatch.
	out, ok := dispatchPlatform(context.Background(), ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"pinout","id":"no_such_pinout","pin":4}`), dc)
	if !ok || !strings.HasPrefix(out, "Tool Output: ") || !strings.Contains(out, `"status":"error"`) || !strings.Contains(out, `"code":"unknown_id"`) || strings.Contains(out, "invalid_operation") {
		t.Fatalf("dispatch = %v %s", ok, out)
	}
	out, _ = dispatchPlatform(context.Background(), ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"pinout","id":"awg"}`), dc)
	if !strings.Contains(out, `"code":"not_a_pinout"`) {
		t.Fatalf("pinout on a table: %s", out)
	}
	if len(broker.json) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("pinout must not broadcast: %v", broker.json)
	}
	if a := DescribeAction(ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"pinout","id":"usb_a"}`), nil); a.Mutating || a.Operation != "pinout" {
		t.Fatalf("action = %+v", a)
	}
}

func TestECalcSearchTermsFindPinouts(t *testing.T) {
	catalog := BuildToolCatalog(BuildNativeToolSchemas("", nil, ToolFeatureFlags{}, nil), nil, "")
	for _, query := range []string{"connector pinout", "USB connector pins", "Steckerbelegung", "Pinbelegung Stecker"} {
		matches := catalog.Search(query)
		found := false
		for _, entry := range matches[:min(5, len(matches))] {
			found = found || entry.Name == "ecalc"
		}
		if !found {
			t.Errorf("%q did not find ecalc in the top five", query)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
			if cat, err := ecalc.Default(); err == nil && len(cat.Pinouts) == 0 {
				if _, known := cat.Item(id); !known {
					t.Logf("the catalog has no pinouts yet: the example %s is only checked against the schema", example[1])
					continue
				}
			}
		}
		out, ok := dispatchPlatform(context.Background(), tc, &DispatchContext{Cfg: ecalcAgentConfig(), Logger: testLogger, Broker: &ecalcJSONBroker{}})
		if !ok || !strings.Contains(out, `"status":"ok"`) {
			t.Errorf("the example does not run: %s\n%s", example[1], out)
		}
	}
	for _, op := range []string{"search", "describe", "calculate", "open", "table", "pinout", "decode", "encode"} {
		if !seen[op] {
			t.Errorf("the manual has no example for %s", op)
		}
```

Replace (block 1 of 5, it occurs once):
````markdown
# ECalc (electronics calculators, reference tables and component codes)

Use `ecalc` for electronics formulas: Ohm's law, voltage dividers, filters, timers, op-amp stages, power supplies, RF, standard resistor values and more. It computes with the same catalog and formulas as the ECalc desktop app, exactly and with units; use it instead of calculating by hand. The catalog also holds reference **tables** (AWG wire sizes, PCB trace width after IPC-2221, E-series values and more) that you read with `table`, and **component codes** (resistor and inductor colour bands, SMD markings, capacitor and ceramic codes) that you read with `decode` and write with `encode`. It reads nothing from the network or from files.

## Workflow

1. `search` with a few words (English or German, at most 256 characters): a topic, a part or a formula. A hit has a `kind`: `calculator`, `table` or `code`. An empty `query` lists the categories.
2. `describe` the item you picked. A calculator: its variables with units and defaults, the choices, how many values are needed (`dof`), which input combinations work (`sets`), the computed outputs (`derived`), the checks and the formula. A table: its columns, key, row count, notes and source. A code: its `code_kind` and the forms it reads and writes.
3. `calculate` with the values you know (any complete input set works, so you can solve for whichever quantity is missing), `table` to read rows or one value of a table, `decode` to read a code, `encode` to write one.
4. `open` only when the user wants to see or play with the item; it opens the ECalc app on the desktop (pre-filled for a calculator).

```json
````
with:
````markdown
# ECalc (electronics calculators, reference tables, component codes and pinouts)

Use `ecalc` for electronics formulas: Ohm's law, voltage dividers, filters, timers, op-amp stages, power supplies, RF, standard resistor values and more. It computes with the same catalog and formulas as the ECalc desktop app, exactly and with units; use it instead of calculating by hand. The catalog also holds reference **tables** (AWG wire sizes, PCB trace width after IPC-2221, E-series values and more) that you read with `table`, **component codes** (resistor and inductor colour bands, SMD markings, capacitor and ceramic codes) that you read with `decode` and write with `encode`, and **pinouts** (connectors, PC power plugs, board headers, debug ports, IC packages) whose pins you read with `pinout`. It reads nothing from the network or from files.

## Workflow

1. `search` with a few words (English or German, at most 256 characters): a topic, a part or a formula. A hit has a `kind`: `calculator`, `table`, `code` or `pinout`. An empty `query` lists the categories.
2. `describe` the item you picked. A calculator: its variables with units and defaults, the choices, how many values are needed (`dof`), which input combinations work (`sets`), the computed outputs (`derived`), the checks and the formula. A table: its columns, key, row count, notes and source. A code: its `code_kind` and the forms it reads and writes. A pinout: its group, connector, what the drawing shows (`view`), the pin count, the variants and the pins per type, but not the pins.
3. `calculate` with the values you know (any complete input set works, so you can solve for whichever quantity is missing), `table` to read rows or one value of a table, `pinout` to read the pins of a connector or board, `decode` to read a code, `encode` to write one.
4. `open` only when the user wants to see or play with the item; it opens the ECalc app on the desktop (pre-filled for a calculator).

```json
````

```markdown
## Operations

- `search`: `query`, optional `limit` (1-25, default 10). Results hold `id`, `kind`, `name`, `category` and a one-sentence `summary`, best match first; `total` is the number of matches and `truncated: true` means more exist than were returned.
- `describe`: `id` of a calculator, table or code. Calculator vars have `id`, `label`, `name`, `dim`, `unit` (the unit a bare number is read in; empty means the SI unit), `units` (units a value may carry), `input`, `eseries` and the `default`. A table has `columns` (`id`, `name`, `dim`, `unit`, `units`, `key`), `key`, `row_count`, `notes`, `source`, `guide`/`mains` with a `caution`, and a `finder` when a calculator selects its rows. A code has `code_kind` (the `kind` for decode and encode), `decode` (the forms it reads), `encode` (the request fields) and `fields`.
- `calculate`: `id`, `inputs`, optional `choices` and `eseries` (E3, E6, E12, E24, E48, E96 or E192; default E24).
- `table`: `id` and optionally `filter`, `offset`, `limit` and `lookup` (see Tables).
- `decode`: `kind` and `code` (see Codes).
- `encode`: `kind`, `value` and optionally `bands`, `tolerance`, `tempco`, `voltage` and `class` (which of them a kind reads: see Codes).
- `open`: `id` of any item (optional), optional `inputs` and `choices` (calculators only). Without `id` it only opens the app. The values are not checked against each other; the app shows them as typed.
```

```markdown
- `guide: true` marks values transcribed from a standard as a guide: the standard itself is authoritative. `mains: true` marks installation data: the national rules and a qualified person decide. Pass the `caution` on to the user and name the `source` when they rely on a value. `notes` explain conditions and assumptions of the table.
- Answers are shortened to fit the output limit and the `note` says what was left out: first `si`, then fewer rows are listed (`truncated`, continue at `next_offset`); with a very small limit also the column names, the notes and the source, and as the last resort the rows themselves (`returned: 0`: read single cells with a `lookup` that names its `output` column). A table page is shortened, never refused for its size. Use `filter` or `lookup` instead of asking for more rows.

## Codes

- `decode` reads a code, `encode` writes one. `kind` is the `code_kind` from `describe` of a code item (the id of the code item works too).
```

with:
```markdown
- `guide: true` marks values transcribed from a standard as a guide: the standard itself is authoritative. `mains: true` marks installation data: the national rules and a qualified person decide. Pass the `caution` on to the user and name the `source` when they rely on a value. `notes` explain conditions and assumptions of the table.
- Answers are shortened to fit the output limit and the `note` says what was left out: first `si`, then fewer rows are listed (`truncated`, continue at `next_offset`); with a very small limit also the column names, the notes and the source, and as the last resort the rows themselves (`returned: 0`: read single cells with a `lookup` that names its `output` column). A table page is shortened, never refused for its size. Use `filter` or `lookup` instead of asking for more rows.

## Pinouts

- `pinout` lists the pins of a connector, board header or IC package: `pins` is a list of `{number, name, function, type, wire, notes}` in pin order. `type` is `power`, `ground`, `signal`, `data`, `io` (a pin the user programs, such as GPIO) or `nc` (not connected or reserved). `wire` is the English colour name (`white-green`) where a standard names one (RJ45, ATX, servo cables) and absent otherwise. `connector` says what the item is, `view` what its drawing shows: read it before you tell the user where a pin sits (rows are as seen looking at the mating face of the plug or the socket; a DIP is seen from above with the notch at the top).
- `pin` is a pin number (`"7"`, `"A1"`) or a name (`GND`, `TX+`), exact and case-insensitive; several pins can share a name (a board has many GND), and all of them are returned. A `pin` that matches nothing answers `found: false` with an empty list and the `variants`, not an error: try another spelling, another variant, or leave `pin` out. The value is text, a number is read as typed.
- `variant` is a variant id from `describe` (RJ45 `t568a` and `t568b`, audio `ctia` and `omtp`); without it the first variant is read and `variant` and `variants` in the answer say which. A variant the item does not have is an error that lists the ids.
- `filter` keeps the pins whose number, name, function or notes contain the text (English or German, at most 128 characters); with `pin` both must match. `total` counts the pins that match, `returned` those listed from `offset`; `limit` is 1-50, default 50.
- Pins come from datasheets and standards named in `source`; pass the `notes` on when a pin has a caution (voltage, direction) and name the `source` when the user relies on a pin out for wiring or soldering. Never guess a pin the answer does not list.
- Answers are shortened to fit the output limit and the `note` says what was left out: first the clipped notes and source, then the notes of the pins, then the notes of the pinout, then fewer pins are listed (`truncated`, continue at `next_offset`). Use `pin` or `filter` instead of asking for more.

## Codes

- `decode` reads a code, `encode` writes one. `kind` is the `code_kind` from `describe` of a code item (the id of the code item works too).
```

```markdown
## Errors

- `unknown_id`: the message suggests close matches; search first. An id of more than 256 characters is refused as unknown without a search. `not_a_calculator`, `not_a_table` and `not_a_code`: the id names an item of another kind; the message says which operation reads it.
- `unknown_variable`, `not_an_input` (a computed output cannot be given), `unknown_choice`, `unknown_option`, `unknown_eseries`, `duplicate_name`, `too_many_values`: the message lists the valid names; fix the call.
- `parse_error`: the text of one value could not be read with the unit of its variable or column; the message names the variable or column and its dimension.
- `underdetermined`: too few values, or no combination of them is a solvable set; `sets` lists the input sets closest first and the message says what to add.
- `unknown_column`, `invalid_lookup` (bad mode, no value, missing output, a text column in ge or interp, a column that is not steady for interp), `invalid_filter` (more than 128 characters): the message lists the columns or the valid forms.
- `unknown_code_kind`: the message lists the kinds. `invalid_code`: the code to decode could not be read (the message says why: an unknown colour, a wrong number of bands, more than 64 characters). `invalid_value`: a field of an encode request could not be read or contradicts another (a value that is no number, `bands` out of range, nothing to encode). `unsupported`: well formed, but not decodable or not codable, for example a symbol that makers disagree on or a tolerance without a band colour.
- `invalid_operation`: use `search`, `describe`, `calculate`, `table`, `decode`, `encode` or `open`.
- `policy_denied` with `desktop_unavailable` or `desktop_agent_control_disabled` (open only): the desktop is off or the user has not allowed the agent to control it. Give the numbers from `calculate` or `table` instead and say that the user can open ECalc themselves.
- `output_budget_exceeded`: a complete calculation cannot fit the available response budget. Do not interpret it as a partial numeric result. Describe/search responses may omit optional explanatory detail.
- Answers are shortened to fit the output limit; `truncated: true` marks it. Search again with more specific words or fewer results rather than asking for more.
```

```markdown
Operates the visible Desktop Notes library with `list`, `search`, `read`, and `create`. Existing notes are immutable to the agent (create-only); the protection also holds against detours through other file tools whenever isolation is active.

### `ecalc`
Electronics calculators from the same catalog and formulas as the ECalc desktop app ([Chapter 32](32-ecalc.md)): Ohm's law, dividers, filters, timers, op-amps, power supplies, RF and standard resistor values, plus its reference tables (AWG, IPC-2221 trace width, E-series and more) and component codes (colour bands, SMD markings, capacitor and ceramic codes). Always available, without a config switch: it computes on an embedded catalog and reads no network or files. The agent finds it through `discover_tools` (search terms such as *electronics calculator*, *Widerstand berechnen*, *Spannungsteiler berechnen*). `search` lists calculators, tables and codes (`id`, `kind`, name, category and a one-sentence summary; an empty `query` lists the categories); `describe` returns the variables with units and defaults, the choices, `dof`, the solvable input sets, the computed outputs, the checks and the formulas (for a table the columns with units, the key, the row count, notes, source and the caution of guide and mains tables; for a code its kind and the forms it reads and writes); `calculate` solves from the given `inputs` (a bare number is read in the variable's default unit) and answers SI and formatted values, E-series suggestions for computed resistors (the standard-value combiner lists `combos`: the nearest single value and the best series and parallel pairs), the calculator's warnings and `contradictions` when a redundant value differs from the computed one by more than 1 %; a request that cannot be solved answers `underdetermined` and lists the input sets closest first. `table` lists the rows of a table (`filter`, `offset`, `limit`: 20 rows by default, at most 50) and answers one `lookup` (`exact`, `ge` or `interp`) with formatted and SI values; `decode` reads a component code (band colours or a marking as printed) and `encode` writes the code of a value, both answering the value, the bands and the decoded fields. `open` shows a calculator (pre-filled with the given values), a table or a code in the ECalc app, and needs the Virtual Desktop, **Allow agent control** and the desktop agent tool (otherwise `policy_denied` with `desktop_unavailable` or `desktop_agent_control_disabled`). A2A requests may search, describe, calculate, read tables and decode or encode codes but not open. Answers are shortened to the inline output limit.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `operation` | string | `search`, `describe`, `calculate`, `table`, `decode`, `encode` or `open` |
| `query` | string | Topic, part or formula in English or German (`search`; empty lists the categories) |
| `id` | string | Item id from `search` (`describe`, `calculate`, `table`, `open`) |
| `inputs` | array | `{name, value}` pairs: variable id and the value as typed, for example `4k7`, `12 V`, `25 °C` (`calculate`, `open`) |
| `choices` | array | `{name, option}` pairs for choices such as the waveform (`calculate`, `open`) |
| `eseries` | string | `E3`, `E6`, `E12`, `E24` (default), `E48`, `E96` or `E192` (`calculate`) |
| `limit` | integer | Number of results, 1–25 (default 10; `search`), or of rows, 1–50 (default 20; `table`) |
| `offset` | integer | First row to list (`table`) |
| `filter` | string | Only rows with a cell that contains this text, case-insensitive (`table`, at most 128 characters) |
| `lookup` | object | `{column, value, mode, output}`: `mode` is `exact` (default), `ge` (the row with the smallest cell that is at least the value) or `interp` (linear, needs `output`) (`table`) |
| `kind` | string | Code kind, as shown by `describe` of a code item (`decode`, `encode`) |
| `code` | string | The code as printed or as English colour names, at most 64 characters (`decode`) |
```
