```markdown
Bedient die sichtbare Desktop-Notizbibliothek mit `list`, `search`, `read` und `create`. Bestehende Notizen sind für den Agenten unveränderlich (Create-only); der Schutz gilt auch gegenüber Umwegen über andere Datei-Tools, sofern Isolation aktiv ist.

### `ecalc`
Elektronik-Rechner aus demselben Katalog und mit denselben Formeln wie die Desktop-App ECalc ([Kapitel 32](32-ecalc.md)): Ohmsches Gesetz, Teiler, Filter, Timer, OpAmps, Stromversorgung, HF und Normwerte für Widerstände, dazu die Referenztabellen (AWG, IPC-2221-Leiterbahnbreite, E-Reihen und mehr) und Bauteilcodes (Farbringe, SMD-Aufdrucke, Kondensator- und Keramikcodes). Immer verfügbar, ohne Config-Schalter: Das Tool rechnet auf einem eingebetteten Katalog und liest weder Netzwerk noch Dateien. Der Agent findet es über `discover_tools` (Suchbegriffe wie *Elektronik Rechner*, *Widerstand berechnen*, *Spannungsteiler berechnen*). `search` listet Rechner, Tabellen und Codes (`id`, `kind`, Name, Kategorie und ein Satz Zusammenfassung; eine leere `query` listet die Kategorien); `describe` liefert Variablen mit Einheiten und Vorgaben, die Auswahlfelder, `dof`, die lösbaren Eingabekombinationen, die berechneten Ausgaben, die Prüfungen und die Formeln (bei einer Tabelle die Spalten mit Einheiten, den Schlüssel, die Zeilenzahl, Anmerkungen, Quelle und den Warnhinweis von Richtwert- und Netztabellen; bei einem Code seine Art und die Formen, die er liest und schreibt); `calculate` löst aus den angegebenen `inputs` (eine nackte Zahl gilt in der Standardeinheit der Variablen) und antwortet mit SI- und formatierten Werten, E-Reihen-Vorschlägen für berechnete Widerstände (die Normwert-Kombination listet `combos`: den nächsten Einzelwert und die besten Reihen- und Parallelpaare), den Warnungen des Rechners und `contradictions`, wenn ein überzähliger Wert um mehr als 1 % vom berechneten abweicht; eine nicht lösbare Anfrage antwortet mit `underdetermined` und nennt die nächstliegenden Eingabekombinationen zuerst. `table` listet die Zeilen einer Tabelle (`filter`, `offset`, `limit`: standardmäßig 20 Zeilen, höchstens 50) und beantwortet eine `lookup`-Abfrage (`exact`, `ge` oder `interp`) mit formatierten und SI-Werten; `decode` liest einen Bauteilcode (Farbringe oder ein Aufdruck wie gedruckt) und `encode` schreibt den Code zu einem Wert, beide antworten mit Wert, Ringen und den entschlüsselten Feldern. `open` zeigt einen Rechner (mit den Werten vorausgefüllt), eine Tabelle oder einen Code in der ECalc-App und braucht den Virtual Desktop, die Option `allow_agent_control` und das Desktop-Agent-Tool (sonst `policy_denied` mit `desktop_unavailable` oder `desktop_agent_control_disabled`). A2A-Anfragen dürfen suchen, beschreiben, rechnen, Tabellen lesen und Codes lesen oder schreiben, aber nichts öffnen. Antworten werden auf das Inline-Ausgabelimit gekürzt.

| Parameter | Typ | Beschreibung |
|-----------|-----|--------------|
| `operation` | string | `search`, `describe`, `calculate`, `table`, `decode`, `encode` oder `open` |
| `query` | string | Thema, Bauteil oder Formel auf Deutsch oder Englisch (`search`; leer listet die Kategorien) |
| `id` | string | Element-ID aus `search` (`describe`, `calculate`, `table`, `open`) |
| `inputs` | array | `{name, value}`-Paare: Variablen-ID und der Wert, wie man ihn tippt, zum Beispiel `4k7`, `12 V`, `25 °C` (`calculate`, `open`) |
| `choices` | array | `{name, option}`-Paare für Auswahlfelder wie die Kurvenform (`calculate`, `open`) |
| `eseries` | string | `E3`, `E6`, `E12`, `E24` (Standard), `E48`, `E96` oder `E192` (`calculate`) |
| `limit` | integer | Anzahl der Treffer, 1–25 (Standard 10; `search`), oder der Zeilen, 1–50 (Standard 20; `table`) |
| `offset` | integer | Erste aufzulistende Zeile (`table`) |
| `filter` | string | Nur Zeilen mit einer Zelle, die diesen Text enthält, ohne Beachtung der Groß-/Kleinschreibung (`table`, höchstens 128 Zeichen) |
| `lookup` | object | `{column, value, mode, output}`: `mode` ist `exact` (Standard), `ge` (die Zeile mit dem kleinsten Wert, der mindestens dem gesuchten entspricht) oder `interp` (linear, braucht `output`) (`table`) |
| `kind` | string | Codeart, wie `describe` eines Code-Elements sie nennt (`decode`, `encode`) |
| `code` | string | Der Code wie gedruckt oder als englische Farbnamen, höchstens 64 Zeichen (`decode`) |
```
with:
```markdown
Bedient die sichtbare Desktop-Notizbibliothek mit `list`, `search`, `read` und `create`. Bestehende Notizen sind für den Agenten unveränderlich (Create-only); der Schutz gilt auch gegenüber Umwegen über andere Datei-Tools, sofern Isolation aktiv ist.

### `ecalc`
Elektronik-Rechner aus demselben Katalog und mit denselben Formeln wie die Desktop-App ECalc ([Kapitel 32](32-ecalc.md)): Ohmsches Gesetz, Teiler, Filter, Timer, OpAmps, Stromversorgung, HF und Normwerte für Widerstände, dazu die Referenztabellen (AWG, IPC-2221-Leiterbahnbreite, E-Reihen und mehr), Bauteilcodes (Farbringe, SMD-Aufdrucke, Kondensator- und Keramikcodes) und Steckerbelegungen (Stecker, PC-Netzteilstecker, Board-Header, Debug-Anschlüsse und IC-Gehäuse). Immer verfügbar, ohne Config-Schalter: Das Tool rechnet auf einem eingebetteten Katalog und liest weder Netzwerk noch Dateien. Der Agent findet es über `discover_tools` (Suchbegriffe wie *Elektronik Rechner*, *Widerstand berechnen*, *Spannungsteiler berechnen*). `search` listet Rechner, Tabellen, Codes und Belegungen (`id`, `kind`, Name, Kategorie und ein Satz Zusammenfassung; eine leere `query` listet die Kategorien); `describe` liefert Variablen mit Einheiten und Vorgaben, die Auswahlfelder, `dof`, die lösbaren Eingabekombinationen, die berechneten Ausgaben, die Prüfungen und die Formeln (bei einer Tabelle die Spalten mit Einheiten, den Schlüssel, die Zeilenzahl, Anmerkungen, Quelle und den Warnhinweis von Richtwert- und Netztabellen; bei einem Code seine Art und die Formen, die er liest und schreibt; bei einer Belegung ihre Gruppe, den Steckertyp, was die Zeichnung zeigt, die Pinzahl, die Varianten, die Pins je Typ, Anmerkungen und Quelle, aber keine Pins); `calculate` löst aus den angegebenen `inputs` (eine nackte Zahl gilt in der Standardeinheit der Variablen) und antwortet mit SI- und formatierten Werten, E-Reihen-Vorschlägen für berechnete Widerstände (die Normwert-Kombination listet `combos`: den nächsten Einzelwert und die besten Reihen- und Parallelpaare), den Warnungen des Rechners und `contradictions`, wenn ein überzähliger Wert um mehr als 1 % vom berechneten abweicht; eine nicht lösbare Anfrage antwortet mit `underdetermined` und nennt die nächstliegenden Eingabekombinationen zuerst. `table` listet die Zeilen einer Tabelle (`filter`, `offset`, `limit`: standardmäßig 20 Zeilen, höchstens 50) und beantwortet eine `lookup`-Abfrage (`exact`, `ge` oder `interp`) mit formatierten und SI-Werten; `pinout` listet die Pins eines Steckers, Board-Headers oder IC-Gehäuses (`number`, `name`, `function`, `type`, die Normfarbe `wire` und `notes`) einer `variant` (standardmäßig der ersten; eine unbekannte Variante antwortet mit einem Fehler, der die IDs nennt), eingegrenzt durch `pin` (Nummer oder Name, genau und ohne Beachtung der Groß-/Kleinschreibung: alle Pins mit diesem Namen, etwa GND) oder durch einen `filter`; ein `pin`, der nichts trifft, antwortet mit `found: false` und den Varianten, nicht mit einem Fehler; `decode` liest einen Bauteilcode (Farbringe oder ein Aufdruck wie gedruckt) und `encode` schreibt den Code zu einem Wert, beide antworten mit Wert, Ringen und den entschlüsselten Feldern. `open` zeigt einen Rechner (mit den Werten vorausgefüllt), eine Tabelle, einen Code oder eine Belegung in der ECalc-App und braucht den Virtual Desktop, die Option `allow_agent_control` und das Desktop-Agent-Tool (sonst `policy_denied` mit `desktop_unavailable` oder `desktop_agent_control_disabled`). A2A-Anfragen dürfen suchen, beschreiben, rechnen, Tabellen und Belegungen lesen und Codes lesen oder schreiben, aber nichts öffnen. Antworten werden auf das Inline-Ausgabelimit gekürzt (eine Belegungsseite verliert zuerst die Anmerkungen, dann Pins; `next_offset` sagt, wo es weitergeht).

| Parameter | Typ | Beschreibung |
|-----------|-----|--------------|
| `operation` | string | `search`, `describe`, `calculate`, `table`, `pinout`, `decode`, `encode` oder `open` |
| `query` | string | Thema, Bauteil oder Formel auf Deutsch oder Englisch (`search`; leer listet die Kategorien) |
| `id` | string | Element-ID aus `search` (`describe`, `calculate`, `table`, `pinout`, `open`) |
| `inputs` | array | `{name, value}`-Paare: Variablen-ID und der Wert, wie man ihn tippt, zum Beispiel `4k7`, `12 V`, `25 °C` (`calculate`, `open`) |
| `choices` | array | `{name, option}`-Paare für Auswahlfelder wie die Kurvenform (`calculate`, `open`) |
| `eseries` | string | `E3`, `E6`, `E12`, `E24` (Standard), `E48`, `E96` oder `E192` (`calculate`) |
| `limit` | integer | Anzahl der Treffer, 1–25 (Standard 10; `search`), der Zeilen, 1–50 (Standard 20; `table`), oder der Pins, 1–50 (Standard 50; `pinout`) |
| `offset` | integer | Erste aufzulistende Zeile oder erster Pin (`table`, `pinout`) |
| `filter` | string | Nur Zeilen mit einer Zelle, die diesen Text enthält, ohne Beachtung der Groß-/Kleinschreibung (`table`, höchstens 128 Zeichen); bei `pinout` die Pins, deren Nummer, Name, Funktion oder Anmerkung ihn enthält |
| `pin` | string | Pinnummer oder Name, genau und ohne Beachtung der Groß-/Kleinschreibung (`pinout`) |
| `variant` | string | Varianten-ID aus `describe`, zum Beispiel `t568b`; standardmäßig die erste Variante (`pinout`) |
| `lookup` | object | `{column, value, mode, output}`: `mode` ist `exact` (Standard), `ge` (die Zeile mit dem kleinsten Wert, der mindestens dem gesuchten entspricht) oder `interp` (linear, braucht `output`) (`table`) |
| `kind` | string | Codeart, wie `describe` eines Code-Elements sie nennt (`decode`, `encode`) |
| `code` | string | Der Code wie gedruckt oder als englische Farbnamen, höchstens 64 Zeichen (`decode`) |
```

Insert U+00AD (a soft hyphen, invisible) into the `power` category name: `de: "Strom` + U+00AD + `versorgung"` and `sv: "Ström` + U+00AD + `försörjning"`, so that these words break with a hyphen in the rail instead of inside a syllable.

```powershell
python -I -c "import pathlib; p=pathlib.Path('internal/ecalc/catalog/categories.yaml'); t=p.read_bytes().decode('utf-8'); s=chr(0xad); o=chr(0xf6); a='de: \"Stromversorgung\"'; b='sv: \"Str'+o+'mf'+o+'rs'+o+'rjning\"'; assert t.count(a)==1 and t.count(b)==1; t=t.replace(a,'de: \"Strom'+s+'versorgung\"').replace(b,'sv: \"Str'+o+'m'+s+'f'+o+'rs'+o+'rjning\"'); p.write_bytes(t.encode('utf-8'))"
```

The contact plan repeats after a half turn, so the plug fits both ways; the CC lines show which way it is in.", de: "Der umsteckbare USB-Anschluss mit 24 Kontakten. Der Kontaktplan wiederholt sich nach einer halben Drehung, darum passt der Stecker in beiden Lagen; die CC-Leitungen zeigen, wie er steckt."}
```yaml
  notes: {en: "CC resistors, from tables 4-27 and 4-28 of the Type-C specification. Sink: Rd 5.1 kΩ to GND on CC1 and on CC2 (±10% if it reads the advertised current, otherwise ±20% is allowed). Source: Rp to 4.75–5.5 V on CC1 and on CC2: 56 kΩ ±20% for default USB power, 22 kΩ ±5% for 1.5 A, 10 kΩ ±5% for 3.0 A. With a pull-up to 3.3 V: 36 kΩ ±20%, 12 kΩ ±5%, 4.7 kΩ ±5%. A cable or adapter whose Type-C plug stands for a legacy USB host uses 56 kΩ ±5%. All VBUS contacts are tied together, and so are all GND contacts. A USB 2.0 receptacle leaves A2, A3, A10, A11, B2, B3, B10 and B11 unconnected.", de: "CC-Widerstände aus den Tabellen 4-27 und 4-28 der Type-C-Spezifikation. Senke: Rd 5,1 kΩ gegen GND an CC1 und an CC2 (±10 %, wenn sie den angebotenen Strom auswertet, sonst sind ±20 % erlaubt). Quelle: Rp nach 4,75–5,5 V an CC1 und an CC2: 56 kΩ ±20 % für die normale USB-Leistung, 22 kΩ ±5 % für 1,5 A, 10 kΩ ±5 % für 3,0 A. Mit Pull-up nach 3,3 V: 36 kΩ ±20 %, 12 kΩ ±5 %, 4,7 kΩ ±5 %. Ein Kabel oder Adapter, dessen Type-C-Stecker für einen älteren USB-Host steht, nutzt 56 kΩ ±5 %. Alle VBUS-Kontakte sind miteinander verbunden, ebenso alle GND-Kontakte. Eine USB-2.0-Buchse lässt A2, A3, A10, A11, B2, B3, B10 und B11 unbeschaltet."}
  tags: [usb, usb-c, type-c, "typ c", usb4, "usb 3.2", thunderbolt, cc, cc1, cc2, vconn, sbu, vbus, rd, rp, "5.1 k", "5,1 k", tx, rx, "power delivery", stecker, buchse, receptacle, plug]
  source: "USB Type-C Cable and Connector Specification, Release 2.5 (March 2026), figures 2-1 and 2-2, tables 3-4, 3-5, 4-27 and 4-28"

- id: hdmi_a
  kind: pinout
  category: pinouts
  group: data
  name: {cs: "HDMI Type A", da: "HDMI Type A", de: "HDMI Type A", el: "HDMI Type A", en: "HDMI Type A", es: "HDMI Type A", fr: "HDMI Type A", hi: "HDMI Type A", it: "HDMI Type A", ja: "HDMI Type A", nl: "HDMI Type A", no: "HDMI Type A", pl: "HDMI Type A", pt: "HDMI Type A", sv: "HDMI Type A", zh: "HDMI Type A"}
  doc: {en: "The full-size 19-contact HDMI connector: three TMDS data channels and a clock, each with its own shield, plus DDC, CEC, +5 V and hot plug detect.", de: "Der große 19-polige HDMI-Anschluss: drei TMDS-Datenkanäle und ein Takt, jeder mit eigener Abschirmung, dazu DDC, CEC, +5 V und Hot-Plug-Erkennung."}
  notes: {en: "The drawing has the wider side of the shell at the top, with the odd pins in the upper row. From HDMI 1.4 pins 14 and 19 can also carry the HDMI Ethernet and audio return channel (HEAC+ on 14, HEAC- on 19). Older cables and devices leave pin 14 unused. The +5 V line is only for low currents: the sources name 50 mA or 55 mA.", de: "In der Zeichnung liegt die breitere Seite des Gehäuses oben, die ungeraden Pins in der oberen Reihe. Ab HDMI 1.4 können die Pins 14 und 19 auch den HDMI-Ethernet- und Audio-Rückkanal führen (HEAC+ auf 14, HEAC- auf 19). Ältere Kabel und Geräte lassen Pin 14 ungenutzt. Die +5-V-Leitung ist nur für kleine Ströme gedacht: Die Quellen nennen 50 mA oder 55 mA."}
  tags: [hdmi, "type a", "typ a", tmds, ddc, edid, cec, hpd, "hot plug", heac, arc, hec, scl, sda, video, stecker, buchse, receptacle, plug]

      - {pins: ["18", "16", "14", "12", "10", "8", "6", "4", "2"], offset: 0.5}

    - {number: "1", name: "TMDS Data2+", function: {en: "TMDS data channel 2, positive", de: "TMDS-Datenkanal 2, positiv"}, type: data}

  doc: {en: "The full-size 20-contact DisplayPort connector: four main link lanes, an auxiliary channel, hot plug detect and a small supply. A source and a sink number the lanes differently.", de: "Der große 20-polige DisplayPort-Anschluss: vier Hauptkanäle (Lanes), ein Hilfskanal, Hot-Plug-Erkennung und eine kleine Versorgung. Quelle und Senke nummerieren die Lanes unterschiedlich."}
  notes: {en: "Choose the variant by the device: a graphics output is the source side, a monitor input the sink side. Only pins 1 to 12 differ. At a source, pin 1 is ML_Lane 0 (p); at a sink, pin 1 is ML_Lane 3 (n). The drawing has the cut corner of the shell at the lower left.", de: "Die Variante richtet sich nach dem Gerät: Ein Grafikausgang ist die Quellseite, ein Monitoreingang die Senkenseite. Nur die Pins 1 bis 12 unterscheiden sich. An der Quelle ist Pin 1 ML_Lane 0 (p), an der Senke ML_Lane 3 (n). In der Zeichnung liegt die abgeschrägte Ecke des Gehäuses unten links."}

- id: vga
  kind: pinout
  category: pinouts
  group: data
  name: {cs: "VGA (DE-15)", da: "VGA (DE-15)", de: "VGA (DE-15)", el: "VGA (DE-15)", en: "VGA (DE-15)", es: "VGA (DE-15)", fr: "VGA (DE-15)", hi: "VGA (DE-15)", it: "VGA (DE-15)", ja: "VGA (DE-15)", nl: "VGA (DE-15)", no: "VGA (DE-15)", pl: "VGA (DE-15)", pt: "VGA (DE-15)", sv: "VGA (DE-15)", zh: "VGA (DE-15)"}
  doc: {en: "The three-row 15-pin D-sub connector for analogue video. Computers and monitors usually have the female socket, cables the male plug.", de: "Der dreireihige 15-polige D-Sub-Anschluss für analoges Video. Computer und Monitore haben meist die Buchse, Kabel den Stecker."}
  notes: {en: "Devices differ on pins 4, 5, 9 and 11. Pin 9 is a missing key position on older equipment and +5 V or 3.3 V on newer. Monitors may ground pins 4 and 11, or use pin 5 as DDC return or for self-test. Pins 11, 12, 4 and 15 were once monitor ID bits 0 to 3. The drawing has the wide side of the D shell at the top.", de: "Die Geräte unterscheiden sich bei den Pins 4, 5, 9 und 11. Pin 9 ist bei älteren Geräten eine fehlende Kodierposition, bei neueren +5 V oder 3,3 V. Monitore legen die Pins 4 und 11 teils auf Masse oder nutzen Pin 5 als DDC-Rückleitung oder für den Selbsttest. Die Pins 11, 12, 4 und 15 waren früher die Monitor-ID-Bits 0 bis 3. In der Zeichnung liegt die breite Seite des D-Gehäuses oben."}
  tags: [vga, svga, de-15, de15, hd15, hd-15, db15, d-sub, dsub, rgb, hsync, vsync, ddc, edid, scl, sda, monitor, video, stecker, buchse]
  source: "Winford Engineering drawing BRKLD15HDF-SG-DIN rev A (connector pinout); Dell SE2416H user's guide, Pin assignments; Acer B193 user's guide, Connector pin assignment; Crypto Museum, D-sub connectors; Wikipedia, VGA connector with figure VGA_Port.svg; pinouts.ru, 15 pin highdensity D-SUB connector figures"

  doc: {en: "The eight-contact modular connector of twisted-pair Ethernet. T568A and T568B differ only in the wire colours: the green and the orange pair swap places, the signals stay on the same pins.", de: "Der achtpolige Modularstecker von Twisted-Pair-Ethernet. T568A und T568B unterscheiden sich nur in den Aderfarben: Das grüne und das orange Paar tauschen die Plätze, die Signale bleiben auf denselben Pins."}
  notes: {en: "Drawn: a jack seen from the front with the latch notch at the bottom, pin 1 on the left. A plug seen from its tip with the latch at the bottom has pin 1 on the right; with the latch on top, pin 1 is on the left. Signal names are those of an end device; at a switch TX and RX swap. Power over Ethernet: IEEE 802.3af/at Mode A puts the power on the data pairs, pins 1 and 2 as one pole, pins 3 and 6 as the other. Mode B uses the spare pairs, pins 4 and 5 as one pole, pins 7 and 8 as the other. The power source uses only one of the two at a time. Four-pair IEEE 802.3bt can use all four pairs together. The polarity of the data pairs is not the same everywhere, so measure before wiring anything without a rectifier.", de: "Gezeichnet: eine Buchse von vorn mit der Rastnase-Aussparung unten, Pin 1 links. Ein Stecker von der Spitze gesehen hat mit der Rastnase unten Pin 1 rechts, mit der Rastnase oben Pin 1 links. Die Signalnamen gelten für ein Endgerät, an einem Switch tauschen TX und RX. Power over Ethernet: IEEE 802.3af/at Mode A legt die Leistung auf die Datenpaare, Pins 1 und 2 als einen Pol, Pins 3 und 6 als den anderen. Mode B nutzt die freien Paare, Pins 4 und 5 als einen Pol, Pins 7 und 8 als den anderen. Die Quelle nutzt immer nur einen der beiden Wege. Vierpaariges IEEE 802.3bt kann alle vier Paare zusammen nutzen. Die Polarität der Datenpaare ist nicht überall gleich, darum vor dem Verdrahten ohne Gleichrichter messen."}

  doc: {en: "The 9-pin serial port of PCs, often called DB9. The DTE (a PC or terminal) has the male connector with pins; the DCE (a modem) has the female connector with sockets.", de: "Der 9-polige serielle Anschluss von PCs, oft DB9 genannt. Die DTE (PC oder Terminal) hat den Stecker mit Stiften, die DCE (Modem) die Buchse."}
  notes: {en: "Every signal name and direction is from the DTE's point of view. A pin carries the same signal at both ends, so the DCE drives what the DTE reads: pin 2 is an output on a DCE. The genders are the usual rule and some devices break it, so check the pin directions on the device before you connect a cable. To join two DTEs you need a cable that crosses TXD and RXD. The levels are RS-232 voltages, not logic levels.", de: "Alle Signalnamen und Richtungen sind aus Sicht der DTE angegeben. Ein Pin führt an beiden Enden dasselbe Signal, die DCE treibt also, was die DTE liest: Pin 2 ist an einer DCE ein Ausgang. Die Steckerformen sind die übliche Regel, manche Geräte halten sich nicht daran, darum vor dem Anschließen die Pinrichtungen am Gerät prüfen. Zwei DTEs verbindet ein Kabel, das TXD und RXD kreuzt. Die Pegel sind RS-232-Spannungen, keine Logikpegel."}
```

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/data/usb_a.md`:

`````markdown
# usb_a — USB 2.0 Type-A / USB 2.0 Type-A

Kind: free official specification
Pins: 4; types: power 1, ground 1, data 2

## View
Written for the receptacle, looking at its mating face (`drawn: socket`): 1 2 3 4 left to right, contact tongue in the upper half of the shell, contacts on its underside.

Basis: the text layer of the interface drawings, read by position. USB 2.0 figure 6-7 ("USB Series "A" Receptacle Interface") has the labels `1 23 4` left to right under the face view. Figure 6-9 (Series A plug, "Section A - A") has `4 32 1` left to right. The two are mirror images, which is what the catalog schema's other view produces. I rendered the same receptacle sheet from ECN #1 (page 17) and the USB 3.1 legacy figure 5-1 and looked at them: tongue on top, contacts below it.

## Sources
1. Universal Serial Bus Specification, Revision 2.0, USB-IF, file usb_20.pdf in usb_20_20250603.zip, https://www.usb.org/document-library/usb-20-specification — table 6-1 "USB Connector Termination Assignment" (contacts, signal names, typical wire colours), figures 6-7 and 6-9. Accessed 2026-11-04.

## Cross-check
One free official specification is enough. No disagreement. The USB 3.1 legacy specification, table 5-2 (read for usb_a_3), repeats pins 1 to 4.

## Choices
- The shell (table 6-1: "Shield", "Drain Wire") is not a pin in the list; it is in `notes`.
- Colours are the column "Typical Wiring Assignment".
- `VBUS` function "nominally +5 V" comes from section 4.2.1 of the same specification ("nominally +5 V at the source").
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/data/usb_a_3.md`:

`````markdown
# usb_a_3 — USB 3.x Type-A / USB 3.x Type-A

Kind: free official specification
Pins: 9; types: power 1, ground 2, data 6

## View
Written for the receptacle, looking at its mating face (`drawn: socket`): upper row 9 8 7 6 5, lower row 1 2 3 4, both left to right.

Basis, seen in the figures (extracted from the PDF and looked at): figure 5-4, detail G, is the front view of the Standard-A plug and labels `5 6 7 8 9` left to right above `4 3 2 1` left to right. The receptacle is its mirror image, which gives the order above. Check against a second drawing: figure 5-5 (example footprint "PCB layout, standard mount type", connector front edge at the bottom of the drawing) has pins 9 8 7 6 5 in the rear row and 1 2 3 4 in the front row, left to right. Read from the component side, which the drawing does not state, that puts pin 1 on the left seen from the front of the receptacle, in line with detail G. Figure 5-1 shows the receptacle with the tongue in the upper half.

The half-pitch offset follows the dimensions of detail G: pins 5 to 9 at ±4.00, ±2.00 and 0 mm, pins 1 to 4 at ±3.50 and ±1.00 mm from the centre line.

The rows are not at one depth. Top and bottom in the drawing follow detail G and are a face-on schematic; `notes` says so.

## Sources
1. USB 3.1 Legacy Cable and Connector Specification, Revision 1.0, 22 September 2017, USB 3.0 Promoter Group, https://www.usb.org/document-library/usb-31-legacy-cable-and-connector-revision-10 — table 5-2 (pins, signal names, mating sequence), figures 5-1, 5-4 and 5-5. Accessed 2026-11-04.

## Cross-check
One free official specification is enough. Pins 1 to 4 agree with USB 2.0 table 6-1.

UNVERIFIED: no wire colours. Table 5-6 of this revision lists wires by number and signal only, so `wire` is left out everywhere in this item, also on pins 1 to 4.

## Choices
- Title "3.x": chapter 5 of USB 3.2 Revision 1.1 (usb_32_202206.zip, read) refers to this legacy document for the Standard-A connector, so the pinout also holds for USB 3.2 Type-A.
- Outline `usb_a` as assigned.
- Shell left out of the pins (table 5-2 lists it as "Shield") and named in `notes`.
- Note 2 of table 5-2 says Tx and Rx are defined from the host perspective; repeated in `notes`.
- VBUS: the table says only "Power", so no voltage in `function`.
`````

`````markdown
# usb_b — USB 2.0 Type-B / USB 2.0 Type-B

Kind: free official specification
Pins: 4; types: power 1, ground 1, data 2

## View
Written for the receptacle, looking at its mating face (`drawn: socket`): upper row 2 1, lower row 3 4, chamfered corners at the top.

Basis: the text layer of the interface drawings, read by position. Figure 6-8 ("USB Series "B" Receptacle Interface") has `2 1` above `3 4`. Figure 6-10 (Series B plug, "Section A - A") has `1 2` above `4 3`. These are mirror images of each other, as the catalog schema's other view expects. I rendered the same receptacle sheet from ECN #1 (page 18) and looked at it: the shell is chamfered at the top.

## Sources
1. Universal Serial Bus Specification, Revision 2.0, USB-IF, file usb_20.pdf in usb_20_20250603.zip, https://www.usb.org/document-library/usb-20-specification — table 6-1 (contacts, signal names, typical wire colours), figures 6-8 and 6-10. Accessed 2026-11-04.
2. USB 2.0 Specification Engineering Change Notice #1: Mini-B connector, file ecn1-usb20-miniB-revd.pdf in the same package — table 6-1 repeated, sheet of the Series B receptacle rendered. Accessed 2026-11-04.

## Cross-check
One free official specification is enough. No disagreement.

## Choices
Shell left out of the pins and named in `notes`. Colours are the column "Typical Wiring Assignment".
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/data/usb_mini_b.md`:

`````markdown
# usb_mini_b — USB Mini-B / USB Mini-B

Kind: free official specification
Pins: 5; types: power 1, ground 1, data 2, signal 1

## View
Written for the receptacle, looking at its mating face (`drawn: socket`): 1 2 3 4 5 left to right, wider side of the shell at the top.

Basis, seen in the drawings (rendered from the PDF and looked at): figure 6-11, "Series "Mini-B" Receptacle Interface Drawing", front view with the callouts "Pin 1" on the left and "Pin 5" on the right, shell wider at the top. Figure 6-15, "Series 'Mini-B' Plug Interface Drawing", front view with "Pin 5" on the left and "Pin 1" on the right, same way up. The two are mirror images.

## Sources
1. USB 2.0 Specification Engineering Change Notice (ECN) #1: Mini-B connector, 20 October 2000, file ecn1-usb20-miniB-revd.pdf in usb_20_20250603.zip, https://www.usb.org/document-library/usb-20-specification — table 6-2 "USB Series "mini-B" Connector Termination Assignment", figures 6-11 and 6-15 with note 1 of the plug drawing. Accessed 2026-11-04.

## Cross-check
One free official specification is enough. No disagreement. Table 6-2 lists contact 4 as "ID", wiring "not connected"; note 1 of figure 6-15 says pin 4 is installed but goes to no wire of the cable.

## Choices
- Pin 4 is `signal`, not `nc`: the contact is real and has a name, only the cable leaves it open.
- No `wire` on pin 4, the table names no colour for it.
- Shell left out of the pins and named in `notes`.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/data/usb_micro_b.md`:

`````markdown
# usb_micro_b — USB Micro-B / USB Micro-B

Kind: free official specification
Pins: 5; types: power 1, ground 1, data 2, signal 1

## View
Written for the receptacle, looking at its mating face (`drawn: socket`): 1 2 3 4 5 left to right, wider side of the shell at the top.

Basis: part seen, part derived. Figure 4-7, "Micro-B Plug Interface" (extracted from the PDF and looked at), has the front view of the plug with the callouts "No.5" on the left and "No.1" on the right, wider side at the top. Figure 4-10, "Micro-B receptacle interface", shows the receptacle the same way up but does not label the contacts. So the receptacle order is derived: it is the mirror image of the plug, because the two faces look at each other. The plug view of the item gives exactly the labelled figure 4-7.

## Sources
1. Universal Serial Bus Micro-USB Cables and Connectors Specification, Revision 1.01, 4 April 2007, file Micro-USB_1_01.pdf in usb_20_20250603.zip, https://www.usb.org/document-library/usb-20-specification — table 4-2 "Micro-A Plug Pin Assignments" and the text below it on the ID pin, figures 4-7 and 4-10. Accessed 2026-11-04.

## Cross-check
One free official specification is enough. No disagreement.

The only table in the document is written for the Micro-A plug. Its numbers, names and colours are carried to Micro-B for pins 1, 2, 3 and 5, because the same contact numbers appear on the Micro-B drawing. Pin 4 differs: the text under the table describes it for both plugs, and note 1 of figure 4-7 says pin 4 is not connected to pin 5 inside the plug.

The PDF text layer lost the ohm sign in "Ra_PLUG_ID (10 MAX)"; I read it as 10 Ω and "100k MIN" as 100 kΩ.

## Choices
- Pin 4 is `signal`: on a Micro-B plug it may be open, but the receptacle contact is the sense input of an On-The-Go device.
- Shell left out of the pins and named in `notes`.
- `drawn: socket` although the labelled figure is the plug, so that all USB items open on the receptacle.
`````

`````markdown
# usb_c — USB Type-C / USB Type-C

Kind: free official specification
Pins: 24; types: power 4, ground 4, data 12, signal 4

## View
Written for the receptacle, looking at its mating face (`drawn: socket`): upper row A1 … A12 left to right, lower row B12 … B1 left to right.

Basis, seen in the figures (extracted from the PDF and looked at): figure 2-1 is captioned "USB Type-C Receptacle Interface (Front View)" and shows exactly these rows. Figure 2-2, "USB Full-Featured Type-C Plug Interface (Front View)", shows A12 … A1 above B1 … B12, which is the mirror image the catalog schema's other view produces.

## Sources
1. USB Type-C Cable and Connector Specification, Release 2.5, March 2026, USB 3.0 Promoter Group, https://www.usb.org/document-library/usb-type-cr-cable-and-connector-specification-release-25 — figures 2-1 and 2-2; table 3-4 (pins and descriptions, with notes on B6/B7 and tied contacts); table 3-5 (USB 2.0 only); table 4-27 "Source CC Termination (Rp) Requirements"; table 4-28 "Sink CC Termination (Rd) Requirements". Accessed 2026-11-04.

## Cross-check
One free official specification is enough. Figure 2-1 and table 3-4 agree on every pin.

Values from table 4-27: default USB power 56 kΩ ±20% (to 4.75–5.5 V), 36 kΩ ±20% (to 3.3 V ±5%); 1.5 A at 5 V 22 kΩ ±5%, 12 kΩ ±5%; 3.0 A at 5 V 10 kΩ ±5%, 4.7 kΩ ±5%. Note 1: 56 kΩ ±5% in a plug on a Type-C to legacy Standard-A assembly, a Type-C to Micro-B receptacle adapter or a captive cable to a host.

Values from table 4-28: ±20% resistor 5.1 kΩ cannot detect power capability, ±10% resistor 5.1 kΩ can.

Search excerpts of a vendor page (Infineon) showed the same Rp and Rd values; I did not use it as a source.

## Choices
- Names follow figure 2-1 (`TX1+`, `D+`, `CC1`), not the table's `TXp1`, `Dp1`: people look for the former. The table's names are in the vector `ref`. ASCII hyphen instead of the figure's minus sign, so a search finds them.
- `SBU` is `signal`: the table gives only "Sideband Use", with no fixed bus. The catalog schema names CC as `signal`.
- The other two ways of building a source (current source 80 µA, 180 µA, 330 µA) and the 1.1 V clamp as Rd are left out of `notes`.
- Plug differences are in the pin `notes` of A5, B5, B6 and B7: figure 2-2 labels A5 "CC", B5 "VCONN", and B6/B7 empty; table 3-4 note 1 says B6 and B7 should not be present in the plug.
- "Thunderbolt" in the tags is a search term only, not from the specification.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/data/hdmi_a.md`:

`````markdown
# hdmi_a — HDMI Type A / HDMI Type A

Kind: cross-checked reproductions
Pins: 19; types: data 11, ground 5, power 1, signal 2

## View
Written for the receptacle, looking at its mating face (`drawn: socket`): upper row 19 17 … 1, lower row 18 16 … 2, both left to right, wider side of the shell at the top.

Basis, seen in figures and read in one text layer (the HDMI specification itself was not read):
- TRU Components 15 71 072, "HDMI Terminal Block Adaptor, Type A, Receptacle": beside the face view its text layer has `19 17 15 13 11 9 7 5 3 1` above `18 16 14 12 10 8 6 4 2`.
- Sony VPL-PHZ50 help guide, picture of the "HDMI, Female" terminal: 19 upper left, 1 upper right, 18 lower left, 2 lower right, chamfers at the bottom.
- Barco Event Master user guide, image A-4 "HDMI connector" (a device port): the same rows, numbered in the picture.
- Amphenol drawing 191-PLC-1038-00: receptacle face drawn upright, "Pin 1" and "Pin 19" on the wide side of the tongue, "Pin 2" and "Pin 18" on the chamfered side, pins 1 and 2 at the top. Turned a quarter clockwise so that the wide side is up, this is the same arrangement. This part has a receptacle at both ends, so the view is a receptacle face in either case.

The half-pitch offset of the lower row is seen in the Barco picture: 18 lies between 19 and 17.

## Sources
1. Amphenol Socapex, drawing 191-PLC-1038-00, "HDMIF TV 7 x x", receptacle, rev A, https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/2593/HDMI%20FTV%207%20x%20x.pdf — pin table, face drawing with pins 1, 2, 18, 19. Accessed 2026-11-04.
2. Rohde & Schwarz, HDMI poster, 3606.8489.82, version 03.02, June 2014, https://scdn.rohde-schwarz.com/ur/pws/dl_downloads/dl_common_library/dl_brochures_and_datasheets/pdf_1/HDMI_po_en_3606-8489-82_v0302.pdf — table "Pin assignment of HDMI connectors (type A and E)". Accessed 2026-11-04.
3. Schlegel, RRJ_HDMI_STB data sheet, 17.05.2022, https://schlegelusa.com/wp-content/uploads/product-documents/RRJ_HDMI_STB-Datasheet.pdf — pin table with HEC notes. Accessed 2026-11-04.
4. TRU Components (Conrad), 15 71 072 HDMI Terminal Block Adaptor, V1_07092021_01_en, https://static.rapidonline.com/pdf/20-2627_v1.pdf — pin table, rows. Accessed 2026-11-04.
5. Barco, Event Master Devices user guide R5905948, A.24 Standard connector pinouts, https://www.barco.com/manuals/R5905948/eriqm1q9ogv8.html — HDMI table and image A-4. Accessed 2026-11-04.
6. Sony, VPL-PHZ50 help guide, Pin Assignment (HDMI Terminal), https://helpguide.sony.net/vpl/phz50/v1/en/contents/TP1000002596.html — table and picture. Accessed 2026-11-04.
7. Sony Corp, patent EP2405654B1, https://patents.google.com/patent/EP2405654B1/en — names the HPD line (HEAC- line) on pin 19 and the utility line (HEAC+ line) on pin 14. Accessed 2026-11-04.
8. Wikipedia, HDMI, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HDMI — pin table, only as a further check of pins 14 and 19. Accessed 2026-11-04.

## Cross-check
Pins 1 to 12, 15, 16, 17 and 18 agree in sources 1 to 6 (spelling aside).

Disagreements:
- HEAC polarity. Schlegel, the Sony patent and Wikipedia: + on pin 14, - on pin 19. Rohde & Schwarz: HEC Data- on 14 and HEC Data+ on 19. Barco: HEC Data+ on 19, pin 14 blank. I chose + on 14, - on 19: three sources, among them a patent by an HDMI founder that names both lines explicitly. Rohde & Schwarz and Barco are the minority here and may share an origin.
- Pin 13. Sony's projector page says "N.C."; all others say CEC. That page describes one product that does not use CEC. CEC chosen.
- Pin 14. Amphenol "Utility"; TRU and Sony "Reserved"; Rohde & Schwarz and Schlegel "reserved up to 1.3, HEC from 1.4". All compatible; name `Utility` chosen, the history is in `function`.
- +5 V current. Rohde & Schwarz and Schlegel name 55 mA, Barco and Wikipedia 50 mA. Not resolved from what I read (the specification is paywalled), so `notes` gives both and `function` no number.

## Choices
- Names as the sources write them ("TMDS Data2+"), not the catalog schema's sample "TMDS D2+". A name fits in 24 characters.
- CEC is `data` (a one-wire bus). `Utility` is `signal` because it has no one bus role across versions. It is not `nc`: from HDMI 1.4 it can be in use.
- Shields are `ground` by the catalog schema.
- Name kept as "HDMI Type A" in all locales: treated as a proper name, like USB Type-A in the plan.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/data/displayport.md`:

`````markdown
# displayport — DisplayPort / DisplayPort

Kind: cross-checked reproductions
Pins: 20; types: data 10, ground 6, signal 3, power 1 (each variant)

## View
Written for the receptacle, looking at its mating face (`drawn: socket`): upper row 19 17 … 1, lower row 20 18 … 2, both left to right, cut corner of the shell at the lower left.

Basis, seen in three pictures (the VESA standard itself was not read):
- Barco Event Master user guide, image A-1 "DisplayPort connector": device port, numbered 19 … 1 above 20 … 2, cut corner at the lower left.
- Barco MDSC-8255 user guide, image 2-8, "Overview (sink side pin-out)": the same arrangement.
- University of Oregon page, picture beside its source-side table: the same arrangement.

The upper row is shifted to the right by about half a pitch against the lower: in the pictures 19 lies right of 20, and 1 right of 2. So `offset: 0.5` goes on the upper row.

The view is implied more than stated. Wikipedia captions the same arrangement "Pinout as looking at source side connector". Otherwise no text says "viewed from the mating side": the pictures are of device ports in device manuals, with the contacts on a central tongue, which is what a receptacle has. No maker drawing of a bare connector was found: a Molex drawing URL timed out, and the search turned up nothing else I could open.

## Sources
1. NCR Voyix, 7772 workstation online help, DisplayPort pinout, https://onlinehelp.ncrvoyix.com/Retail/Workstations/7772/HTML/Topics/CircuitBoard/PinoutDisplayPort.htm — pin table of a PC's output. Accessed 2026-11-04.
2. Barco, Event Master Devices user guide R5905948, A.24 Standard connector pinouts, https://www.barco.com/manuals/R5905948/eriqm1q9ogv8.html — pin table and image A-1. Accessed 2026-11-04.
3. Barco, MDSC-8255 user guide, 2.4.5 DisplayPort connector, https://www.barco.com/manuals/R5911693/yf14wdmancf9.html — "Overview (sink side pin-out)", list and picture. Accessed 2026-11-04.
4. Dell, P3424WEB user's guide, page "Pin assignments", read at https://www.manualslib.com/manual/3349470/Dell-P3424web.html?page=25 — table of a monitor's "DP port (in)". Accessed 2026-11-04.
5. University of Oregon, Projection Design Bootcamp, Display Port Information, https://blogs.uoregon.edu/projectiondesignpdw/?p=178 — source-side table, note on CONFIG pins, note on the sink side. Accessed 2026-11-04.
6. Wikipedia, DisplayPort, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DisplayPort — caption of the pin diagram, only as a further check of the view. Accessed 2026-11-04.

## Cross-check
Source side: NCR, Barco Event Master and University of Oregon agree on all 20 pins.

Sink side: Barco MDSC-8255 and Dell agree on all 20 pins, and the University of Oregon note describes the same reversal: lane 3 on pins 1 and 3, lane 0 on pins 10 and 12.

Disagreements, all small:
- CONFIG1/CONFIG2. NCR and Dell give only the names. Barco Event Master says "connected to Ground". University of Oregon says directly to ground or through a pull-down device. The wider wording is used at the source side.
- UNVERIFIED: whether the same ground rule holds at a sink. Sink-side sources only give the names, so `function` there says only "Configuration pin".
- Spelling: Dell writes ML3(n), Barco ML_Lane 3 (n). Barco's and NCR's form is used. Barco MDSC writes "Hot Plug", the others "Hot Plug Detect".
- The University of Oregon page probably copies an older public table, so I do not count it as an independent witness; NCR and Barco are the two independent sources.

## Choices
- **Variants `source` and `sink` go beyond the catalog schema's list**, which names variants only for rj45. A single source-side list would be wrong by four lanes for anyone wiring a monitor input. The shape is shared, as the catalog schema requires.
- `Return` is `ground`: it is the return of DP_PWR.
- Not stated: how a cable connects the two ends. I read no source that spells out the wiring of a cable.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/data/vga.md`:

`````markdown
# vga — VGA (DE-15) / VGA (DE-15)

Kind: cross-checked reproductions
Pins: 15; types: signal 5, nc 2, ground 5, power 1, data 2

## View
Written for the female connector on a computer or monitor, looking at its mating face (`drawn: socket`): 5 4 3 2 1 on top, 10 9 8 7 6 in the middle shifted half a pitch to the right, 15 14 13 12 11 at the bottom, wide side of the D shell at the top. The male cable connector is the mirror image.

Basis:
- Winford Engineering drawing BRKLD15HDF-SG-DIN rev A ("DB15HD Female Breakout", box "CONNECTOR PINOUT"): text layer `5 1`, `10 6`, `15 11` at the corners of the rows. Rendered and looked at: the middle row is shifted to the right.
- Wikipedia figure VGA_Port.svg, captioned "A female DE-15 socket": I read the coordinates in the SVG file. Top row 5 … 1, middle row 10 … 6 half a pitch further right, bottom row 15 … 11.
- pinouts.ru figures: female the same way, male with 1 … 5 on top and the middle row shifted to the left, which is the mirror image.

## Sources
1. Winford Engineering, drawing BRKLD15HDF-SG-DIN rev A, DB15HD Female Breakout, https://www.bipom.com/documents/peripherals/winford/brkld15hdf-sg-din_rev_a_dwg.pdf — face view with pin numbers. Accessed 2026-11-04.
2. Dell, SE2416H user's guide, page "Pin assignments", read at https://www.manualslib.com/manual/1121260/Dell-Se2416h.html?page=43 — full pin table of a monitor's D-SUB input. Accessed 2026-11-04.
3. Acer, B193 user's guide, page "Connector pin assignment", read at https://www.manualslib.com/manual/451319/Acer-B193.html?page=20 — full pin table. Accessed 2026-11-04.
4. Crypto Museum, D-sub connectors, https://cryptomuseum.com/ref/conn/dsub — DE-15 table. Accessed 2026-11-04.
5. Wikipedia, VGA connector, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VGA_connector, with https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/96/VGA_Port.svg — table with names, figure. Accessed 2026-11-04.
6. pinouts.ru, 15 pin highdensity D-SUB male connector, https://connector.pinouts.ru/15_pin_highdensity_D-SUB_male/ — figures dsubhi15m.gif and dsubhi15f.gif. Accessed 2026-11-04.

## Cross-check
Pins 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 12, 13, 14 and 15 agree in sources 2 to 5 (names differ, signals do not). Pin 10 is a ground in all four.

Disagreements. The pins differ between real devices, so none of them is an error:
- Pin 4: Dell GND, Acer monitor ground, Crypto Museum ID2, Wikipedia ID2/RES.
- Pin 5: Dell self-test, Acer DDC return, Crypto Museum and Wikipedia GND.
- Pin 9: Dell "Computer 5V/3.3V", Acer +5 V, Crypto Museum no pin (key), Wikipedia KEY/PWR (+5 V, once a key).
- Pin 11: Dell GND, Acer monitor ground, Crypto Museum ID0, Wikipedia ID0/RES.

Chosen: the names of the computer-side table (Wikipedia, with Crypto Museum for the ID history) for the number and name, and each variation in the pin `notes` and item `notes`. Dell and Acer describe monitor inputs.

The middle row's direction is confirmed by a maker drawing only for the female part; for the male part it follows from the mirror rule and the pinouts.ru figure.

UNVERIFIED: the VESA DDC standard itself (not free) was not read. Pins 12 and 15 as I²C rest on the sources above.

## Choices
- `drawn: socket`, since that is the part on a device and the part with a maker drawing. rs232_db9 uses `drawn: plug`, because a PC's port is male.
- Pins 4 and 11 are `nc` (reserved). Pin 9 is `power`, with a note that it may be missing.
- Pin 5 is `ground` as the computer-side tables have it, with the monitor variations in its note.
- Red, green and blue are `signal` (analogue).
- `offset` on the middle row because it is drawn from the female side; negative offsets do not exist in the catalog schema.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/data/rj45.md`:

`````markdown
# rj45 — RJ45 (8P8C) / RJ45 (8P8C)

Kind: cross-checked reproductions
Pins: 8; types: data 8 (each variant)

## View
Written for the jack, looking into its opening, with the latch notch at the bottom and the contacts at the top (`drawn: socket`): 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 left to right.

The other view is the plug seen from its tip, latch at the bottom: 8 … 1 left to right. With the plug turned so that the latch is on top, it reads 1 … 8, and `notes` says both, because this is where people go wrong.

Basis, seen in figures (no text states a view):
- Barco Event Master user guide, image A-3 "Ethernet connector" (a device port): notch at the bottom, 1 on the left, 8 on the right.
- pinouts.ru figure rj45f.gif: same.
- L-com drawing TDG1026-8R, jack J1: drawn with the notch at the top, callouts "PIN 8" on the left and "PIN 1" on the right. A half turn gives the same picture.
- pinouts.ru figure rj45m.gif, plug "FRONT": latch at the top, contacts at the bottom, 1 on the left, 8 on the right. This is the half-turned mirror image of the jack, as the two faces require.

- Winford Engineering, PBC8P8C, "8P8C / RJ45 Jack Pinout": notch at the bottom in the rendered face view; the numbers are not drawn by my renderer, but the text layer has 1 before 8, left to right.

**For the drawing:** the view holds only if the `rj45` outline has its notch at the bottom. The catalog schema has no `key` for this outline.

## Sources
1. NetAlly, PoE reference flyer, https://www.netally.com/poe-reference-flyer/ — table "PoE pin/data assignment (PSE perspective)": pin at switch, T568B and T568A colours, Mode B, Mode A, 4-pair mode. Accessed 2026-11-04.
2. Seetronic, RJ45 Color Code: T568A vs T568B Wiring Standards, https://seetronic.com/blog/rj45-color-code-t568a-vs-t568b-wiring-standards/ — pin table of both schemes. Accessed 2026-11-04.
3. Microchip, AN3361, Designing an IEEE 802.3af/at/bt PoE System Based on PD692x0/PD69208, DS00003361C, 2023, table 3-1 "Allowed Polarity" on page 17 and section 3.1, read from a copy at https://file.aichiplink.com/static/microchip/documents/2025-06-20/c38e2cb3d86d8e0f17ecbf4b406e1aeb.pdf — pair colours for 568-A and 568-B, Alternative and Mode terms, polarity options. Accessed 2026-11-04.
4. Barco, Event Master Devices user guide R5905948, A.24 Standard connector pinouts, https://www.barco.com/manuals/R5905948/eriqm1q9ogv8.html — Ethernet table (pin, colour, 10/100 and 1000BASE-T signals) and image A-3. Accessed 2026-11-04.
5. L-com, drawing TDG1026-8R, https://l-com.com/images/downloadables/2D/TDG1026-8R_2D.pdf — jack face with pin callouts. Accessed 2026-11-04.
6. GlobTek, Power over Ethernet (PoE) Mode A vs. Mode B, https://en.globtek.com/technical-articles/power-over-ethernet-poe-mode-a-vs-mode-b — pins and polarity per mode, four pairs above 60 W. Accessed 2026-11-04.
7. L-com, Power over Ethernet white paper, https://l-com.com/images/downloadables/white-papers/Power-Over-Ethernet-White-Paper.pdf — pairs per mode; says polarity is not specified in 802.3af. Accessed 2026-11-04.
8. Y. Darshan (Microsemi), IEEE 802.3bt Task Force contribution darshan_02_0314, March 2014, https://www.ieee802.org/3/bt/public/mar14/darshan_02_0314.pdf — Alternative A pairs 1,2,3,6, Alternative B pairs 4,5,7,8; quotes clause 33.2.3 of IEEE 802.3-2012: not both at once on a link. Accessed 2026-11-04.
9. Wikipedia, Power over Ethernet, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_over_Ethernet — MDI and MDI-X polarity, powered device works with either; only as a further check. Accessed 2026-11-04.
10. pinouts.ru, 8 pin RJ45 (8P8C) male connector, https://connector.pinouts.ru/8_pin_RJ45_8P8C_male/ — figures only. Accessed 2026-11-04.
11. Winford Engineering, PBC8P8C physical layout, https://www.bipom.com/documents/peripherals/winford/pbc8p8c_layout.pdf — jack face. Accessed 2026-11-04.

## Cross-check
Colours: NetAlly and Seetronic agree on every pin of both schemes. Microchip's pair colours and Barco's T568A-pattern table agree. TIA-568 itself is paywalled and was not read.

Signals: Barco names 1000BASE-T as TX0+, TX0-, RX0+, TX1+, TX1-, RX0-, RX1+, RX1-; NetAlly as TxRx A+, A-, B+, C+, C-, B-, D+, D-. Same pins and pairing, the letters of NetAlly are used. On 10/100BASE-T, Barco (a device) has TXD on 1, 2 and RXD on 3, 6; NetAlly (a switch) has Rx on 1, 2 and Tx on 3, 6. They agree once the side is taken into account; `notes` says so.

PoE pairs: NetAlly, GlobTek, L-com, Microchip and the IEEE contribution all agree: 1,2,3,6 and 4,5,7,8.

Disagreement, polarity: NetAlly and GlobTek give pins 1, 2 DC+ and pins 3, 6 DC-. Microchip's table for Type 4 gives pins 1, 2 negative and 3, 6 positive, with several options for Type 3. L-com says polarity is not specified in 802.3af, and Wikipedia says the data pairs change polarity between MDI and MDI-X. So I state no polarity, only which pins form one pole, and warn in `notes`. Pins 4, 5 positive and 7, 8 negative is what NetAlly, GlobTek and Microchip's Type 4 column share, but Type 3 allows the swap, so that stays out too.

Words: the IEEE contribution and Microchip use "Alternative" at the power source and "Mode" at the powered device; NetAlly and GlobTek use "Mode" for both. `notes` uses Mode, as asked for and most searched.

## Choices
- Names combine the 10/100 and 1000BASE-T terms, "TX+ / A+" and so on, within 24 characters. The catalog schema's sample says "TX+".
- All pins are `data`; PoE does not change the type.
- The same pin notes in both variants. Wire colours are the only difference, as both colour sources show.
- No crossover cable table: not part of this item.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/data/rs232_db9.md`:

`````markdown
# rs232_db9 — RS-232 (DE-9) / RS-232 (DE-9)

Kind: cross-checked reproductions
Pins: 9; types: signal 6, data 2, ground 1

## View
Written for the male connector, looking at its pins (`drawn: plug`): 1 2 3 4 5 on top, 6 7 8 9 below shifted half a pitch to the right, wide side of the D shell at the top.

Basis, quotes from the text of the sources:
- serial_pinout.txt: the drawing is labelled "Looking at pins on male connector" and shows `\1 2 3 4 5/` above `\6 7 8 9/`. It adds that on a female connector the numbers run right to left, starting with 1 in the upper right corner.
- CS Club Waterloo wiki: male "1 2 3 4 5" over "6 7 8 9", female "5 4 3 2 1" over "9 8 7 6".

The female order is exactly the mirror image the catalog schema's other view produces.

## Sources
1. Texas Instruments, SLLA037A, Interface Circuits for TIA/EIA-232-F, https://www.ti.com/lit/an/slla037a/slla037a.pdf — section "The DB9S Connector", figure 6, and the description of each signal with who drives it; which side is male and which female. Accessed 2026-11-04.
2. Moxa, NPort 6110 user's manual, Pin assignments, read at https://www.manualsdir.com/manuals/124486/moxa-technologies-6110.html?page=47 — RS-232 "DB9 male" table. Accessed 2026-11-04.
3. Crypto Museum, D-sub connectors, https://cryptomuseum.com/ref/conn/dsub — plug usually DTE, socket usually DCE, with exceptions. Accessed 2026-11-04.
4. File serial_pinout.txt in the xmtel archive, University of Louisville (no author named in the file), https://www.astro.louisville.edu/software/xmtel/archive/xmtel-indi-6.0/xmtel-6.0l/support/serial/serial_pinout.txt — view, pins, direction out of or into the PC. Accessed 2026-11-04.
5. CS Club, University of Waterloo, Serial Pin-outs, https://wiki.csclub.uwaterloo.ca/Serial_Pin-outs — male and female layouts, RS-232 over DE-9 table. Accessed 2026-11-04.

## Cross-check
TI, Moxa, serial_pinout.txt and CS Club agree on pins 1 to 8. TI, serial_pinout.txt and CS Club also agree on pin 9 (RI). Crypto Museum was used only for the male and female rule.

Directions: TI says for each signal who turns it on (DCE for DCD, DSR, CTS, RI; DTE for RTS, DTR; TD from DTE to DCE). serial_pinout.txt gives the same as arrows out of or into the PC. RD going into the DTE is only implicit in TI and explicit in serial_pinout.txt.

Disagreements:
- Moxa's table has pin 9 "Not assigned": that is that product, which has no RI. RI chosen.
- TI's figure 6 writes "RST" for pin 7, while its text says "Request to Send (RTS)". A typo in TI; RTS chosen.
- TI writes RD/TD, Moxa RxD/TxD, others RXD/TXD. The catalog schema's RXD/TXD is used.
- TI describes the genders by casing and contacts together: at the DTE a female casing with male contacts, at the DCE the reverse. Same meaning as "male pins at the DTE", but a reader looking at the casing could read it the other way round, so `doc` speaks of pins and sockets.

UNVERIFIED: TIA-232-F and TIA-574 themselves are paywalled and were not read.

## Choices
- `drawn: plug`, as in the catalog schema's example and because a PC's port is male.
- Direction is in `function`, for both ends.
- The note on crossing TXD and RXD between two DTEs is a consequence of the direction table. I name no specific null-modem wiring, because the handshake lines vary.
- The closing remark on levels stays general; TI's document covers the voltages, I give no numbers here.
- Connector name DE-9 in the title, DB9 in `doc` and in the tags, because most people search for that.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/audio/audio_trs.md`:

`````markdown
# audio_trs — 3.5 mm stereo jack (TRS) / 3,5-mm-Stereoklinke (TRS)

Kind: cross-checked reproductions
Pins: 3; types: signal 2, ground 1

## View
The catalog schema's `jack` shape: a plug from the side, tip at the left, segments from tip to sleeve. It has one fixed view, so no mirror question arises. TI's table 2 draws the same order on a plug photo labelled tip, ring, sleeve.

## Sources
1. Texas Instruments, TS3A225E datasheet, SCDS329A, August 2012, revised May 2013, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ts3a225e.pdf — table 2 "Headset Configuration", page 21: Tip Audio Left, Ring Audio Right, Sleeve Ground, accessed 2026-11-04
2. Rane Corporation, Rane Note 102, "Analog I/O Standards", https://www.ranecommercial.com/legacy/pdf/old/note102.pdf — section on phone jacks: "Tip = Left Positive", "Ring = Right Positive", "Sleeve = Common Ground" for jacks made for headphones, and the balanced wiring tip positive, ring negative, sleeve ground, accessed 2026-11-04
3. Wikipedia, "Phone connector (audio)", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phone_connector_(audio) — stereo and balanced assignment of tip, ring, sleeve, accessed 2026-11-04

## Cross-check
TI (a chip maker) and Rane (an audio equipment maker) are independent and agree on left, right and ground. Rane writes about 1/4-inch jacks, TI about 3.5 mm jacks; the assignment is the same. No disagreement. No free standard was reached; the convention is reproduced by these sources.

## Choices
- `name` L, R, GND: short forms of what the sources call Audio Left, Audio Right, Ground.
- `signal` for L and R and `ground` for the sleeve, as the catalog schema says.
- No `wire`: no source names colours for a stereo plug.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/audio/audio_trrs.md`:

`````markdown
# audio_trrs — 3.5 mm headset jack (TRRS) / 3,5-mm-Headset-Klinke (TRRS)

Kind: cross-checked reproductions
Pins: 4; variants: ctia, omtp; types in each variant: signal 3, ground 1

## View
The catalog schema's `jack` shape: a plug from the side, tip at the left, segments from tip to sleeve (T, R1, R2, S). One fixed view, no mirror question.

## Sources
1. Android Open Source Project, "3.5 mm headset: Accessory specification", https://source.android.com/docs/core/interaction/accessories/headset/plug-headset-spec — mechanical table: "CTIA pinout order (LRGM)" required, except in regions with legal requirements for OMTP; "OMTP pinout order (LRMG)" optional, accessed 2026-11-04
2. Android Open Source Project, "3.5 mm headset jack: Device specification", https://source.android.com/docs/core/interaction/accessories/headset/jack-headset-spec — same two orders for the jack; the OMTP circuit note says to switch the MIC and GND segments, accessed 2026-11-04
3. Texas Instruments, TS3A225E datasheet, SCDS329A, August 2012, revised May 2013, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ts3a225e.pdf — section "Application Information" and table 2, page 21: Standard (CTIA) Tip Left, Ring 1 Right, Ring 2 Ground, Sleeve Microphone; text: the GND and microphone bands are switched between the two, accessed 2026-11-04
4. Wikipedia, "Phone connector (audio)", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phone_connector_(audio) — OMTP has ground on the sleeve and the microphone on the second ring; CTIA/AHJ reverses these, accessed 2026-11-04
5. Electronic Specifier, product note on the Fairchild FSA8049, https://www.electronicspecifier.com/products/passives/fsa8049-fairchild-semiconductors-audio-jack-detection-switch — names "L/R/M/G" for OMTP and "L/R/G/M" for CTIA, accessed 2026-11-04

## Cross-check
All agree on the swap. **One disagreement inside a source:** TI's table 2 repeats the Standard rows for OMTP ("Ring 2 Audio Right", "Ring 2 Ground", "Sleeve Microphone"). That is a copy error: TI's own text says the bands are switched, and its OMTP band diagram reads G M R L from the sleeve end. I use the diagram and text, in line with Android and Wikipedia. The OMTP spot checks therefore cite Android, Wikipedia and TI's diagram, not TI's rows.

The Android pages give only the letter orders and do not say that they run from tip to sleeve; TI's Standard rows settle that reading.

## Choices
- Variant name `CTIA (AHJ)`: TI calls the same order "Standard", Wikipedia "CTIA/AHJ".
- `signal` for MIC, as the catalog schema's "everything else that is one defined signal".
- No `wire`: no source names colours.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/audio/xlr.md`:

`````markdown
# xlr — XLR 3-pin / XLR 3-polig

Kind: cross-checked reproductions
Pins: 3; types: ground 1, signal 2

## View
Written for the male connector, looking at its mating face (`drawn: plug`), rotated so that pin 3 is straight below the centre.

Angles (clockwise from 12 o'clock, male face): **pin 1 = 270°, pin 2 = 90°, pin 3 = 180°, radius 0.5; key = 0° (the latch).** The female face follows from the mirror rule: pin 1 = 90°, pin 2 = 270°, key = 0°. The polarising rib sits at 45° on the male face and at 315° on the female face.

Derivation:
- Neutrik drawing ST-NC3MAH, front view of the male receptacle: 1 at the left, 2 at the right, 3 below the centre, with the latch cut-out at 12 o'clock. Measured on the rendered drawing from the centre: pin 1 is 104 px left, pin 2 is 103 px right, pin 3 is 100 px below, all on the level of the centre lines. So the pattern is a T with equal radii, not a 120-degree triangle.
- Neutrik drawing 3102 St 18 19, front view of the female NC3FAV1, "PUSH" latch on top: 2 at the left, 1 at the right, 3 below. This is exactly the mirror image. The same sheet's rear view shows 1 left, 2 right, and its "PCB-Layout (component side)" shows 2 and "1+G".
- Amphenol, "AX Series Contact Arrangements (Front view of pin inserts)": 1 left, 2 right, 3 below, all three at the same distance from the centre.
- ITT Cannon, the originator of the XLR, "Contact Arrangement Configuration (Engaging View Pin Insert)": the same pattern, without readable numbers at this print quality.
- Key: Amphenol and ITT Cannon draw a small rib on the rim of the pin insert at the upper right. Measured at 45° on both Amphenol's figure (95 px right, 95 px up) and Neutrik's male drawing (143 px, 145 px). Neutrik's female drawing has it at the upper left, at 315°.
- Radius: 104 px of an inner radius of about 200 px on ST-NC3MAH, 70 of 137 px on Amphenol's figure, so 0.5.

## Sources
1. Neutrik, drawing ST-NC3MAH, "XLR Chassis Connectors NC3MAH", copy at https://pdf2.datasheet.su/neutrik/nc3mah.pdf — front view of the male connector, pin numbers and key position, accessed 2026-11-04
2. Neutrik, product page and drawing 3102 St 18 19, NC3FAV1, copy at https://pdf2.datasheet.su/neutrik/nc3fav1.pdf — front and rear view of the female connector, PCB layout, latch position, accessed 2026-11-04
3. Amphenol Australia, Entertainment Interconnect Catalogue, "Standard Data AX Series Cable Connectors" (page 7, Rev 2, 11/2009), copy at https://allchip.ru/content/pdfs/142/4573652.pdf — front view of pin inserts with numbers and key, accessed 2026-11-04
4. ITT Cannon, Audio XL catalogue, "XLR Series" (page 8), copy at https://radel.ru/upload/iblock/e44/8o3rfdvnh0bl7u3qrdvbzn6o0edrp67t.pdf — engaging view of the pin insert, pattern and key, no readable numbers, accessed 2026-11-04
5. Rane Corporation, Rane Note 102, "Analog I/O Standards", https://www.ranecommercial.com/legacy/pdf/old/note102.pdf — pin functions: "Pin 1 Ground (Shield, screen, etc.)", "Pin 2 Positive", "Pin 3 Negative", per IEC 268, with AES14-1992 agreeing, accessed 2026-11-04
6. Shure, SM58 user guide, https://pubs.shure.com/view/guide/SM58/en-US.pdf — three-pin XLR male connector, positive pressure gives positive voltage on pin 2 with respect to pin 3, accessed 2026-11-04
7. Mackie, 1620 manual, appendix B "Connections", https://www.manualslib.com/manual/97163/Mackie-1620.html?page=23 — "Pin 1 = Shield", "Pin 2 = Hot (+)", "Pin 3 = Cold", accessed 2026-11-04

## Cross-check
Functions: Rane, Shure and Mackie agree. Geometry: Neutrik and Amphenol agree, and Neutrik's male and female drawings are mirror images of each other.

AES14 itself was not read: the AES preview page answered 403, and the standard is not free. Its content here comes only through Rane's statement. Rane calls "European" and "American" wiring a myth, but also says many makers do not follow the standard, so the notes tell the reader to check old equipment.

**A correction worth keeping:** I first expected 2 at the left and 1 at the right on the male face, and an equal triangle. That is the female face. The drawings decide.

## Choices
- Only one angle fits `key`. The catalog gives the latch at 12 o'clock (0°), the feature people orient the connector by. The polarising rib (45° on the male face) is named in `notes`.
- `Cold (-)` uses a plain hyphen, as a pin name people type.
- `signal` for pins 2 and 3: analogue audio, as in the catalog schema.
- No `wire`: cable colours are not fixed by these sources.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/audio/midi.md`:

`````markdown
# midi — MIDI (DIN-5, 180°) / MIDI (DIN-5, 180°)

Kind: free official specification
Pins: 5; types: nc 2, ground 1, data 2

## View
Written for the female device jack, looking at its mating face from the front (`drawn: socket`), notch at 12 o'clock.

Angles (clockwise from 12 o'clock, jack face): **pin 1 = 90°, pin 4 = 135°, pin 2 = 180°, pin 5 = 225°, pin 3 = 270°, radius 0.53; key = 0°.** The plug face follows from the mirror rule: pin 1 = 270°, pin 4 = 225°, pin 2 = 180°, pin 5 = 135°, pin 3 = 90°.

Derivation:
- binder catalogue, series 423/723, page 34, "5 pol Stereo (DIN 41524)", with coordinates in mm. "Buchseneinsatz (Steckseite) / Female insert (mating side)": 1 (-3.50, 0), 2 (0, 3.50), 3 (3.50, 0), 4 (-2.47, 2.47), 5 (2.47, 2.47). "Stifteinsatz (Steckseite) / Male insert (mating side)": 1 (3.50, 0), 2 (0, 3.50), 3 (-3.50, 0), 4 (2.47, 2.47), 5 (-2.47, 2.47). The notch is at the bottom. Turned by 180° (a rotation, no mirror) the female values give the angles above.
- Switchcraft catalogue: the arrangement drawings for 5 pins at 180° (pin arrangement 5, contact arrangement F) have the notch at 12 o'clock and the contacts in the lower half; I keep that orientation. The "Recommended PC board layout (component side)" of the 57PC5F, the part family CA-033 names, shows the tails labelled in the order (1), 4, 2, 5, 3 from the top of the drawing to the bottom with the panel to the right. Seen from the front of the panel, the top of that drawing is on the viewer's right. So pin 1 is on the right of the jack's front face, which agrees with binder. (The digit 1 itself is not legible in the print; the other four are.)
- Radius: 3.5 mm (binder; Switchcraft: pin circle 7.00 mm) of a 6.6 mm shell radius (Switchcraft: 13.20 mm), so 0.53.

**The common mistake:** CA-033 figures 1 and 2 draw the jack with 1 at the left and 3 at the right, and figure 3 uses the same handedness for the plugs. CA-033 does not name the view. It matches the plug's mating face and the jack's solder side, and it does not match the jack's mating face. Taken for the front of a jack, it would be mirrored.

## Sources
1. MMA/AMEI, CA-033, "MIDI 1.0 Electrical Specification Update [2014]", copy on the MIDI Association site, https://midi.org/wp-content/uploads/wpforo/default_attachments/1709416667-ca33-MIDI-10-Electrical-Specification-Update.pdf — jacks and cable: "DIN 5-pin (180 degree) female panel-mount", pins 1 and 3 unused, pin 2 grounded at the transmitter only, current loop and figures 1 to 3, accessed 2026-11-04
2. binder, catalogue M16 IP 67, "Miniatursteckverbinder Serie 423 - 723" contact arrangements (page 34), copy at https://static.chipdip.ru/lib/959/DOC027959862.pdf — coordinates of male and female inserts, each labelled mating side, accessed 2026-11-04
3. Switchcraft, catalogue pages 46 to 49, "DIN connectors and plugs" and "DIN receptacles", copy at https://assets.sourcengine.com/datasheets/80db8068-6e03-493b-82e0-1ecaa5f26323.pdf — arrangement drawings and the 57PC5F board layout, accessed 2026-11-04

## Cross-check
One free official specification is enough for the functions. For the geometry, binder and Switchcraft are independent and agree. I found no disagreement in what I read. Pages that assign pin 4 as sink at MIDI Out were seen only as search excerpts and not used; CA-033 figure 1 is clear that pin 4 goes to VTX through RA and pin 5 to the UART through RC.

## Choices
- The MIDI spec gives pins 4 and 5 no names. `Loop +` and `Loop -` are mine: the current flows from pin 4 through the receiver's opto-isolator back to pin 5 (figure 2).
- `N/C` is how CA-033 writes it. CA-033 adds that a cable may have wires on pins 1 and 3.
- `data` for pins 4 and 5: a serial data line.
- `ground` for pin 2: a shield. At MIDI In it is not grounded; the function and the notes say so.
- Item names are the same in all locales: MIDI and DIN are proper names, and there is no generic word in the name.
`````

```yaml
  doc: {en: "Extra 12 V supply of a graphics card, up to 75 W. Ein Stecker im Raster 4,2 mm mit zwei Dreierreihen; die Rastnase sitzt an der Reihe mit den Pins 4 bis 6 und ist oben gezeichnet."}
  notes: {en: "In an 8-pin header this plug reaches pins 1 to 3 and 5 to 7, so its sense pin meets Sense0 and Sense1 stays open: the card then draws at most 75 W. Some older cables leave pin 2 unconnected.", de: "In einer 8-poligen Stiftleiste erreicht dieser Stecker die Pins 1 bis 3 und 5 bis 7. Sein Sense-Pin trifft auf Sense0, Sense1 bleibt offen: Die Karte zieht dann höchstens 75 W. Manche älteren Kabel lassen Pin 2 unbelegt."}

  doc: {en: "Seven contacts in a single row at 1.27 mm pitch: three grounds around two differential pairs. The L-shaped key sits at the S7 end and is drawn at the bottom.", de: "Sieben Kontakte in einer Reihe im Raster 1,27 mm: drei Massen um zwei differenzielle Paare. Der L-förmige Kodiersteg sitzt am Ende bei S7 und ist unten gezeichnet."}
  notes: {en: "Both ends of a data cable are the same and either may go to the drive or the host. On a drive the data contacts continue the row of the power contacts: S1 to S7, a gap, then P1 to P15.", de: "Beide Enden eines Datenkabels sind gleich, jedes darf ans Laufwerk oder an den Host. Am Laufwerk setzt sich die Reihe der Datenkontakte in den Stromkontakten fort: S1 bis S7, eine Lücke, dann P1 bis P15."}

  kind: pinout

  group: pc_power
  name: {cs: "Napájení SATA, 15 pinů", da: "SATA-strøm, 15-polet", de: "SATA-Strom, 15-polig", el: "Τροφοδοσία SATA, 15 ακίδων", en: "SATA power, 15-pin", es: "Alimentación SATA, 15 pines", fr: "Alimentation SATA, 15 broches", hi: "SATA पावर, 15-पिन", it: "Alimentazione SATA, 15 pin", ja: "SATA 電源 15 ピン", nl: "SATA-voeding, 15-polig", "no": "SATA-strøm, 15-polet", pl: "Zasilanie SATA, 15-pinowe", pt: "Alimentação SATA, 15 pinos", sv: "SATA-ström, 15-polig", zh: "SATA 电源 15 针"}
  doc: {en: "Fifteen contacts in a single row at 1.27 mm pitch, three each for +3.3 V, ground, +5 V, ground and +12 V. The L-shaped key sits at the P1 end and is drawn at the bottom.", de: "Fünfzehn Kontakte in einer Reihe im Raster 1,27 mm, je drei für +3,3 V, Masse, +5 V, Masse und +12 V. Der L-förmige Kodiersteg sitzt am Ende bei P1 und ist unten gezeichnet."}
  notes: {en: "Five wires feed the fifteen contacts, so wire numbers and contact numbers are not the same. The SATA specification has retired +3.3 V on P1 to P3, but some power supplies still deliver it, which matters for drives with the Power Disable feature on P3.", de: "Fünf Adern versorgen die fünfzehn Kontakte, Adernummern und Kontaktnummern sind also nicht gleich. Die SATA-Spezifikation hat +3,3 V auf P1 bis P3 gestrichen, manche Netzteile liefern sie aber weiter. Das ist wichtig für Laufwerke mit Power Disable auf P3."}
  tags: ["sata", "serial ata", "power", "strom", "15-pin", "15-polig", "hdd", "ssd", "festplatte", "hard disk", "psu", "netzteil", "power disable", "pwdis", "staggered spin-up", "das", "dss", "3.3v", "5v", "12v"]
  source: "SATA-IO Technical Proposal TP 037 v1.1, table 1; Seagate BarraCuda Product Manual 100817550 Rev. L, table 5; Intel ATX Version 3 Multi Rail Desktop Platform Power Supply Design Guide (336521) Rev. 2.1a, table 5-10 and figure 5-2; Western Digital tech brief, Power Disable Feature"

  pins:

    - {number: "P2", name: "V33", function: {en: "3.3 V supply (retired)", de: "3,3-V-Versorgung (gestrichen)"}, type: power, wire: orange}
```
