`````markdown
# arduino_uno — Arduino Uno R3 headers / Arduino Uno R3 Stiftleisten

Kind: authoritative maker document
Pins: 38; types: power 5; ground 4; signal 3; data 3; io 22; nc 1

## View
Board from the component side, portrait, USB at the top, as `connector: top`. Basis: Arduino's UNO R3 Full Pinout (A000066) page 1 is captioned "TOP VIEW" and I rendered and looked at it: USB and DC jack at the top edge, header POWER/AD on the left, IOH/IOL on the right, from top to bottom NC … VIN, gap, A0 … A5 and D19/SCL … D8, gap, D7 … D0/RX. The YAML lists are read straight from that figure.

ICSP block: same figure family, page 4, also "TOP VIEW", with numbered circles around the header at the bottom of the board: upper row 5 3 1, lower row 6 4 2 (zoomed render checked). So pin 1 is at the upper right in this orientation, which is what the `inner` rows state.

Position along the edge: in the figure both columns end level at the bottom (A5 and D0/RX), and the left column starts about 3.6 pitches lower than the right one, with NC about level with D13. So the left list starts with four `null`, which puts NC beside D13 and A5 beside D0.

Header numbers: the schematic's header names POWER, AD, IOH, IOL, ICSP plus the position printed there. POWER and AD count from the top of the left side; IOH and IOL have pin 1 at the D8 and D0 end, which is why the right list runs 10…1 and 8…1. The label at each schematic position (for example IOH pin 6 = 13, IOL pin 1 = 0) ties the numbers to the figure's names.

## Sources
1. Arduino, UNO R3 Full Pinout, SKU A000066, last update 6 Oct 2022, https://docs.arduino.cc/resources/pinouts/A000066-full-pinout.pdf — pages 1, 3 (advanced functions, read as text) and 4 (ICSP) rendered and read, accessed 2026-11-04
2. Arduino, UNO-TH_Rev3e schematic (Arduino(TM) UNO Rev3, dated 06/03/19), https://docs.arduino.cc/resources/schematics/A000066-schematics.pdf — header names, positions and nets, rendered and zoomed, accessed 2026-11-04
3. Arduino, UNO R3 datasheet (user manual), SKU A000066, modified 03/11/2026, https://docs.arduino.cc/resources/datasheets/A000066-datasheet.pdf — sections 2.2, 5.1, 5.2, accessed 2026-11-04

## Cross-check
Schematic and full pinout agree on every pin. Differences:
- The datasheet's section 5 numbers the pins differently (JANALOG 1–14, JDIGITAL 1–18). Its D-numbers match, but it writes "A4/SD4" and "A5/SD5" for pins 17 and 18 (typos for SDA/SCL). I use the schematic's header names as planned.
- The datasheet types +3V3, +5V and VIN as "Power", and IOREF as its own type. The catalog schema has no such type; I use `power` because the schematic ties it to +5V.
- The datasheet's section 3.2 says "up to 20 MHz" for the processor; not used here.
- The schematic calls the SPI pins MISO/MOSI, the full pinout CIPO/COPI and says these are the former names. Name follows the full pinout; the old names are in `function` and in the tags.
- The VIN range 6–20 V stands in both the full pinout's legend and the datasheet's table 2.2. No UNVERIFIED pin.

## Choices
- Names: `3V3` and `5V` for the pinout's `+3V3` and `+5V`, as planned; the plain D-numbers for `D1/TX`, `~D3` and so on, with TX, RX and PWM in `function`.
- IOH.9 and IOH.10 are named `SDA` and `SCL`, type `io`: the full pinout calls them D18/SDA and D19/SCL and they are the same nets as A4 and A5.
- AREF is `signal`, IOREF is `power`, NC is `nc`.
- The gaps: one `null` between VIN and A0 and one between D8 and D7. In the figure the D8/D7 spacing is about 1.6 pitches and the VIN/A0 spacing about 2; the catalog schema only knows whole pitches, so D7 … D0 sit about half a pitch lower in the drawing than to scale.
- Only the ICSP header of the ATmega328P is an `inner` block, as planned. ICSP1 of the ATmega16U2 is named in the notes, not drawn, because its pins would add six more rows for a header that very few people need.
- The optional 2x2 JP2 pads are left out.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/boards/arduino_nano.md`:

`````markdown
# arduino_nano — Arduino Nano headers / Arduino Nano Stiftleisten

Kind: authoritative maker document
Pins: 36; types: power 4; ground 3; signal 6; data 3; io 20

## View
Board from the component side, portrait, USB at the top, as `connector: top`. Basis: Arduino's Nano Full Pinout (A000005) page 1, rendered and read: the Mini-B connector is at the top edge and the MCU and reset button are visible, so it is the component side (page 3 draws the other side separately and captions it "BOTTOM"). Left column top to bottom: D13, +3V3, AREF, A0 … A7, +5V, RESET, GND, VIN. Right column: D12, ~D11 … D2, GND, RESET, D0/RX, D1/TX. The two square pads in the figure are at VIN and D1/TX.

Numbers: the schematic's J1 runs 1 D1/TX, 2 D0/RX, 3 RESET, 4 GND, 5 D2 … 15 D12/MISO; J2 runs 1 VIN, 2 GND, 3 RESET, 4 +5V, 5 A7 … 12 A0, 13 AREF, 14 3V3, 15 D13/SCK. Pin 1 of each is the square pad of the figure, which fixes the lists as J2.15…J2.1 on the left and J1.15…J1.1 on the right.

ICSP block: page 3, left picture (component side, USB at the top), zoom checked: upper row 2 4 6, lower row 1 3 5.

## Sources
1. Arduino, Nano Full Pinout, SKU A000005, last update 30/06/2021, https://docs.arduino.cc/resources/pinouts/A000005-full-pinout.pdf — pages 1 to 3 rendered and read, accessed 2026-11-04
2. Arduino, NanoV3.3 schematic (dated 23/01/19), https://docs.arduino.cc/resources/schematics/A000005-schematics.pdf — J1, J2, J4 (ICSP), rendered and zoomed, accessed 2026-11-04
3. Arduino, Nano datasheet, SKU A000005, modified 03/11/2026, https://docs.arduino.cc/resources/datasheets/A000005-datasheet.pdf — features and section 5, accessed 2026-11-04

## Cross-check
Schematic and full pinout agree on every pin. Differences, all in the datasheet:
- Section 5.1 lists only 13 analog-side pins (no D13, no AREF) and numbers two of them 12; section 5.2 lists D1 … D13, Reset, GND. Not usable for numbering, so J1 and J2 come from the schematic.
- Section 5.1 calls A6 and A7 "Analog input … /GPIO". The full pinout draws them as analog only with no digital number, and the schematic wires them to ADC6 and ADC7 of the MCU. I chose analog only, type `signal`.
- Its features say "7-15V unregulated external power supply (pin 30)", the full pinout says "VIN 7-12 V input to the board". `function` uses the narrower 7–12 V; the notes give both.
- Its "pin 27" and "pin 30" are the old count around the board. Both match J2.4 and J2.1 if that count continues from J1 (1–15) back along J2 (30 = J2.1); I state only these two in the notes because they are what the document names.
No UNVERIFIED pin.

## Choices
- Classic Nano with ATmega328 (schematic NanoV3.3). Clones are not covered; nothing in the sources speaks about them.
- A6 and A7 are `signal`, not `io`: the catalog schema lists A0–A5 as `io`, and these two can only be read as analog.
- `ICSP.n` for the schematic's J4 (titled ICSP there), so that the label in the drawing and the number agree.
- Names as on the pinout, shortened as planned (`D1` for `D1/TX`, `3V3` for `+3V3`); TX and RX stand in `function`.
- J2.14 "output of the FT232RL": the schematic's 3V3 net comes from pin 17 (3V3OUT) of IC1. The 50 mA limit is in the pinout's legend.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/boards/esp32_devkitc.md`:

`````markdown
# esp32_devkitc — ESP32-DevKitC V4 headers / ESP32-DevKitC V4 Stiftleisten

Kind: authoritative maker document
Pins: 38; types: power 2; ground 3; signal 1; data 6; io 26

## View
Board from the component side, portrait, Micro-USB at the top (`connector: top`, as planned), which is Espressif's figure turned by 180°. Basis:
- Espressif's pin layout figure (`esp32_devkitC_v4_pinlayout.png`, downloaded and looked at) shows the module and antenna at the top and the USB socket at the bottom, with pin labels printed beside the pins: left top to bottom 3V3, EN, VP, VN, 34, 35, 32, 33, 25, 26, 27, 14, 12, GND, 13, D2, D3, CMD, 5V; right top to bottom GND, 23, 22, TX, RX, 21, GND, 19, 18, 5, 17, 16, 4, 0, 2, 15, D1, D0, CLK.
- These two orders are exactly tables J2 and J3 of the guide, and the schematic's J2 and J3 (pins 1–19, zoomed render).
- Espressif's photo (`esp32-devkitc-v4-functional-overview.png`) shows the real board's silk: USB left, antenna right; upper row from the USB end 5V, CMD, D3 …, 3V3; lower row from the USB end CLK, D0, D1, 15 …, GND. Turned so that USB points up, the lower row becomes the left column and the upper row the right one.

Turning by 180° gives the lists: left J3.19 (CLK) … J3.1 (GND), right J2.19 (5V) … J2.1 (3V3). A rotation, not a mirror: the module side stays towards the viewer.

## Sources
1. Espressif, ESP32-DevKitC V4 User Guide (esp-dev-kits, latest), https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-dev-kits/en/latest/esp32/esp32-devkitc/user_guide.html — tables J2 and J3, notes on flash and GPIO16/17, power warning, accessed 2026-11-04
2. Espressif, pin layout figure of that guide, https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-dev-kits/en/latest/esp32/_images/esp32_devkitC_v4_pinlayout.png — positions, input-only marks, strapping marks, SPI and Arduino functions, accessed 2026-11-04
3. Espressif, functional overview photo of that guide, https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-dev-kits/en/latest/esp32/_images/esp32-devkitc-v4-functional-overview.png — silk screen and orientation, accessed 2026-11-04
4. Espressif, ESP32_DevKitc_V4 schematic (Dec 2017), https://dl.espressif.com/dl/schematics/esp32_devkitc_v4-sch.pdf — connectors J2 and J3, accessed 2026-11-04
5. Espressif, ESP32 Series Datasheet v5.3, https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/esp32_datasheet_en.pdf — section 2 pin overview, section 3 strapping pins (tables 3-1, 3-3, 3-4, section 3.2), table 5-3 VIH, accessed 2026-11-04

## Cross-check
Guide tables, figure and schematic agree on all 38 pins. Details:
- The guide's text does not call any pin strapping or input-only. Input-only comes from the figure's arrows and the type `I` in the tables; strapping pins come from the datasheet's section 3 (GPIO0, GPIO2, MTDI = GPIO12, MTDO = GPIO15, GPIO5).
- The figure gives STRAP labels to GPIO0, GPIO12, GPIO15 and GPIO5 but none to GPIO2. The datasheet lists GPIO2 as strapping (boot mode), so I mark it.
- The figure labels GPIO12 as `VDD_FLASH`, GPIO15 as `LOG` and GPIO5 as `SDIO`, matching the datasheet's 3.2, 3.3 and 3.4.
- The guide says D0–D3, CMD, CLK "may disrupt" flash access; the figure says they cannot be used as regular GPIO. The notes use the figure's stricter wording.
- UART2 on GPIO16/17 is from the datasheet's pin list, not from the guide.
- The Arduino I2C names (`WIRE_SDA`, `WIRE_SCL`) and `VSPI`/`HSPI` come from the figure. I2C has no fixed hardware pin on the chip, so `function` says "in the Arduino core".
No UNVERIFIED pin.

## Choices
- `connector: top` as planned, although Espressif draws the board with USB at the bottom; the doc text says so, because a reader comparing with Espressif's picture will see it turned.
- Names are `GPIOnn` for every GPIO as planned, so GPIO36 instead of the silk `VP`, GPIO1 instead of `TX`, GPIO9 instead of `D2`. The silk label stands in `function`.
- GPIO6–GPIO11 are type `data`, not `io`: Espressif's table calls them I/O, but the lines are the SPI flash bus and a user scanning for free (green) pins must not take them. The catalog schema's `data` covers bus lines.
- GPIO16 and GPIO17 stay `io` with a note, because they are free on WROOM boards.
- The drawing covers the V4 with any of the listed modules (WROOM-32E/UE, WROVER-E/IE); the WROVER difference is GPIO16/17.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/boards/esp8266_nodemcu.md`:

`````markdown
# esp8266_nodemcu — NodeMCU DevKit 1.0 headers / NodeMCU DevKit 1.0 Stiftleisten

Kind: authoritative maker document
Pins: 30; types: power 4; ground 4; signal 3; data 4; io 13; nc 2

## View
Board from the component side, portrait, Micro-USB at the top (`connector: top`, as planned), which is the project's pin map turned by 180°. Basis:
- The pin map `NODEMCU_DEVKIT_V1.0_PINMAP.png` (downloaded and looked at) shows the board with the chamfered antenna end up: left column A0, RSV, RSV, SD3, SD2, SD1, CMD, SD0, CLK, GND, 3V3, EN, RST, GND, Vin; right column D0, D1, D2, D3, D4, 3V3, GND, D5, D6, D7, D8, D9, D10, GND, 3V3. Both orders equal J1 and J2 of the schematic's IO CONN sheet, pin 1 at the antenna end.
- The figure itself does not state the side. The photo `NodeMCU_DEVKIT_1.0.jpg` in the same repository settles it: with the ESP-12 module facing the camera and the antenna end up, the silk RSV, RSV, SD3, SD2, SD1, CMD, SD0, CLK, GND, 3V, EN … is on the left and … D5, D6, D7, D8, RX, TX, GND, 3V on the right, so the pin map is the component side. I zoomed into both rows.

Turning by 180° gives: left J2.15 (3V3) … J2.1 (D0), right J1.15 (VIN) … J1.1 (A0). A rotation, not a mirror.

Revision drawn: NodeMCU DEVKIT V1.0 (`NODEMCU_DEVKIT_V1.0.PDF`), ESP-12E core, per the repository README.

## Sources
1. NodeMCU team, `NODEMCU_DEVKIT_V1.0.PDF` schematic, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodemcu/nodemcu-devkit-v1.0/master/NODEMCU_DEVKIT_V1.0.PDF — sheets ESP-12 CORE, IO CONN, KEY, ADC rendered and read, accessed 2026-11-04
2. NodeMCU team, pin map, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodemcu/nodemcu-devkit-v1.0/master/Documents/NODEMCU_DEVKIT_V1.0_PINMAP.png, and the same map in `NODEMCU-DEVKIT-V1.0-INSTRUCTION-EN.pdf` (V1.0, 2015-1-28), https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodemcu/nodemcu-devkit-v1.0/master/Documents/NODEMCU-DEVKIT-V1.0-INSTRUCTION-EN.pdf, accessed 2026-11-04
3. NodeMCU team, board photo, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodemcu/nodemcu-devkit-v1.0/master/Documents/NodeMCU_DEVKIT_1.0.jpg, and repository README, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodemcu/nodemcu-devkit-v1.0/master/README.md, accessed 2026-11-04
4. NodeMCU firmware documentation, modules gpio, i2c, pwm, spi, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodemcu/nodemcu-firmware/release/docs/modules/gpio.md (and i2c.md, pwm.md, spi.md in the same folder) — IO index table, HSPI pins, accessed 2026-11-04
5. Espressif, ESP8266EX Datasheet v7.1, https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/0a-esp8266ex_datasheet_en.pdf — tables 2-1, 4-2, 4-3, 4-4, 4-6, 4-7, 5-1, section 4.9, accessed 2026-11-04. Espressif publishes the chip data; the ESP-12E module itself is an Ai-Thinker part, and I did not read a module datasheet.
6. ESP8266 Arduino core documentation, Libraries, https://arduino-esp8266.readthedocs.io/en/latest/libraries.html — default I2C pins, accessed 2026-11-04

## Cross-check
Schematic, pin map and firmware table agree on every D-pin. Disagreements:
- **D1/D2.** `Documents/新版本管脚对应关系.txt` in the devkit repository lists D1 GPIO4 and D2 GPIO5. Schematic J2, pin map and firmware `gpio.md` all say D1 GPIO5, D2 GPIO4. I chose the three documents that agree over the single text file.
- **SD pins.** The schematic labels SD_CMD as SPI_MOSI and SD_D1 as SPI_INT; the pin map and Espressif's tables 2-1 and 4-2 say SD_CMD = SPI_CS0 and SD_D1 = SPI_MOSI. I follow Espressif, as they are its chip's pins. Nobody should wire these anyway.
- **J1.2.** The pin map calls it RSV (RESERVED); the schematic connects it to the `ADC` net behind the divider. Name and type follow the pin map, the pin's note states the schematic's fact.
- **D0 and I2C.** The pin map's footnote and `gpio.md` exclude I2C on D0; `i2c.md` allows GPIO16 as SCL with a build option. The note follows the footnote.
- **I2C pins.** Espressif's table 4-4 names GPIO14 and GPIO2; the firmware takes any IO index, with an example using pin 1 as SDA and pin 2 as SCL; the Arduino core defaults to GPIO4 SDA and GPIO5 SCL. The functions name only the Arduino default, labelled as such; the notes say that it is software and that the firmware's examples differ.
- **Title blocks.** The IO CONN, KEY and ADC sheets still say VER 0.9, the ESP-12 CORE sheet says 1.0, all in the same `V1.0` PDF. The pin map of the same revision agrees with them, so I treat them as the V1.0 board.
- The A0 range "3.2 V" is my calculation from the schematic (220 kΩ + 100 kΩ) and the datasheet's 1.0 V limit on TOUT, not a figure printed in a source.
No UNVERIFIED pin.

## Choices
- `RX` and `TX` as names (silk in the photo); the pin map's D9 and D10 are in `function`.
- `3V3` for the silk `3V`, `VIN` for `Vin`, as in the pin map.
- SD3 and SD2 are `io`, because the pin map calls them GPIO10 and GPIO9 and the firmware gives them IO indexes 12 and 11. SD1, CMD, SD0 and CLK are `data`: the pin map gives them only SPI and SD roles and they are the flash bus.
- A0 is `signal`, not `io`: it is an ADC input only, unlike the A pins of an Arduino.
- The two RSV pins are `nc`, as `reserved` is in that type by the catalog schema.
- "Clones differ" is stated in general terms as planned; no source lists which clone differs how, so I name no clone.
- The LED on D0 is from the KEY sheet (LED1 from 3.3 V through 470 Ω to GPIO16). Any LED of the ESP-12E module itself is not in the sources read and is left out.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/boards/raspberry_pi_40.md`:

`````markdown
# raspberry_pi_40 — Raspberry Pi 40-pin header / Raspberry Pi 40-Pin-Stiftleiste

Kind: authoritative maker document
Pins: 40; types: power 4; ground 8; io 26; nc 2

## View
Written for the male pin header on the board (`drawn: plug`), looking down at the pins from above, pin 1 at the top left. Basis, both from Raspberry Pi's documentation:
- Figure "Raspberry Pi pinout diagram" (`GPIO-Pinout-Diagram-2.png`, downloaded and looked at): a Pi from the component side with the header at the right edge and USB and Ethernet at the bottom; the enlarged header shows 1 2 / 3 4 … 39 40, odd numbers in the left column.
- Text: the header lies "along the top edge" of classic SBCs and Zero models, with pin 1 in the "lower-left corner" and pin 40 in the "upper-right corner". Figure "The pin labelling for a Raspberry Pi GPIO header" (`GPIO-numbers.png`) shows that landscape view: top row 5V, 5V, GND …, bottom row 3V3, GP2, GP3 ….

The two agree: turning the landscape view by 90° clockwise moves the lower left corner to the top left and the upper left (pin 2) to the top right. It is a rotation of the same side, not a mirror, so the rows `["1","2"] … ["39","40"]` state the plug view correctly. The toggle's mirror then shows a cable socket looking into its holes, with pin 2 at the top left, which is physically right for the face that mates with this header.

## Sources
1. Raspberry Pi, documentation, Raspberry Pi hardware, section "40-pin GPIO header", https://www.raspberrypi.com/documentation/computers/raspberry-pi.html (read through the fetch tool) and its source file https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raspberrypi/documentation/master/documentation/asciidoc/computers/raspberry-pi/gpio-on-raspberry-pi.adoc (read in full for this section) — models, layout text, pin types table, pin functions table, limits, accessed 2026-11-04
2. Figures of that section: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raspberrypi/documentation/master/documentation/asciidoc/computers/raspberry-pi/images/GPIO-Pinout-Diagram-2.png and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raspberrypi/documentation/master/documentation/asciidoc/computers/raspberry-pi/images/GPIO-numbers.png, accessed 2026-11-04
3. Raspberry Pi, BCM2711 ARM Peripherals, table 94 "GPIO Pins Alternative Function Assignment", https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/bcm2711/bcm2711-peripherals.pdf — bus numbers of I2C and SPI, PWM on GPIO18/19, SPI1 on GPIO19–21, accessed 2026-11-04

## Cross-check
The pin table and both figures agree on all 40 positions and names, and the counts (4 power, 8 ground, 26 GPIO, 2 ID EEPROM) match the pin types table. Disagreements:
- **GPIO0 and GPIO1.** The pin functions table gives them type GPIO; the pin types table gives them their own type "ID EEPROM", "reserved"; the labelling figure marks them DNC. I chose `nc` because the catalog schema puts reserved pins there and because the safe reading for someone wiring is to leave them free. The name stays `GPIO0`/`GPIO1` as in the pinout diagram.
- **Label style.** The current documentation writes GP2 in tables and GPIO 2 in the pinout diagram. The task asks for `GPIO2`.
- **Bus numbers.** The documentation writes CE0, CE1, CE2 and MISO without bus numbers. Table 94 of BCM2711 gives SPI0 on GPIO7–11 and SPI1 on GPIO16–21. GPIO18 and GPIO19 also have PWM0_0 and PWM0_1 there, which the documentation's table does not mention; `function` says "on BCM2711". GPIO20 and GPIO21 as SPI1 MOSI and SCLK come only from table 94, as does I2C1 for GPIO2 and GPIO3.
- I did not read the BCM2835 or the Compute Module 4 and 5 datasheets that the documentation points to for other SoCs, so the bus numbers are checked for BCM2711 only. The note in the item says alternatives vary with the SoC.
No UNVERIFIED pin.

## Choices
- `views` as planned: plug is the board's pin header, socket is a cable socket.
- 3.3 V limits are from the documentation; "not 5 V tolerant" is in its own warning.
- `3V3` and `5V` keep their type `power`. The documentation says the 5 V pins can also feed the Pi, so the function says output or input; 3V3 is described only as output.
- Pi models with a 26-pin header, and Compute Modules, are not covered.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/boards/raspberry_pi_pico.md`:

`````markdown
# raspberry_pi_pico — Raspberry Pi Pico and Pico W pins / Raspberry Pi Pico und Pico W Pins

Kind: authoritative maker document
Pins: 43; types: power 3; ground 9; signal 3; data 2; io 26

## View
Board from the component side, portrait, USB at the top, as `connector: top`. Basis:
- Raspberry Pi Pico Datasheet, figure 4, "The pin numbering of the Raspberry Pi Pico Rev3 board" (page rendered and looked at): USB at the top, 1 … 20 down the left side, 40 … 21 down the right side, pads D1, D2, D3 from left to right on the bottom edge. The figure's text "TP1-6 ARE ON REVERSE SIDE" shows it is drawn from the component side.
- The pinout diagram `Pico-R3-A4-Pinout.pdf` (figure 2 of the datasheet; rendered and read), with the RP2040 and BOOTSEL visible, gives the same positions and the signal names, and shows the debug pads SWCLK, GND, SWDIO from left to right.
- Pico W: datasheet figure 4 and `PicoW-A4-Pinout.pdf` give the same 1 … 40. Its debug pads are at a different place: inside the board, level with pins 13 and 28, labelled SWCLK, GND, SWDIO from left to right.

## Sources
1. Raspberry Pi, Raspberry Pi Pico Datasheet, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/pico/pico-datasheet.pdf — figures 2 and 4, sections 2.1 and 4.2, accessed 2026-11-04
2. Raspberry Pi, Pico pinout diagram, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/pico/Pico-R3-A4-Pinout.pdf — alternative functions and defaults, accessed 2026-11-04
3. Raspberry Pi, Raspberry Pi Pico W Datasheet, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/picow/pico-w-datasheet.pdf — figures 3 and 4, section 2.1 (internal GPIOs, LED), accessed 2026-11-04
4. Raspberry Pi, Pico W pinout diagram, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/picow/PicoW-A4-Pinout.pdf — same pins, debug pad position, LED, accessed 2026-11-04

## Cross-check
The two datasheets and the two diagrams agree on pins 1 to 40. Details:
- Debug pads differ between the boards, as above. The task puts them at the bottom edge, which is the Pico; the notes state the Pico W position. This is the one place where the shared drawing is not physically right for the Pico W.
- The D1, D2, D3 numbers are in the Pico figure 4. The Pico W figure 4 prints only the signal names at these pads. I use the Pico's numbers for both.
- Pin 36: the diagram writes 3V3(OUT), the datasheet's list PIN36 3V3. Name follows the diagram because it says the direction.
- Pin 33: the diagram shows GND and AGND, the datasheet's list AGND. Name is `AGND`.
- "(default)" is read from the colour legend of the diagrams (darker tag = default): GP0/GP1 UART0, GP4/GP5 I2C0, GP16–GP19 SPI0. Checked on a zoomed render of the Pico diagram.
No UNVERIFIED pin.

## Choices
- One item for both boards, with no variants, as planned.
- Pico 2 and Pico 2 W are not covered: I did not read their documents.
- ADC_VREF is `signal`, like AREF on the Arduino boards, although it also feeds the ADC; 3V3_EN and RUN are `signal`.
- AGND and the debug pad D2 count as `ground`.
- SWCLK and SWDIO are `data` (a serial line and its clock).
- Pad numbers D1–D3 can be mistaken for Arduino D pins; the names beside them make clear what they are.
- The test points TP1–TP6 on the back are left out.
`````

  notes: {en: "Connect like to like: MISO to MISO and MOSI to MOSI, there is no crossover. A boxed header has its notch on the side of pins 1, 3 and 5; many boards use bare pins without a notch. Microchips andere 6-polige Anschlüsse (PDI, TPI, UPDI) sind anders belegt."}

TXD ist ein Ausgang und RXD ein Eingang des Kabels: TXD des Kabels an RX des Ziels und RXD des Kabels an TX des Ziels. Ein Dreieck auf dem Gehäuse markiert Pin 1. Die Versionen mit Klinke, offenen Enden und 2-mm-Raster sind anders belegt."}

- id: qwiic
  kind: pinout
  category: pinouts
  group: debug
  name: {cs: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT", da: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT", de: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT", el: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT", en: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT", es: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT", fr: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT", hi: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT", it: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT", ja: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT", nl: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT", no: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT", pl: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT", pt: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT", sv: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT", zh: "Qwiic / STEMMA QT"}
  doc: {en: "4-pin, 1 mm JST SH connector for I2C modules, used by SparkFun Qwiic and Adafruit STEMMA QT.", de: "4-poliger JST-SH-Stecker im 1-mm-Raster für I2C-Module, verwendet von SparkFun Qwiic und Adafruit STEMMA QT."}
  notes: {en: "STEMMA QT is compatible with Qwiic: connector, pin order and wire colours are the same, and Adafruit states that both kinds of device work together. They differ in the supply. Qwiic boards run on 3.3 V only, while STEMMA QT devices accept 3 to 5 V and carry their own regulator and level shifting. So keep V+ at 3.3 V when a Qwiic device is on the bus. Pin numbers are not uniform: the schematics of both makers count GND as pin 1, SparkFun's cable drawing counts the yellow SCL wire as 1. Go by signal and wire colour, not by number.", de: "STEMMA QT ist mit Qwiic kompatibel: Stecker, Pinfolge und Aderfarben sind gleich, und Adafruit nennt beide Gerätearten ausdrücklich zusammen verwendbar. Der Unterschied liegt in der Versorgung. Qwiic-Platinen laufen nur mit 3,3 V, STEMMA-QT-Geräte vertragen 3 bis 5 V und haben eigenen Regler und Pegelwandler. Ist ein Qwiic-Gerät am Bus, muss V+ also 3,3 V bleiben. Die Pinnummern sind nicht einheitlich: Die Schaltpläne beider Hersteller zählen GND als Pin 1, SparkFuns Kabelzeichnung zählt die gelbe SCL-Ader als 1. Nach Signal und Aderfarbe gehen, nicht nach der Nummer."}
  tags: [qwiic, stemma, "stemma qt", sparkfun, adafruit, jst, "jst sh", "jst-sh", i2c, iic, sda, scl, "3.3v", "4-pin", "4-polig", sensor, sm04b, shr-04v, kabel, cable]
  source: "SparkFun, Qwiic Connect System page (sparkfun.com/qwiic), Qwiic cable drawing ACCA-1571 and SparkFun-Connectors.lbr (device QWIIC_CONNECTOR); Adafruit, Adafruit STEMMA & STEMMA QT guide (What is STEMMA QT?, Technical Specs, comparison page) and Adafruit QT Py schematic (device STEMMA_I2C)"
  views:
    plug: {en: "Header on the board (pins)", de: "Stiftleiste auf der Platine"}
    socket: {en: "Housing on the cable (sockets)", de: "Gehäuse am Kabel (Buchsenkontakte)"}
  shape:
    type: rows
    outline: jst
    contact: square
    drawn: plug
    rows:
      - {pins: ["1"]}
      - {pins: ["2"]}
      - {pins: ["3"]}
      - {pins: ["4"]}
  pins:
    - {number: "1", name: "GND", function: {en: "Ground", de: "Masse"}, type: ground, wire: black}
    - {number: "2", name: "3.3V", function: {en: "3.3 V supply on Qwiic; V+ of 3 to 5 V on STEMMA QT", de: "3,3-V-Versorgung bei Qwiic; V+ von 3 bis 5 V bei STEMMA QT"}, type: power, wire: red}
    - {number: "3", name: "SDA", function: {en: "I2C data", de: "I2C-Daten"}, type: data, wire: blue}
    - {number: "4", name: "SCL", function: {en: "I2C clock", de: "I2C-Takt"}, type: data, wire: yellow}

- id: grove
  kind: pinout
  category: pinouts
  group: debug
  name: {cs: "Grove (4 piny)", da: "Grove (4 ben)", de: "Grove (4-polig)", el: "Grove (4 ακίδες)", en: "Grove (4-pin)", es: "Grove (4 pines)", fr: "Grove (4 broches)", hi: "Grove (4-पिन)", it: "Grove (4 pin)", ja: "Grove(4ピン)", nl: "Grove (4-pins)", no: "Grove (4 pinner)", pl: "Grove (4 piny)", pt: "Grove (4 pinos)", sv: "Grove (4 stift)", zh: "Grove(4 针)"}
  doc: {en: "The 4-wire, 2.0 mm connector of Seeed's Grove modules. Pins 3 and 4 always carry the supply; the meaning of pins 1 and 2 depends on the interface.", de: "Der 4-adrige Anschluss im 2,0-mm-Raster der Grove-Module von Seeed. Pin 3 und 4 führen immer die Versorgung; die Bedeutung von Pin 1 und 2 hängt von der Schnittstelle ab."}
  notes: {en: "Digital: pin 1 is Dn (main line), pin 2 is Dn+1 (second line). Analog: pin 1 is An (main input), pin 2 is An+1. UART: pin 1 is RX and pin 2 is TX, both named from the base unit's side. I2C: pin 1 is SCL, pin 2 is SDA. VCC is 5 V or 3.3 V, and some modules accept only one of them: check the module. Grove is not Qwiic: the pitch differs, and the wires run in the opposite order. Adafruit describes the housing as an HY type and not as a true JST.", de: "Digital: Pin 1 ist Dn (Hauptleitung), Pin 2 ist Dn+1 (zweite Leitung). Analog: Pin 1 ist An (Haupteingang), Pin 2 ist An+1. UART: Pin 1 ist RX und Pin 2 ist TX, beide aus Sicht der Basiseinheit benannt. I2C: Pin 1 ist SCL, Pin 2 ist SDA. VCC beträgt 5 V oder 3,3 V, manche Module vertragen nur einen der Werte: das Modul prüfen. Grove ist nicht Qwiic: Das Raster ist anders, und die Adern liegen in umgekehrter Folge. Adafruit beschreibt das Gehäuse als HY-Typ und nicht als echtes JST."}
  tags: [grove, seeed, seeedstudio, "4-pin", "4-polig", i2c, uart, digital, analog, scl, sda, rx, tx, d0, a0, sensor, modul, module, hy, kabel, cable]
  source: "Seeed Studio Wiki, Grove Ecosystem Introduction (Grove_System), interface tables for digital, analog, UART and I2C; Adafruit STEMMA & STEMMA QT guide, STEMMA / Grove comparison"
  views:
    plug: {en: "Plug on the cable", de: "Stecker am Kabel"}
    socket: {en: "Connector on the module (Seeed: female header)", de: "Anschluss auf dem Modul (Seeed: Female Header)"}
  shape:
    type: rows
    outline: jst
    contact: square
    drawn: socket
    rows:
      - {pins: ["1"]}
      - {pins: ["2"]}
      - {pins: ["3"]}
      - {pins: ["4"]}
  pins:
    - {number: "1", name: "SIG1", function: {en: "Signal 1: Dn, An, RX or SCL", de: "Signal 1: Dn, An, RX oder SCL"}, type: signal, wire: yellow}
    - {number: "2", name: "SIG2", function: {en: "Signal 2: Dn+1, An+1, TX or SDA", de: "Signal 2: Dn+1, An+1, TX oder SDA"}, type: signal, wire: white}
    - {number: "3", name: "VCC", function: {en: "Module supply, 5 V or 3.3 V", de: "Modulversorgung, 5 V oder 3,3 V"}, type: power, wire: red}
    - {number: "4", name: "GND", function: {en: "Ground", de: "Masse"}, type: ground, wire: black}

- id: servo
  kind: pinout
  category: pinouts
  group: debug
  name: {cs: "Modelářské servo (3 piny)", da: "Modelservo (3 ben)", de: "Modellbau-Servo (3-polig)", el: "Σέρβο μοντελισμού (3 ακίδες)", en: "Hobby servo (3-pin)", es: "Servo de modelismo (3 pines)", fr: "Servo de modélisme (3 broches)", hi: "हॉबी सर्वो (3-पिन)", it: "Servo da modellismo (3 pin)", ja: "ホビー用サーボ(3ピン)", nl: "Modelbouwservo (3-pins)", no: "Modellservo (3 pinner)", pl: "Serwo modelarskie (3 piny)", pt: "Servo de modelismo (3 pinos)", sv: "Modellservo (3 stift)", zh: "模型舵机(3 针)"}
  doc: {en: "The usual 3-way, 0.1 inch plug of hobby servos: signal, V+, ground. Makers number these pins differently, so this page calls them S, + and -.", de: "Der übliche 3-polige Stecker im 2,54-mm-Raster von Modellbau-Servos: Signal, V+, Masse. Die Hersteller nummerieren diese Pins unterschiedlich, deshalb heißen sie hier S, + und -."}
  notes: {en: "V+ sits in the middle. That matters because a plug turned round keeps V+ on V+ and only swaps signal and ground, so the supply is not reversed across the servo; it just gets no usable signal. Avoid it anyway, because the servo's ground then hangs on the controller's signal pin. Truly reversed power, for example from a wrongly built adapter, can destroy a servo at once. Wire colours drawn here: Futaba scheme, white signal, red V+, black ground. JR scheme: orange signal, red V+, brown ground. Hitec scheme: signal on the third wire, usually yellow, red V+, black ground. Exceptions exist: Spektrum's AR6310 manual has the brown negative wire in the middle of its JST micro plug and warns that JST servos differ, and Airtronics is reported to use another order. Check the data sheet of an unknown servo.", de: "V+ liegt in der Mitte. Das ist wichtig, weil ein umgedrehter Stecker V+ auf V+ lässt und nur Signal und Masse vertauscht. Die Versorgung liegt also nicht verpolt am Servo; es bekommt nur kein brauchbares Signal. Trotzdem vermeiden, denn die Servomasse hängt dann am Signalpin des Controllers. Eine echte Verpolung, etwa durch einen falsch gebauten Adapter, kann ein Servo sofort zerstören. Hier gezeichnete Aderfarben: Futaba-Schema, weiß Signal, rot V+, schwarz Masse. JR-Schema: orange Signal, rot V+, braun Masse. Hitec-Schema: Signal auf der dritten Ader, meist gelb, rot V+, schwarz Masse. Es gibt Ausnahmen: Spektrums Handbuch zum AR6310 legt beim JST-Mikrostecker die braune Minusader in die Mitte und warnt vor abweichenden JST-Servos, und für Airtronics wird eine andere Reihenfolge berichtet. Bei einem unbekannten Servo das Datenblatt prüfen."}

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/debug/arm_jtag_20.md`:

`````markdown
# arm_jtag_20 — ARM JTAG (20-pin) / ARM JTAG (20-polig)

Kind: authoritative maker document
Pins: 20; types: power 1, ground 9, signal 4, data 5, nc 1

## View
Written for the male box header on the board, looking down at its pins (the mating face): `drawn: plug`, 10 rows of 2, odd pins left, pin 1 top left, notch `left`.

Basis, seen in the figures themselves (rendered or downloaded and looked at; no text in these documents says "top view"):
- Arm, Cortex-M Debug Connectors, page 3: diagram with "1 2" on top and "19 20" at the bottom, odd pins left, the outline interrupted on the left side between TMS and TDO. It stands next to a photo of the boxed header on a board labelled JTAG.
- SEGGER figure JTAG_Port.png: same layout, notch on the left at pins 9 and 11. SEGGER calls the part a "keyed box header (2.54mm male)".
- Keil figure conjtag.png: same layout and left gap, beside a photo of the header with its notch on the left.

Derived check of the mirror direction: Microchip's Atmel-ICE guide (page 15) says that pin 1 of its 100-mil socket sits to the right of the keying "when the connector is seen from the cable". Looking at a socket from the cable is the same direction as looking down on the header it plugs into. Rotating this drawing until the notch is on top puts pin 1 to the right of the notch, so the drawing is the view from above and not the mirror image. This sentence is about the AVR cable, so it supports the IDC convention but does not name the ARM connector.

## Sources
1. ARM DSTREAM System and Interface Design Reference Guide, ARM 100956_0527_00_en (DS-5 5.27), section 2.4, table 2-6 (pinout) and table 2-7 (signals), read in the copy at https://www.manualslib.com/manual/2490558/Arm-Ds-5.html?page=33 (also page=34, page=35). Arm's own site served no text to the fetch tool (support.arm.com loads the document by script). Accessed 2026-11-04.
2. Arm, Cortex-M Debug Connectors, https://documentation-service.arm.com/static/5fce6c49e167456a35b36af1 — page 3, 20-pin IDC diagram. The document says that it is for general information and not a specification. Accessed 2026-11-04.
3. SEGGER Knowledge Base, 20-pin J-Link Connector, https://kb.segger.com/20-pin_J-Link_Connector with figure https://kb.segger.com/images/3/3c/JTAG_Port.png — JTAG table and notes. Accessed 2026-11-04.
4. Keil ULINKpro User's Guide, Connectors, https://www.keil.com/support/man/docs/ulinkpro/ulinkpro_cs_connectors.asp with figure conjtag.png in the same folder. Accessed 2026-11-04.
5. Microchip Atmel-ICE User Guide, Atmel-42330C, 10/2016, https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/DeviceDoc/Atmel-ICE_UserGuide.pdf — page 15, keying sentence (view check only). Accessed 2026-11-04.

## Cross-check
Signal pins 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 and 15 agree everywhere apart from spelling. Disagreements:
- Pin 2: ARM 100956 and SEGGER NC; Keil and Arm's Cortex-M document "VCC (optional)". Chose NC (the DSTREAM reference table), the optional VCC is in the pin note.
- Pins 14, 16, 18, 20: ARM 100956, Arm's Cortex-M document and Keil GND; SEGGER reserved ("do not assume them to be connected to GND inside J-Link"). Chose GND as the ARM standard, SEGGER's difference is in the item notes and pin notes.
- Pin 17: ARM 100956 DBGRQ; Arm's Cortex-M document NC/DBGRQ; Keil N/C; SEGGER DBGRQ, not connected in the J-Link. Chose DBGRQ.
- Pin 19: ARM 100956 DBGACK; Arm's Cortex-M document NC/DBACK; Keil N/C; SEGGER 5V-Supply output, max. 300 mA. Chose DBGACK and put a caution in the pin note, because a 5 V output on this pin can damage a target that uses it as a signal.
- Pin 15: nSRST (ARM 100956), nRESET (SEGGER, Arm's Cortex-M document), RESET (Keil). Chose nSRST and named the others in the note.
- Pin 1: VTREF (ARM 100956), VTref (SEGGER), VCC (Arm's Cortex-M document, Keil). Chose SEGGER's spelling VTref; the role is the same.

Unverified: nothing about pin numbers or names. Not read: IEEE 1149.1 itself (it does not define this header).

## Choices
- `key: left` comes from the drawings, not from text. The notch position at pins 9 and 11 is drawn by SEGGER only; the catalog schema's `key` carries the side only.
- `type: power` for VTref: it connects to the target's rail although the probe only senses it. Stated in the pin note.
- TCK, TMS and RTCK are `data` by the catalog schema's rule on bus lines and their clocks; nTRST, nSRST, DBGRQ and DBGACK are `signal`.
- "Normally active low" for the two resets: Arm says that polarity and strength are configurable on DSTREAM but that both lines are pulled high and driven low to reset.
- Pin 2 is `nc` although some targets use it for VCC, as documented in its note.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/debug/arm_swd_10.md`:

`````markdown
# arm_swd_10 — Cortex Debug / SWD (10-pin) / Cortex Debug / SWD (10-polig)

Kind: authoritative maker document
Pins: 10; types: power 1, ground 3, signal 1, data 4, nc 1

## View
Written for the header on the board, looking down at its pins (the mating face): `drawn: plug`, 5 rows of 2, odd pins left, pin 1 top left, notch `left`.

Basis, seen in the figures (no text in these documents says "top view"):
- Arm, Cortex-M Debug Connectors, page 2: diagram with "1 2" on top and "9 10" at the bottom, odd pins left, no contact at KEY, the outline interrupted on the left side between pins 3 and 7. It stands next to a photo of the header on a board.
- Keil figure concortex10pindesc.png: same order and an empty position 7 (this figure draws no notch).
- Keil photo concortex10pin.png: the ribbon socket is shown from its mating face with the bump on top and the red wire on the left. Mirrored for the header seen from above and turned so that the bump goes to the left, this puts the red-wire end at the top, in line with pin 1 top left, assuming that the red wire marks pin 1 (Microchip states that for its own cable). The photo does not show which row of that end is pin 1.

## Sources
1. Arm, Cortex-M Debug Connectors, https://documentation-service.arm.com/static/5fce6c49e167456a35b36af1 — page 2, diagram. The document says that it is for general information and not a specification. Accessed 2026-11-04.
2. ARM DSTREAM System and Interface Design Reference Guide, ARM 100956_0527_00_en (DS-5 5.27), section 2.7, table 2-12 (pinout) and table 2-13 (signals), read in the copy at https://www.manualslib.com/manual/2490558/Arm-Ds-5.html?page=40 and page=41. Accessed 2026-11-04.
3. Keil ULINKpro User's Guide, Connectors, https://www.keil.com/support/man/docs/ulinkpro/ulinkpro_cs_connectors.asp with figures concortex10pindesc.png and concortex10pin.png. Accessed 2026-11-04.
4. Microchip SAM E54 Xplained Pro User's Guide, section 5.2.8, table 5-10, https://onlinedocs.microchip.com/oxy/GUID-AA358083-AEED-4BA8-8511-9F986D3390A5-en-US-2/GUID-6AEFC2EC-DBA5-4292-8134-E311C8CE37CD.html — the same connector on a real board. Accessed 2026-11-04.

5. SEGGER Knowledge Base, Debug Connectors, https://kb.segger.com/Connectors — remark on variants without pin 7. Accessed 2026-11-04.

Not reached: the CoreSight Components Technical Reference Manual, appendix C, which Arm names as the detailed specification. Arm's pages load by script and the fetch tool got no text.

## Cross-check
All sources agree on the position of every signal. Differences in naming:
- Pin 1: VCC (Arm's Cortex-M document, Microchip), VTREF (ARM 100956), VTref (Keil). Chose VTref: table 2-13 defines it as an input of the probe.
- Pin 4: SWDCLK (Arm's Cortex-M document, Keil), SWCLK (ARM 100956, Microchip). Chose SWCLK and named SWDCLK in the function.
- Pin 6: Keil also lists EXTa and TRACECTL. Left out, they belong to trace setups.
- Pin 8: NC/TDI (Arm's Cortex-M document, Microchip), TDI (ARM 100956), NC/EXTb/TDI (Keil). Chose NC/TDI.
- Pin 9: GNDDetect (Arm's Cortex-M document, Keil, Microchip), GND (ARM 100956). Chose GNDDetect with `type: ground`, the note names the difference. Only Microchip explains the name ("Ground detection").
- Pin 10: nRESET (Arm's Cortex-M document, Keil, Microchip), nSRST (ARM 100956). Chose nRESET.
- Pin 7: a keying position whose pin must be absent on the target's connector (ARM 100956, table 2-13, read through a summary of that page), no pin (Keil). SEGGER's connector page says that variants with pin 7 removed can also be used, which suggests that headers with a pin 7 exist in practice.

## Choices
- Pin 7 appears as a pin with `type: nc` and not as a `null` position, as the assignment asks and because every source lists it as position 7.
- `key: left` rests on the gap in Arm's drawing alone (a drawing, and the document is not a specification). The Keil photo agrees but cannot settle it. The key field is the least certain part of this item; the pin positions are not in doubt.
- "Active low" is not stated for pin 10 because only the name suggests it here and ARM 100956 says that polarity is configurable.
- 0.05 inch is written as 1,27 mm in German, the usual metric value of that pitch.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/debug/avr_isp_6.md`:

`````markdown
# avr_isp_6 — AVR ISP (6-pin) / AVR ISP (6-polig)

Kind: authoritative maker document
Pins: 6; types: power 1, ground 1, signal 1, data 3

## View
Written for the header on the target board seen from above, looking at its pins (the mating face): `drawn: plug`, rows [1 2], [3 4], [5 6], odd pins left.

Basis: AVR910 caption "Figure 1-2. Recommended In-System Programming Interface Connector Layout (Top View)", rendered and read: MISO 1 / 2 VCC, SCK 3 / 4 MOSI, RESET 5 / 6 GND, on a "2 x 3 pin header contact, with pin spacing of 100 mils". AN2519 figure 4-1 and Atmel-ICE figure 4-10 draw the same layout with "1 2" on top.

`key: left` is derived, not drawn. The Atmel-ICE guide (page 15) puts pin 1 of its 6-pin 100-mil connector "to the right of the keying", seen from the cable. Looking at the socket from the cable is the same direction as looking down on the header. With the key turned to the top, pin 1 is to its right only if the key lies on the side of pins 1, 3 and 5, which in the drawn view is the left side.

## Sources
1. Atmel/Microchip, AVR910: In-System Programming, Atmel-0943F, 11/2016, https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/AppNotes/Atmel-0943-In-System-Programming_ApplicationNote_AVR910.pdf — page 3, figures 1-1 and 1-2; signal table in section 2. Accessed 2026-11-04.
2. Microchip, AN2519 AVR Microcontroller Hardware Design Considerations, DS00002519B, https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/Appnotes/AN2519-AVR-Microcontroller-Hardware-Design-Considerations-00002519B.pdf — page 9, figure 4-1, VTG supply text. Accessed 2026-11-04.
3. Atmel-ICE User Guide, Atmel-42330C, 10/2016, https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/DeviceDoc/Atmel-ICE_UserGuide.pdf — page 15 (keying), page 38 (figure 4-10), table 3-6. Accessed 2026-11-04.
4. Microchip, MPLAB ICE 4 In-Circuit Emulator User's Guide, section 3.3.4.2.2, table 3-7, https://onlinedocs.microchip.com/oxy/GUID-E9773D3D-A940-4268-9E35-189A30B5467E-en-US-1/GUID-A86E8194-0702-42A1-99BC-DC4BC6CDB518.html — the same mapping in a current tool guide. Accessed 2026-11-04.

## Cross-check
All four agree on every pin. Spelling only:
- Pin 2: VCC (AVR910, Atmel-ICE figure), VTG (AN2519, table 3-6, MPLAB ICE 4). Chose VCC, VTG is in the function.
- Pin 5: RESET with overbar (AVR910), RST (AN2519), /RESET (Atmel-ICE). Chose RESET, the low level is in the function.
- Pins 1 and 4: PDO/MISO and PDI/MOSI in Atmel-ICE figure 4-10, because that header is also used for PDI on older parts. Chose MISO and MOSI.

Unverified: nothing about the pins. No document draws the notch for this header; see the derivation above.

## Choices
- `key: left` although many boards (for example bare 2 × 3 headers) have no shroud. The note says so.
- "No crossover" is taken from AVR910 figure 1-1, which joins MISO to MISO and MOSI to MOSI.
- The 10-way ISP header is not part of this item. It is drawn in AN2519 figure 4-1 with another layout.
- The reset line is `signal`, SCK, MISO and MOSI are `data` by the catalog schema.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/debug/ftdi_6.md`:

`````markdown
# ftdi_6 — FTDI TTL-232R (6-pin) / FTDI TTL-232R (6-polig)

Kind: authoritative maker document
Pins: 6; types: power 1, ground 1, signal 2, data 2

## View
Written for the connector at the cable end: `drawn: socket`, one column of 6, pin 1 on top. A single column looks the same in both views, so a mirror error cannot occur; only the sequence along the connector is a fact here.

Basis: figure 4.1 (rendered and looked at) draws the header as one vertical bar with contacts 1 to 6 from top to bottom and the colours in the same order, captioned "6 Way Header Pin Out". Table 4.1 gives the same numbers. Figure 4.2 shows a row of six funnel-shaped openings on the end face and a triangle labelled "Pin 1". That is why I treat the part as a socket: the text only calls it a "6 way, 0.1", Single-In-Line (SIL) connector" and "6 pin header", it never says female.

## Sources
1. Connective Peripherals, TTL-232R TTL to USB Serial Converter Range of Cables Datasheet, CP_000069, version 1.1, copy at https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0434/1376/6295/files/DS_TTL-232R_CABLES.pdf — page 9 and 10: figures 4.1 and 4.2, tables 4.1 to 4.5. Accessed 2026-11-04.
2. Future Technology Devices International, TTL-232R datasheet, FT_000054, version 2.01, 2008-08-28, copy at https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/teaching/0910/P31/docs/usbseriallead.pdf — section 4: same figure and table. Accessed 2026-11-04.

FTDI's own download URLs (ftdichip.com) answered 403 to my request, so both documents were read in the copies above. The first document carries the Connective Peripherals name, which now issues this datasheet; the second is FTDI's own issue.

## Cross-check
Both editions agree on numbers, names and colours: 1 GND black, 2 CTS# brown, 3 VCC red, 4 TXD orange, 5 RXD yellow, 6 RTS# green. They also agree that VCC is +5 V on the 3V3 cable ("signals only, VCC= +5V"). 75 mA is the output power current of tables 4.2 and 4.4.

Unverified: nothing about the pins. Whether the housing is female is taken from figure 4.2, as described above.

## Choices
- "Do not feed a 3.3 V board from it directly" is my conclusion from VCC = +5 V; the datasheet does not phrase it as a warning.
- Direction of TXD and RXD is given from the cable's side, as in table 4.1. The advice to cross them to the target is my wording of what output and input mean.
- `type: signal` for CTS# and RTS# (RTS is the catalog schema's example for `signal`), `data` for TXD and RXD.
- I keep the # in the names as the source writes it. It must stay quoted in YAML.
- The note about other versions: the datasheet's sections 5 to 7 describe audio jack, wire end and 2 mm (8-way) versions. Their tables are not in this item.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/debug/qwiic.md`:

`````markdown
# qwiic — Qwiic / STEMMA QT / Qwiic / STEMMA QT

Kind: authoritative maker document
Pins: 4; types: power 1, ground 1, data 2

## View
Written for the header on the board: `drawn: plug`, one column, pin 1 on top. A single column looks the same in both views, so only the sequence along the connector is stated, and that is what the sources fix: GND, 3.3V, SDA, SCL in consecutive positions.

Which end of a real connector is pin 1 is not stated by the drawing, on purpose. Both makers' side-entry footprints agree with each other: pad 1 at x = -1.5 mm to pad 4 at x = +1.5 mm, with the signal pads at the rear and the mounting tabs on the -y side (SparkFun JST04_1MM_RA; Adafruit JST_SH4 and JST_SH4_SKINNY). I did not turn this into a left/right claim on the mating face because I could not read JST's drawing to confirm which side the opening is on (see Sources). The connector is polarised, so a user only needs the order when making an adapter, and the wire colours settle it then.

## Sources
1. SparkFun, Qwiic Connect System, https://www.sparkfun.com/qwiic — pinout rule GND / 3.3V / SDA / SCL, colours, "Qwiic only supports 3.3V boards", part numbers SM04B-SRSS-TB and SHR-04V-S. Accessed 2026-11-04.
2. SparkFun, Qwiic cable assembly drawing ACCA-1571, rev 1, 2017-02-23, https://cdn.sparkfun.com/assets/e/9/8/9/8/Qwiic-Cable.pdf — pin assignments, rendered and read. Accessed 2026-11-04.
3. SparkFun Eagle library, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sparkfun/SparkFun-Eagle-Libraries/master/SparkFun-Connectors.lbr — device QWIIC_CONNECTOR, symbol I2C_STANDARD, packages JST04_1MM_RA and JST04_1MM_VERT. Accessed 2026-11-04.
4. SparkFun, Qwiic Connect System page print, CAB-17261 technical data, https://static.mercateo.com/0e/34f4cafe25e94508b8eeb4d338befcb1/pdf/CAB-17261_eng_tds.pdf — colours in the order black, red, blue, yellow. Accessed 2026-11-04.
5. SparkFun Learn, I2C, https://learn.sparkfun.com/tutorials/i2c/qwiic-connect-system — "1 mm pitch, 4-pin JST", polarised. Accessed 2026-11-04.
6. Adafruit, Adafruit STEMMA & STEMMA QT, Technical Specs, https://learn.adafruit.com/introducing-adafruit-stemma-qt/technical-specs — colours, V+ 3 to 5 V, level shifting. Accessed 2026-11-04.
7. Same guide, What is STEMMA QT?, https://learn.adafruit.com/introducing-adafruit-stemma-qt/what-is-stemma-qt — JST SH, 1.0 mm, cross-compatibility. Accessed 2026-11-04.
8. Same guide, comparison page, https://learn.adafruit.com/introducing-adafruit-stemma-qt/sparkfun-qwiic — connector identical, same pin ordering, level shifting only on Qwiic controllers, jumper advice. Accessed 2026-11-04.
9. Adafruit QT Py PCB, https://github.com/adafruit/Adafruit-QT-Py-PCB, file "Adafruit QT Py.sch" — device STEMMA_I2C, variants _QT and _QTSKINNY: GND pad 1, V+ pad 2, SDA pad 3, SCL pad 4. Accessed 2026-11-04.

Not usable: JST's SH catalogue (https://www.jst-mfg.com/product/pdf/eng/eSH.pdf). It downloaded, but its text layer is scrambled and the Windows PDF renderer refused the file, so I could not read its drawings and do not cite it.

## Cross-check
Colours agree: black GND, red 3.3 V / V+, blue SDA, yellow SCL (sources 1, 2, 4, 6).

**Disagreement on the numbering, important:** sources 3 and 9 (the makers' schematic symbols) have pin 1 = GND up to pin 4 = SCL. Source 2 (SparkFun's cable supplier) lists position 1 = yellow, 2 = blue, 3 = red, 4 = black. The sequence is identical, only the counting direction differs. I chose 1 = GND: two makers independently use it on the boards, and it matches the rule "GND / 3.3V / SDA / SCL". The note warns about the other count. The SparkFun page's FAQ also lists the colours from yellow to black, without numbers.

Adafruit's sentence "the colors are slightly different for SDA/SCL but the pin order is the same" follows its list of the JST PH (green, white) and JST SH (blue, yellow) cables, so it compares its own two connectors, not Qwiic. A WebFetch summary presented Adafruit's list as numbered; the raw page has an unnumbered list, so I do not use it as evidence for the numbers. Pimoroni (a search result, not read) is reported to sell cables with other SDA/SCL colours, so colours are the makers' rule and not a physical guarantee.

Unverified: left/right of pin 1 on the mating face (not asserted anywhere in the item).

## Choices
- Name of pin 2 is `3.3V` (SparkFun's rule); V+ for STEMMA QT is in the function. SparkFun's symbol prints VCC.
- `type: data` for SDA and SCL by the catalog schema.
- One column instead of one row: avoids an unverifiable left/right statement and lets the page show names beside the contacts (the page rules).
- `drawn: plug` = header on the board: SparkFun calls it the board connector, Adafruit calls the cable end "JST-SH female".
- "Keep V+ at 3.3 V when a Qwiic device is on the bus" is my wording of Adafruit's advice to set a controller's jumper to 3 V and SparkFun's 3.3 V rule.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/debug/grove.md`:

`````markdown
# grove — Grove (4-pin) / Grove (4-polig)

Kind: authoritative maker document
Pins: 4; types: power 1, ground 1, signal 2

## View
Written for the connector on the module: `drawn: socket`, one column, pin 1 on top. A single column looks the same in both views, so only the sequence along the connector is stated: pin 1 yellow, pin 2 white, pin 3 red, pin 4 black, as Seeed lists them.

Seeed gives no statement on which physical end of the connector is pin 1 (the text has none; I did not look at its mechanical drawing ZIP files), so the item makes no left/right claim. The connector is keyed and the wire colours identify the pins. The derivation is the numbering itself; this is not a `GEOMETRY UNVERIFIED` case because the single column asserts nothing beyond the sequence.

## Sources
1. Seeed Studio Wiki, Grove Ecosystem Introduction, https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/Grove_System/ — colours list, the four interface tables, the UART viewpoint sentence, I2C voltage remark, "Grove Female Header" products with 4-pin, 2.0 mm pitch, "Grove plug". Accessed 2026-11-04.
2. Adafruit, Adafruit STEMMA & STEMMA QT, STEMMA / Grove comparison, https://learn.adafruit.com/introducing-adafruit-stemma-qt/seeed-studio-grove — HY-style housing by ZJDLL, "not JST PH". Accessed 2026-11-04.

## Cross-check
Only one maker's document is needed and all pin facts come from it. Seeed's page says of this section that it "may be outdated". The tables are internally consistent. I did not search for a second Seeed table to compare them with.

Comparison with Qwiic (own derivation from the two tables): Grove I2C runs SCL, SDA, VCC, GND from pin 1, Qwiic runs GND, 3.3V, SDA, SCL from pin 1 in the makers' numbering.

Unverified: which end of the housing is pin 1, as above. Left out of the notes.

## Choices
- Pin names `SIG1` and `SIG2` are mine and neutral, as the assignment asks. Seeed's names (Dn, An, RX, SCL and Dn+1, An+1, TX, SDA) are in the functions, and the meanings per interface are in the notes.
- `type: signal` for pins 1 and 2 because they differ per module, although they are data lines on I2C and UART.
- No variants: the assignment asks for one list with the meanings in the notes.
- `plug` and `socket` follow Seeed's words: "Grove plug" for the cable end and "Grove Female Header" for the board part. The board part holds the pins, despite that name, so the caption avoids the word pins.
- Outline `jst` as assigned, although Adafruit says that the housing is not a true JST. The note says so.
- The advice "check the module" reflects Seeed's remark that a few I2C modules take only 3.3 V or only 5 V.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/debug/servo.md`:

`````markdown
# servo — Hobby servo (3-pin) / Modellbau-Servo (3-polig)

Kind: cross-checked reproductions
Pins: 3; types: power 1, ground 1, signal 1

## View
Written for the plug of the servo lead: `drawn: socket` (SparkFun: "a female, 3-pin, 0.1" pitch header"), one column in the order signal, V+, ground. A single column looks the same in both views, and the order is symmetric around V+, so a mirror error cannot change which pin is in the middle. Only the sequence is stated. A plug turned by 180° reads ground, V+, signal, as on a real connector.

Basis: Parallax's table lists "1 (white) Signal", "2 (red) Vservo", "3 (black) Ground". Hitec writes "the Red wire ( center ) is 'power'". Pololu says the power wire is in the middle, with ground and signal on either side. Derivation from these, as none of them states a view.

## Sources
1. Parallax, Standard Servo (#900-00005), product guide v3.0, 8/10/2022, https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/5728/900-00005_Guide.pdf — pages 3 and 4: connection diagram, voltage table. Accessed 2026-11-04.
2. Parallax, Standard Servo (#900-00005), datasheet v2.0, copy at https://cs.umb.edu/cs341/Lab09/900-00005-StdServo-v2.0.pdf — same table; "Manufactured for Parallax exclusively by Futaba". Accessed 2026-11-04.
3. Hitec RCD, General Servo Information, copy at https://people.ece.cornell.edu/land/courses/ece4760/FinalProjects/f2012/jmv87/site/files/Servomanual.pdf — "Wire Color Meanings", voltage range. Accessed 2026-11-04.
4. Pololu (Jan), Electrical characteristics of servos and introduction to the servo control interface, 2011, https://www.pololu.com/blog/16/electrical-characteristics-of-servos-and-introduction-to-the-servo-control-interface — wire order, colour schemes, reversed power warning. Accessed 2026-11-04.
5. SparkFun, Hobby Servo Tutorial, https://learn.sparkfun.com/tutorials/hobby-servo-tutorial/all — connector type, colour table. Accessed 2026-11-04.
6. Spektrum SPMAR6310 User Manual, page 7, copy at https://www.manualsdir.com/manuals/429160/spektrum-spmar6310.html?page=7 — JST B3B-ZR micro connectors, colours, polarity warning. Accessed 2026-11-04.
7. ProgressiveRC, JR/Hitec servo extension, https://www.progressiverc.com/jr-hitec-universal-servo-extension.html — brown, red, orange. Accessed 2026-11-04.
8. RobotPlatform, Major Servo Manufacturers, https://robotplatform.com/knowledge/servo/servo_manufacturers.html — pin order per maker, Airtronics remark. Accessed 2026-11-04.

Not reached: ProgressiveRC's Futaba lead page (HTTP 429 twice). No original Futaba or JR document was found.

## Cross-check
Order signal, V+, ground: sources 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 agree (two makers' documents, Parallax and Hitec, plus Pololu). Disagreements and thin spots:
- Numbering: Parallax has 1 = signal, 3 = ground; SparkFun has 1 = ground, 3 = signal. No common numbering exists, so I use S, + and - rather than inventing numbers.
- SparkFun's colour table is damaged: rows 2 and 3 have one cell too many in its HTML (row 2: Red, Brown, Red, Red; row 3: Yellow, White, Orange, White), so columns do not line up under the headings Hitec, JR, Futaba. I only use its first column (Hitec: black, red, yellow) and take the JR and Futaba colours from elsewhere, where the table agrees if the stray cells are ignored.
- Futaba scheme (drawn): white, red, black from Parallax's servo made by Futaba. Brand and colours are linked only through that sentence and through SparkFun's last column. This is the `wire` choice I trust least in this item, although Pololu lists black, red, white as a common scheme.
- JR scheme: ProgressiveRC for a JR/Hitec lead and Spektrum for its leads. Pololu lists the same colours without a brand.
- Hitec scheme: Hitec names only black and red (centre) and "third wire", and its HS-311 sheet (https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/489/HS-311.pdf, searched for colours, none named) adds nothing. Yellow comes from SparkFun alone, so the note says "usually yellow". ProgressiveRC sells orange leads as JR/Hitec.
- **Exception to the middle pin:** Spektrum's AR6310 manual says "Brown Wire (middle wire): Negative" for its JST micro plugs and warns that some JST servos have another polarity. A search result (not read) reports the same mismatch on Spektrum telemetry cables. Kept as an exception in the note, it applies to JST micro plugs and not to the 0.1 inch plug.
- Airtronics: RobotPlatform alone says that power and ground are swapped, Pololu only names "Airtronics Z" as a connector type. The note says "is reported".

Why the middle matters: this part is my own derivation. Turning a three-in-line plug keeps the centre contact in place, so V+ stays on V+ and only the outer contacts swap. The remark about the ground on the signal pin follows from the same swap. Pololu's warning covers real reversal of power.

## Choices
- Numbers `S`, `+`, `-` are text and quoted. They appear in `data-pin` and in searches; the catalog schema allows 1 to 8 characters and has examples such as "T". If these characters cause trouble, change them in the YAML and vector together.
- `wire` values are the Futaba scheme only, as the assignment asks. The note names the scheme.
- The pulse timing is left out (it is not part of a pinout, and values differ per maker).
- Kind is "cross-checked reproductions" because no standard exists at all: this is a de facto layout confirmed by makers' documents.
`````

`documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/debug/obd2.md`:

`````markdown
# obd2 — OBD-II (SAE J1962) / OBD-II (SAE J1962)

Kind: cross-checked reproductions
Pins: 16; types: power 1, ground 2, data 6, nc 7

## View
Written for the vehicle's socket, looking into it, wide side up: `drawn: socket`, top row 1 to 8 from left to right, bottom row 9 to 16 from left to right. The other view (mirror) is the tester's plug: 8 to 1 on top.

How I know, from two independent drawings:
- ELM327 datasheet, page 79, "Figure 8. The J1962 Vehicle Connector" (rendered and looked at): trapezoid with the wide side on top, mounting lugs, "1" top left, "8" top right, "9" bottom left, "16" bottom right. The next paragraph says that your circuit must connect "by way of a matching male J1962 connector", so the drawn part is the vehicle's female one.
- AESTECHNO's figure j1962.svg (labels read from the SVG): numbers 1 to 8 at rising x on the upper row and 9 to 16 at rising x on the lower row, shell path wider at the top. Its caption describes the vehicle connector with female contacts, "seen from the mating side, facing the connector", and refers to SAE J1962 figure 3.
- Wikipedia's caption agrees on the view: "Female OBD-II type A connector pinout – front view".

For the outline: the JS drawing of `obd2` must put the wide side at the top with this row order.

## Sources
1. Elm Electronics, ELM327 datasheet, ELM327DSK, https://www.elmelectronics.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/ELM327DS.pdf — page 79 (figure 8 and the pin 5 remark), page 81 (figure 9: pins 2, 5, 6, 7, 10, 14, 15, 16). Accessed 2026-11-04.
2. AESTECHNO (electronic design house, France), OBD2 pinout (OBD-II port): J1962 16-pin, CAN, K-line, J1850, https://www.aestechno.com/en/resources/pinouts/obd2-obd-ii/ with figure j1962.svg — full table, states that the allocation comes from SAE J1962 table 1 and section 6.3. Accessed 2026-11-04.
3. Wikipedia, On-board diagnostics, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On-board_diagnostics — table of all 16 pins, type A and B. Accessed 2026-11-04.
4. CSS Electronics, OBD2 Explained, https://www.csselectronics.com/pages/obd2-explained-simple-intro — pin 16, pins 6 and 14, type A 12 V and type B 24 V. Accessed 2026-11-04.

Not read: SAE J1962 and ISO 15031-3 (paywalled). Also seen but not used: Gendan's page (https://m.gendan.co.uk/article_3.html, same pins, no view statement).

## Cross-check
Sources 1, 2 and 3 agree on every pin they name. ELM327 does not draw pin 4 or the manufacturer pins. Details:
- **Differs from the assignment:** the assignment says that all pins apart from 4, 5, 16, 6, 14, 7 and 15 are undefined. Sources 1, 2 and 3 all give pin 2 as J1850 Bus+ and pin 10 as J1850 Bus-. I followed the sources: pins 2 and 10 are `data`, and only 1, 3, 8, 9, 11, 12 and 13 are manufacturer pins (AESTECHNO: "The other seven are left to the manufacturer"; Wikipedia: manufacturer discretion).
- Pin 10: Gendan writes only "J1850 Bus". ELM327 and AESTECHNO write Bus-. Wikipedia and AESTECHNO agree that VPW uses pin 2 alone, so pin 10 is PWM only.
- Pin 15: optional per Wikipedia, and ELM327 says that many vehicles do not need it.
- Pin 16: AESTECHNO and Wikipedia give 12 V for type A and 24 V for type B, and CSS gives the same; AESTECHNO says that J1962 defines the pin as permanent, and CSS says "often" even with the ignition off. I wrote "stays live with the ignition off".
- Fuse advice: AESTECHNO says to fuse or current-limit the adapter itself.
- Pin 5 missing on some vehicles: ELM327 only, worded as "reported".

## Choices
- `type: nc` for the seven manufacturer pins, with the function saying that they are manufacturer-specific and can be live. They may carry signals, but none that the standard defines, and the catalog schema's `nc` includes "reserved". The dashed look must not be read as "free to use"; the function says so. This is a judgement call.
- All seven have the same name `OEM`. Manufacturer uses (Wikipedia lists some for GM, Ford, BMW and others) are left out, they vary too much for a pin table.
- Names follow AESTECHNO's table, except `OEM` (source: "Discretionary").
- `contact: blade`: the drawing style for the flat contacts of this connector, shown as rectangles in the ELM327 figure. No source calls them blades, so the plug caption "blades" is my word for the male contacts.
- Type B has the same pin positions; the item shows type A only, with the voltage difference in the notes.
- Item names stay in Latin script in all locales: only proper names, no generic word.
`````

# Integrated circuits and small packages. The sources behind every item are in documentation/ecalc-sources/pinouts/; a changed pin updates

- id: ne555
  kind: pinout
  category: pinouts
  group: ics
  name: {cs: "NE555 (DIP-8)", da: "NE555 (DIP-8)", de: "NE555 (DIP-8)", el: "NE555 (DIP-8)", en: "NE555 (DIP-8)", es: "NE555 (DIP-8)", fr: "NE555 (DIP-8)", hi: "NE555 (DIP-8)", it: "NE555 (DIP-8)", ja: "NE555 (DIP-8)", nl: "NE555 (DIP-8)", no: "NE555 (DIP-8)", pl: "NE555 (DIP-8)", pt: "NE555 (DIP-8)", sv: "NE555 (DIP-8)", zh: "NE555 (DIP-8)"}
  doc: {en: "Bipolar timer for monostable and astable circuits, drawn as the 8-pin PDIP from above.", de: "Bipolarer Timer für monostabile und astabile Schaltungen, gezeichnet als 8-poliges PDIP von oben."}
  notes: {en: "The SOIC (D), SO (PS) and TSSOP (PW) versions of the NE555 have the same pin numbers as the PDIP (P).", de: "Die Versionen SOIC (D), SO (PS) und TSSOP (PW) des NE555 haben dieselben Pin-Nummern wie das PDIP (P)."}
  tags: ["ne555", "555", "timer", "zeitgeber", "monostable", "monostabil", "astable", "astabil", "oscillator", "oszillator", "dip8", "dip-8", "trig", "thres", "disch"]
  source: "Texas Instruments NA555, NE555, SA555, SE555 datasheet SLFS022K (March 2026), section 4, pin figure and Table 4-1"
  shape:
    type: dip
    pins: 8
  pins:
    - {number: "1", name: "GND", function: {en: "Ground", de: "Masse"}, type: ground}
    - {number: "2", name: "TRIG", function: {en: "Trigger input: starts the timing when it falls below half of CONT", de: "Triggereingang: startet die Zeit, wenn er unter die Hälfte von CONT fällt"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "3", name: "OUT", function: {en: "Timer output, can carry a high current", de: "Timerausgang, hoch belastbar"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "4", name: "RESET", function: {en: "Reset, active low: forces OUT and DISCH low", de: "Reset, aktiv low: zieht OUT und DISCH auf low"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "5", name: "CONT", function: {en: "Control voltage: sets the comparator thresholds, 2/3 of VCC if not driven; place for a bypass capacitor", de: "Steuerspannung: legt die Komparatorschwellen fest, 2/3 von VCC ohne Ansteuerung; Platz für einen Abblockkondensator"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "6", name: "THRES", function: {en: "Threshold input: ends the timing when it rises above CONT", de: "Schwellwerteingang: beendet die Zeit, wenn er über CONT steigt"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "7", name: "DISCH", function: {en: "Open-collector output that discharges the timing capacitor", de: "Open-Collector-Ausgang, der den Zeitkondensator entlädt"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "8", name: "VCC", function: {en: "Supply, 4.5 V to 16 V", de: "Versorgung, 4,5 V bis 16 V"}, type: power}

  kind: pinout

  group: ics

  notes: {en: "The metal tab is connected to pin 2 (OUTPUT), so a heat sink on the tab carries the output voltage: insulate it from metal at any other potential.", de: "Die Metallfahne ist mit Pin 2 (OUTPUT) verbunden; ein Kühlkörper an der Fahne führt also die Ausgangsspannung. Gegen Metall mit anderem Potenzial isolieren."}
  tags: ["lm317", "regulator", "spannungsregler", "regler", "adjustable", "einstellbar", "adj", "adjust", "vin", "vout", "to220", "to-220"]

  notes: {en: "The metal tab of the TO-220 is at ground: ST marks it GND in the pin figure. The TO-220FP has the same lead order.", de: "Die Metallfahne des TO-220 liegt auf Masse: ST bezeichnet sie in der Pin-Abbildung mit GND.   doc: {en: "8-bit shift register with serial input, a storage register and 3-state parallel outputs, drawn as the 16-pin PDIP from above.", de: "8-Bit-Schieberegister mit seriellem Eingang, Speicherregister und parallelen Tri-State-Ausgängen, gezeichnet als 16-poliges PDIP von oben."}
  notes: {en: "QA is alone on pin 15, on the other side from QB to QH. SRCLK shifts SER in; RCLK copies the shift register to the outputs. To chain chips, feed QH' into SER of the next one.", de: "QA liegt allein auf Pin 15, auf der anderen Seite als QB bis QH. SRCLK schiebt SER ein; RCLK übernimmt das Schieberegister an die Ausgänge. Zum Kaskadieren QH' an SER des nächsten Bausteins legen."}

- id: uln2003
  kind: pinout
  category: pinouts
  group: ics
  name: {cs: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)", da: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)", de: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)", el: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)", en: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)", es: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)", fr: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)", hi: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)", it: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)", ja: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)", nl: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)", no: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)", pl: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)", pt: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)", sv: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)", zh: "ULN2003A (DIP-16)"}
  doc: {en: "Seven Darlington sink drivers with common-cathode clamp diodes, drawn as the 16-pin PDIP from above.", de: "Sieben Darlington-Lowside-Treiber mit Freilaufdioden an gemeinsamer Kathode, gezeichnet als 16-poliges PDIP von oben."}
  notes: {en: "Each input nB drives the output nC opposite it, and the outputs only sink current towards E. Pin 9 (COM) joins the cathodes of all seven clamp diodes: for inductive loads such as relay or motor coils, tie it to the coil supply so that the diodes catch the kickback; with resistive loads it may stay open.", de: "Jeder Eingang nB steuert den Ausgang nC gegenüber, und die Ausgänge ziehen den Strom nur nach E. Pin 9 (COM) verbindet die Kathoden aller sieben Freilaufdioden: Bei induktiven Lasten wie Relais- oder Motorspulen gehört er an die Spulenversorgung, damit die Dioden die Abschaltspannung abfangen; bei ohmschen Lasten darf er offen bleiben."}
  tags: ["uln2003", "uln2003a", "darlington", "driver", "treiber", "relay", "relais", "stepper", "schrittmotor", "clamp diode", "flyback", "freilaufdiode", "com", "dip16", "dip-16"]
  source: "Texas Instruments ULN200x, ULQ200x datasheet SLRS027T (March 2025), section 4, Figure 4-1 and Table 4-1; sections 7.4 and 8.4 for COM"
  shape:
    type: dip
    pins: 16
  pins:
    - {number: "1", name: "1B", function: {en: "Input of channel 1 (Darlington base)", de: "Eingang von Kanal 1 (Darlington-Basis)"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "2", name: "2B", function: {en: "Input of channel 2 (Darlington base)", de: "Eingang von Kanal 2 (Darlington-Basis)"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "3", name: "3B", function: {en: "Input of channel 3 (Darlington base)", de: "Eingang von Kanal 3 (Darlington-Basis)"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "4", name: "4B", function: {en: "Input of channel 4 (Darlington base)", de: "Eingang von Kanal 4 (Darlington-Basis)"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "5", name: "5B", function: {en: "Input of channel 5 (Darlington base)", de: "Eingang von Kanal 5 (Darlington-Basis)"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "6", name: "6B", function: {en: "Input of channel 6 (Darlington base)", de: "Eingang von Kanal 6 (Darlington-Basis)"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "7", name: "7B", function: {en: "Input of channel 7 (Darlington base)", de: "Eingang von Kanal 7 (Darlington-Basis)"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "8", name: "E", function: {en: "Common emitter of all channels, normally ground", de: "Gemeinsamer Emitter aller Kanäle, normalerweise Masse"}, type: ground}
    - {number: "9", name: "COM", function: {en: "Common cathode of the clamp diodes", de: "Gemeinsame Kathode der Freilaufdioden"}, type: power, notes: {en: "Tie to the coil supply for inductive loads. The outputs must not rise far above COM, or the diodes conduct heavily.", de: "Bei induktiven Lasten an die Spulenversorgung legen. Die Ausgänge dürfen nicht deutlich über COM steigen, sonst leiten die Dioden stark."}}
    - {number: "10", name: "7C", function: {en: "Output of channel 7 (Darlington collector)", de: "Ausgang von Kanal 7 (Darlington-Kollektor)"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "11", name: "6C", function: {en: "Output of channel 6 (Darlington collector)", de: "Ausgang von Kanal 6 (Darlington-Kollektor)"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "12", name: "5C", function: {en: "Output of channel 5 (Darlington collector)", de: "Ausgang von Kanal 5 (Darlington-Kollektor)"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "13", name: "4C", function: {en: "Output of channel 4 (Darlington collector)", de: "Ausgang von Kanal 4 (Darlington-Kollektor)"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "14", name: "3C", function: {en: "Output of channel 3 (Darlington collector)", de: "Ausgang von Kanal 3 (Darlington-Kollektor)"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "15", name: "2C", function: {en: "Output of channel 2 (Darlington collector)", de: "Ausgang von Kanal 2 (Darlington-Kollektor)"}, type: signal}
    - {number: "16", name: "1C", function: {en: "Output of channel 1 (Darlington collector)", de: "Ausgang von Kanal 1 (Darlington-Kollektor)"}, type: signal}

  doc: {en: "8-bit AVR microcontroller in the 28-pin SPDIP, seen from above. The name is the port bit; the function lists what else the pin can do.", de: "8-Bit-AVR-Mikrocontroller im 28-poligen SPDIP, von oben gesehen. Der Name ist das Port-Bit; die Funktion nennt, was der Pin außerdem kann."}
  notes: {en: "Connect AVCC to VCC even when the ADC is unused, and through a low-pass filter when it is used. PB6 and PB7 are taken when the fuses select a crystal. ADC6 and ADC7 exist only in the TQFP and VQFN packages, not in this one. The ATmega48A/PA, 88A/PA, 168A/PA and 328 of the same datasheet share this drawing.", de: "AVCC auch ohne ADC-Nutzung mit VCC verbinden, bei genutztem ADC über einen Tiefpass. PB6 und PB7 sind belegt, wenn die Fuses einen Quarz wählen. ADC6 und ADC7 gibt es nur in den TQFP- und VQFN-Gehäusen, nicht in diesem. Die ATmega48A/PA, 88A/PA, 168A/PA und 328 desselben Datenblatts teilen diese Zeichnung."}
